items.text: Efes sesli rehberine hoş geldiniz. Burası İzmir ilinde bir antik kent. Dönemi: MÖ 10. yüzyıl. Antik dünyanın en iyi korunmuş Roma kentlerinden biri; Celsus Kütüphanesi ile ünlü.

items.text: İyonların kurduğu kent, Artemis Tapınağı sayesinde Ege'nin dinî merkezi oldu. Roma döneminde Asia eyaletinin başkenti olarak 200 binden fazla nüfusa ulaştı; limanın alüvyonla dolmasıyla önemini yitirdi.

items.text: Celsus Kütüphanesi. Efes'in mermer cephesi bir kütüphanenin değil, bir mezar anıtının önyüzüdür: Celsus'un lahdi hâlâ apsisin altındaki odada duruyor. Model, 1970-78'de yeniden dikilen cepheyi tam yüksekliğiyle, arkasındaki salonu ise duvarların ayakta kaldığı yüksekliğe kadar gösterir.

items.text: Büyük Tiyatro. Antik dünyanın en büyük tiyatrolarından biri: Panayır Dağı'nın yamacına oyulmuş üç katlı cavea, liman caddesinin ucundan Roma sahne binasına bakar. Elçilerin İşleri'ndeki gümüşçüler ayaklanması bu tiyatroda geçer.

items.text: Yamaç Evler. Kuretler Caddesi'nin karşısındaki yamaca kurulmuş altı lüks konut: yerler mozaik, duvarlar fresko. Tabandan ısıtma, kapalı kanalizasyon ve cam pencerelerle, MS 1. yüzyılda bir Roma zenginin evinin nasıl bir yer olduğunu gösteren tek yerdir. Model, peristilli avlusuyla bir konut biriminin içini gösterir.

items.text: Artemis Tapınağı. Dünyanın Yedi Harikası'ndan biri ve bugün ayakta tek bir sütunu bile kalmayan tek yapı: bataklık bir arazide, 137 metre uzunluğunda bir mermer orman. Plinius'a göre 36 sütunun kaidesi kabartmalıydı. Model, MÖ 4. yüzyılda yeniden inşa edilen üçüncü tapınağı gösterir.

items.text: Biliyor muydunuz? Artemis Tapınağı Dünyanın Yedi Harikası'ndan biriydi; bugün ayakta sadece tek bir sütun var. Büyük Tiyatro 24.000 kişilikti. Elçilerin İşleri'ne göre Aziz Pavlus'a karşı iki saat süren 'Efeslilerin Artemis'i uludur!' gösterisi burada yapıldı. Yamaç Evler'de tabandan ve duvardan ısıtma, kapalı kanalizasyon ve cam pencereler vardı — MS 1. yüzyılda. Efes bir liman kentiydi. Küçük Menderes'in alüvyonu limanı doldurdu ve bugün deniz kalıntılardan 5 km uzakta.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Ephesus, an ancient city in İzmir province. Its period: 10th century BC. One of the best-preserved Roman cities of antiquity, famed for the Library of Celsus.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Ephesus, an ancient city in İzmir province. Its period: 10th century BC. One of the best-preserved Roman cities of antiquity, famed for the Library of Celsus.

items.text: Founded by Ionian settlers, the city grew around the Temple of Artemis. Under Rome it became capital of the province of Asia with over 200,000 people, then declined as its harbour silted up.
items.speech: Founded by Ionian settlers, the city grew around the Temple of Artemis. Under Rome it became capital of the province of Asia with over 200,000 people, then declined as its harbour silted up.

items.text: Library of Celsus. The marble front at Ephesus is not the face of a library but of a tomb: Celsus' sarcophagus still lies in the chamber beneath the apse. The model shows the façade re-erected in 1970-78 at its full height, and the hall behind it only as high as its walls survive.
items.speech: Library of Celsus. The marble front at Ephesus is not the face of a library but of a tomb: Celsus' sarcophagus still lies in the chamber beneath the apse. items.text: Great Theatre. One of the largest theatres of antiquity: a three-tiered cavea cut into the slope of Mount Pion, looking down the Harbour Street at a Roman stage building. The riot of the silversmiths in the Acts of the Apostles takes place here.
items.speech: Great Theatre. One of the largest theatres of antiquity: a three-tiered cavea cut into the slope of Mount Pion, looking down the Harbour Street at a Roman stage building. The riot of the silversmiths in the Acts of the Apostles takes place here.

items.text: Terrace Houses. Six luxury residences on the slope opposite Curetes Street, their floors in mosaic and their walls in fresco. With underfloor heating, enclosed drains and glazed windows, they are the one place that shows what a rich Roman's house was actually like in the first century AD. The model shows the inside of one unit, around its colonnaded court.

items.text: Temple of Artemis. One of the Seven Wonders, and the only one with not a single column left standing: a marble forest 137 metres long, raised on marshy ground. Pliny says 36 of the columns were carved in relief at the base. The model shows the third temple, rebuilt in the 4th century BC.

items.text: Curetes Street. The main colonnaded street connecting the Library of Celsus to the theatre, lined with monuments and statues.
items.speech: Curetes Street. The main colonnaded street connecting the Library of Celsus to the theatre, lined with monuments and statues.

items.text: Did you know? The Temple of Artemis was one of the Seven Wonders; a single re-erected column remains today. The Great Theatre seated 24,000. According to Acts, the two-hour chant of 'Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!' against Saint Paul filled this bowl. The Terrace Houses had underfloor and wall heating, enclosed drains and glazed windows — in the first century AD. Ephesus was a port. Silt from the Küçük Menderes filled the harbour, and the sea now lies 5 km from the ruins.

items.text: Willkommen beim Audioguide für Ephesos in der Provinz İzmir. Epoche: 10. Jahrhundert v. Chr. Eine der am besten erhaltenen römischen Städte der Antike, berühmt für die Celsus-Bibliothek.
items.speech: Willkommen beim Audioguide für Ephesos in der Provinz İzmir. Epoche: 10. Jahrhundert vor Christus Eine der am besten erhaltenen römischen Städte der Antike, berühmt für die Celsus-Bibliothek.

items.text: Von ionischen Siedlern gegründet, wuchs die Stadt rund um den Tempel der Artemis. Unter Rom wurde sie mit über 200.000 Einwohnern Hauptstadt der Provinz Asia und verlor dann an Bedeutung, als ihr Hafen verlandete.
items.speech: Von ionischen Siedlern gegründet, wuchs die Stadt rund um den Tempel der Artemis. Unter Rom wurde sie mit über 200.000 Einwohnern Hauptstadt der Provinz Asia und verlor dann an Bedeutung, als ihr Hafen verlandete.

items.text: Celsus-Bibliothek. Die Marmorfront in Ephesos ist nicht die Fassade einer Bibliothek, sondern die eines Grabmals: Der Sarkophag des Celsus liegt noch immer in der Kammer unter der Apsis. Das Modell zeigt die 1970–78 wieder aufgerichtete Fassade in voller Höhe und die Halle dahinter nur so hoch, wie ihre Mauern erhalten sind.

items.text: Großes Theater. Eines der größten Theater der Antike: eine dreirangige Cavea, in den Hang des Berges Pion gehauen, die die Hafenstraße hinab auf ein römisches Bühnengebäude blickt. Hier spielt der Aufstand der Silberschmiede aus der Apostelgeschichte.

items.text: Hanghäuser. Sechs Luxuswohnhäuser am Hang gegenüber der Kuretenstraße, ihre Böden mit Mosaiken, ihre Wände mit Fresken. Mit Fußbodenheizung, geschlossenen Abwasserkanälen und verglasten Fenstern sind sie der einzige Ort, der zeigt, wie das Haus eines reichen Römers im ersten Jahrhundert n. Chr. tatsächlich aussah. Das Modell zeigt das Innere einer Wohneinheit rund um ihren Säulenhof.

items.text: Tempel der Artemis. Eines der Sieben Weltwunder und das einzige, von dem keine einzige Säule mehr steht: ein 137 Meter langer Wald aus Marmor, errichtet auf sumpfigem Boden. Laut Plinius waren 36 der Säulen am Fuß mit Reliefs verziert. Das Modell zeigt den dritten Tempel, der im 4. Jahrhundert v. Chr. neu errichtet wurde.

items.text: Kuretenstraße. Die von Säulen gesäumte Hauptstraße, die die Celsus-Bibliothek mit dem Theater verbindet, gesäumt von Monumenten und Statuen.
items.speech: Kuretenstraße. Die von Säulen gesäumte Hauptstraße, die die Celsus-Bibliothek mit dem Theater verbindet, gesäumt von Monumenten und Statuen.

items.text: Wussten Sie schon? Der Tempel der Artemis war eines der Sieben Weltwunder; heute steht von ihm nur noch eine einzige, wieder aufgerichtete Säule. Das Große Theater bot 24.000 Menschen Platz. Laut der Apostelgeschichte erfüllte der zweistündige Ruf „Groß ist die Artemis der Epheser!“ gegen den Apostel Paulus dieses Rund. Die Hanghäuser hatten Fußboden- und Wandheizung, geschlossene Abwasserkanäle und verglaste Fenster – im ersten Jahrhundert n. Chr. Ephesos war eine Hafenstadt. Schlamm des Küçük Menderes füllte den Hafen, und heute liegt das Meer 5 km von den Ruinen entfernt.

items.text: Добро пожаловать в аудиогид: Эфес, провинция Измир. Период: X век до н. э. Один из наиболее сохранившихся римских городов античности, знаменитый библиотекой Цельса.
items.speech: Добро пожаловать в аудиогид: Эфес, провинция Измир. Период: X век до нашей эры Один из наиболее сохранившихся римских городов античности, знаменитый библиотекой Цельса.

items.text: Основанный ионийскими переселенцами, город вырос вокруг храма Артемиды. При римлянах он стал столицей провинции Азия с населением более 200 000 человек, а затем пришёл в упадок, когда его гавань занесло илом.
items.speech: Основанный ионийскими переселенцами, город вырос вокруг храма Артемиды. При римлянах он стал столицей провинции Азия с населением более 200 000 человек, а затем пришёл в упадок, когда его гавань занесло илом.

items.text: Библиотека Цельса. Мраморный фасад в Эфесе — это лицо не библиотеки, а гробницы: саркофаг Цельса до сих пор покоится в камере под апсидой. Модель показывает фасад, заново возведённый в 1970–78 годах, во всю высоту, а зал за ним — лишь на ту высоту, на которую сохранились его стены.
items.speech: Библиотека Цельса. Мраморный фасад в Эфесе, это лицо не библиотеки, а гробницы: саркофаг Цельса до сих пор покоится в камере под апсидой. Модель показывает фасад, заново возведённый в 1970-1978 годах, во всю высоту, а зал за ним, лишь на ту высоту, на которую сохранились его стены.

items.text: Большой театр. Один из крупнейших театров античности: трёхъярусная кавея, высеченная в склоне горы Пион, обращена вдоль Портовой улицы к римскому сценическому зданию. Именно здесь происходит бунт серебряных дел мастеров, описанный в Деяниях апостолов.

items.text: Террасные дома. Шесть роскошных жилищ на склоне напротив улицы Куретов, с мозаичными полами и расписанными фресками стенами. С подпольным отоплением, закрытой канализацией и застеклёнными окнами они — единственное место, которое показывает, каким на самом деле был дом богатого римлянина в I веке н. э. Модель показывает интерьер одного из домов вокруг его двора с колоннадой.

items.text: Храм Артемиды. Одно из семи чудес света и единственное, от которого не осталось ни одной стоящей колонны: мраморный лес длиной 137 метров, возведённый на болотистой почве. По словам Плиния, 36 колонн были украшены рельефами у основания. Модель показывает третий храм, отстроенный заново в IV веке до н. э.

items.text: Улица Куретов. Главная улица с колоннадой, соединяющая библиотеку Цельса с театром, вдоль которой стоят памятники и статуи.
items.speech: Улица Куретов. Главная улица с колоннадой, соединяющая библиотеку Цельса с театром, вдоль которой стоят памятники и статуи.

items.text: А вы знали? Храм Артемиды был одним из семи чудес света; сегодня от него осталась лишь одна заново установленная колонна. Большой театр вмещал 24 000 зрителей. Согласно Деяниям апостолов, двухчасовой крик «Велика Артемида Ефесская!», направленный против святого Павла, наполнял эту чашу. В террасных домах были подпольное и настенное отопление, закрытая канализация и застеклённые окна — в I веке н. э. Эфес был портом. Наносы реки Кючюк-Мендерес заполнили гавань, и теперь море находится в 5 км от руин.

items.text: Biliyor muydunuz? Kentin adı 'parşömen' kelimesinin kökenidir: Mısır papirüs ihracatını kesince burada deri işlenmeye başlandı. Akropoldeki tiyatro antik dünyanın en dik tiyatrosudur: 80 sıra, neredeyse uçurum eğiminde, 10.000 kişilik. Asklepion'da tedavi rüya yorumu, su kürleri ve tiyatroyla yapılırdı. items.text: Capital of the Attalid dynasty, its 200,000-scroll library gave parchment its name. Bequeathed to Rome in 133 BC, it became famous for the Asklepion healing centre.

items.text: Great Altar terrace. Less an altar than a stage: the 113-metre Gigantomachy frieze wraps the building in a battle told in stone. It was dismantled and shipped to Berlin between 1878 and 1886; what stands at Pergamon now is the terrace and the footings.

items.text: Did you know? The word 'parchment' comes from Pergamon: when Egypt cut off papyrus, the city perfected treated skins. The acropolis theatre is the steepest of the ancient world: 80 rows pitched almost like a cliff, seating 10,000. At the Asklepion, treatment meant dream interpretation, water cures and theatre. Galen, the physician, trained here. The Great Altar was dismantled and shipped to Berlin between 1878 and 1886; it is the building the Pergamon Museum is named after.

items.text: Wussten Sie schon? Das Wort „Pergament“ stammt von Pergamon: Als Ägypten die Papyruslieferungen einstellte, perfektionierte die Stadt die Verarbeitung von Tierhäuten. Das Theater der Akropolis ist das steilste der antiken Welt: 80 Reihen, fast wie eine Klippe geneigt, mit Platz für 10.000 Menschen. Im Asklepieion bestand die Behandlung aus Traumdeutung, Wasserkuren und Theater. Der Arzt Galen wurde hier ausgebildet. Der Große Altar wurde zwischen 1878 und 1886 abgebaut und nach Berlin verschifft; nach ihm ist das Pergamonmuseum benannt.

items.text: Столица династии Атталидов, чья библиотека в 200 000 свитков дала название пергаменту. Завещанный Риму в 133 году до н. э., город прославился лечебным центром Асклепион.

items.text: Терраса Большого алтаря. Не столько алтарь, сколько сцена: 113-метровый фриз Гигантомахии опоясывает здание битвой, рассказанной в камне. Его разобрали и вывезли в Берлин между 1878 и 1886 годами; в Пергаме сегодня остались лишь терраса и фундамент.

items.text: А вы знали? Слово «пергамент» происходит от Пергама: когда Египет прекратил поставки папируса, город довёл до совершенства выделку кож. Театр акрополя — самый крутой в античном мире: 80 рядов с наклоном почти как у утёса, на 10 000 зрителей. В Асклепионе лечение состояло из толкования снов, водолечения и театра. Здесь учился врач Гален. Большой алтарь был разобран и вывезен в Берлин между 1878 и 1886 годами; именно в его честь назван Пергамский музей.

items.text: Did you know? Its 30,000-seat stadium is the best-preserved stadium surviving from antiquity. The stadium seated 30,000 and is the best-preserved in the ancient world, with both ends still standing. The Sebasteion reliefs show Roman emperors beside gods — the fullest surviving programme of imperial propaganda carved in stone. The marble quarry was two kilometres away. Signatures of Aphrodisian sculptors turn up from Rome to North Africa.

items.text: А вы знали? Его стадион на 30 000 мест — наиболее сохранившийся из дошедших до нас стадионов античности. Стадион вмещал 30 000 зрителей и является наиболее сохранившимся в античном мире; оба его торца всё ещё стоят. Рельефы Себастейона изображают римских императоров рядом с богами — это наиболее полная из сохранившихся программ императорской пропаганды, высеченная в камне. Мраморная каменоломня находилась в двух километрах. Подписи скульпторов из Афродисиаса встречаются от Рима до Северной Африки.

Kurban hayvanları ölürken rahiplerin sağ kalması mucize sayılırdı; gaz yerde birikir, ayakta duran insanın başı bulutun üstünde kalır. Nekropolü 1200'den fazla mezarıyla Anadolu'nun en büyüğüdür. items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Hierapolis, an ancient city in Denizli province. Its period: 2nd century BC. A spa and necropolis city built above the travertines of Pamukkale.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Hierapolis, an ancient city in Denizli province. Its period: 2nd century BC. A spa and necropolis city built above the travertines of Pamukkale.

items.text: Founded by the kings of Pergamon, its hot springs made it a healing centre. Destroyed by earthquakes, it was rebuilt in grand Roman style.
items.speech: Founded by the kings of Pergamon, its hot springs made it a healing centre. Destroyed by earthquakes, it was rebuilt in grand Roman style.

items.text: Theatre. A theatre for 15,000 cut into the slope above the travertines of Pamukkale. Its stage front, three ranks of columns deep, survives in large part and was re-erected between 2004 and 2014.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the Antique Pool, the Necropolis, the Frontinus Street and the Temple of Apollo.
items.speech: As you walk round, don't miss the Antique Pool, the Necropolis, the Frontinus Street and the Temple of Apollo.

items.text: Did you know? The columns lying in the Antique Pool fell there during a 7th-century earthquake. The Plutonion, the 'Gate to Hell', leaks carbon dioxide from below. Sacrificial animals died while the priests survived: the gas pools at ground level, leaving a standing man's head above the cloud. Its necropolis, with more than 1,200 tombs, is the largest in Anatolia. Many who came to the hot springs for a cure never left.

items.text: Von den Königen von Pergamon gegründet, machten ihre heißen Quellen sie zu einem Heilzentrum. Nach der Zerstörung durch Erdbeben wurde sie im prachtvollen römischen Stil wieder aufgebaut.

items.text: Verpassen Sie beim Rundgang nicht: Antikes Becken, Nekropole, Frontinusstraße und Apollontempel.
items.speech: Verpassen Sie beim Rundgang nicht: Antikes Becken, Nekropole, Frontinusstraße und Apollontempel.

items.text: Wussten Sie schon? Die Säulen, die im Antiken Becken liegen, stürzten bei einem Erdbeben im 7. Jahrhundert hinein. Aus dem Plutonion, dem „Tor zur Hölle“, entweicht Kohlendioxid aus der Tiefe. Die Opfertiere starben, während die Priester überlebten: Das Gas sammelt sich am Boden, sodass der Kopf eines stehenden Menschen über der Wolke bleibt. Ihre Nekropole mit mehr als 1.200 Gräbern ist die größte Anatoliens. Viele, die zur Heilung an die heißen Quellen kamen, kehrten nie zurück.

items.text: А вы знали? Колонны, лежащие в Античном бассейне, упали туда во время землетрясения VII века. Из Плутониона, «Врат ада», из-под земли просачивается углекислый газ. Жертвенные животные погибали, а жрецы оставались в живых: газ скапливается у самой земли, и голова стоящего человека остаётся над облаком. Его некрополь, насчитывающий более 1200 гробниц, — крупнейший в Анатолии. Многие из тех, кто приезжал лечиться на горячие источники, так и не уехали.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Miletus, an ancient city in Aydın province. Its period: 15th century BC. The harbour city where grid-plan urbanism was born and philosophy took its first steps.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Miletus, an ancient city in Aydın province. Its period: 15th century BC. The harbour city where grid-plan urbanism was born and philosophy took its first steps.

items.text: With four harbours it dominated Mediterranean trade and founded over 90 colonies. After Persian destruction it was rebuilt on Hippodamus' grid plan.
items.speech: With four harbours it dominated Mediterranean trade and founded over 90 colonies. After Persian destruction it was rebuilt on Hippodamus' grid plan.

items.text: Great Theatre. One of the largest theatres in Anatolia: its cavea, nearly 140 m across, opens like a stadium set against the hillside. Built by Greek architects in 250-225 BC, it was rebuilt under Rome in AD 68-96 with a three-storey stone stage building — a front that survives, with the workshops behind it, among the most complete anywhere.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the Baths of Faustina, the Bouleuterion and the İlyas Bey Mosque.

items.text: Did you know? The city now lies 8 km inland — the Meander river filled in all four harbours. The theatre held 15,000 and is among the largest in the Aegean; the sockets for the emperor's box are still visible in the front row. Thales, Anaximander and Anaximenes all came from here. The first three names in Western philosophy shared one harbour. The monumental Market Gate was shipped piece by piece to Berlin in 1907-08 and re-erected there.

items.text: Linked to Miletus by a sacred way, it was a major oracle. Work on the colossal temple began after Alexander's visit but was never finished.

items.text: Temple of Apollo. One of the largest temples ever attempted: some 500 years in the building, and never finished. It never had a roof — behind the forest of columns lay an open court holding the oracle spring and the laurel tree.

items.text: Did you know? Construction drawings used by ancient architects are still visible on the temple walls. The Temple of Apollo was designed with 122 columns, built over some 500 years, and never finished. Its columns stand 19.7 metres tall, making it one of the largest temples in the Greek world. It was an oracle, linked to Miletus by a 17-kilometre Sacred Way that pilgrims walked.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Priene, an ancient city in Aydın province. Its period: 4th century BC. A compact Ionian city on Mount Mycale whose grid plan survives intact.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Priene, an ancient city in Aydın province. Its period: 4th century BC. A compact Ionian city on Mount Mycale whose grid plan survives intact.

items.text: Refounded in the Hellenistic period, it escaped major Roman rebuilding and is the purest surviving example of classical town planning.
items.speech: Refounded in the Hellenistic period, it escaped major Roman rebuilding and is the purest surviving example of classical town planning.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the Temple of Athena, the Bouleuterion, the Theatre and the Ekklesiasterion.
items.speech: As you walk round, don't miss the Temple of Athena, the Bouleuterion, the Theatre and the Ekklesiasterion.

items.text: Did you know? The marble armchairs in the theatre's front row were reserved for city dignitaries. It is the best-preserved grid-plan city of antiquity, laid out in squares on a steep slope as if the ground were flat. Pytheos, architect of the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus, built the Temple of Athena. Alexander the Great paid for it; the dedication inscription is now in the British Museum. The council house seated 640 — very nearly the city's entire adult male citizenry at once.

items.text: Founded by the Seleucid king Antiochus II for his wife Laodice, it grew rich on textiles and banking and hosted one of the Seven Churches.

items.text: Did you know? After an earthquake the city refused Roman aid and rebuilt itself with its own money. One of the seven churches of Revelation. Its rebuke — 'neither cold nor hot' — is thought to play on the water that arrived lukewarm through kilometres of aqueduct. After the earthquake of AD 60 the city refused imperial aid and rebuilt at its own expense — a detail Tacitus thought worth recording. It had two theatres, a stadium, and one of the largest ancient water-distribution terminals in Anatolia.

items.text: Set where the Aegean meets the Mediterranean, it was an obligatory stop for ships. Praxiteles' Aphrodite drew visitors from across the ancient world.
items.speech: Set where the Aegean meets the Mediterranean, it was an obligatory stop for ships. Praxiteles' Aphrodite drew visitors from across the ancient world.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the Round Temple of Aphrodite, the Theatre, the Sundial terrace and the Twin harbours.

items.text: Did you know? The astronomer Eudoxus built an observatory here and measured the year with striking accuracy. Praxiteles' Aphrodite of Knidos was the first monumental female nude in Greek art. People sailed here simply to see it. The city had two harbours, one naval. Built on the cape where two seas meet, it was where ships waited out the wind. The astronomer Eudoxus came from Knidos; the structure thought to be its observatory carries his name.

items.text: Did you know? Smyrna was one of the Seven Churches of Revelation that has survived to the present day. One of seven cities claiming Homer's birth — and the one with the strongest claim. The agora's three-storey basilica was rebuilt after the earthquake of AD 178 with a donation from the empress Faustina. In the fourth century BC the city moved, on Alexander's orders, to the slopes of today's Kadifekale — and İzmir still sits on that plan.

items.text: The city developed within the Carian world from the 6th century BC and passed through Persian and Roman rule. The Temple of Zeus Lepsinos is one of the best-preserved colonnaded temples in Anatolia.
items.speech: The city developed within the Carian world from the 6th century BC and passed through Persian and Roman rule. The Temple of Zeus Lepsinos is one of the best-preserved colonnaded temples in Anatolia.

items.text: Temple of Zeus Lepsinos. The temple of Zeus at Euromos, with 16 columns still standing.
items.speech: Temple of Zeus Lepsinos. The temple of Zeus at Euromos, with 16 columns still standing.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the Stadium, the Theatre, the Bouleuterion and the City Walls.

items.text: Did you know? An inscription on the temple records that it was dedicated in the name of Emperor Hadrian. With sixteen columns still standing, the Temple of Zeus Lepsinos is among the best-preserved temples in Anatolia. Some columns were never fluted: the temple was left unfinished, and the fact is legible in the stone. Inscriptions on the columns record, by name, which citizen paid for each one.

items.text: Biliyor muydunuz? Nysa'daki kütüphane, Efes'teki Celsus Kütüphanesi'nin ardından Anadolu'nun en büyük ikinci antik kütüphanesidir. Kenti ikiye bölen derenin üzerindeki tonozlu tünel yaklaşık 100 metre uzunluğundadır — antik dünyanın en uzun köprü tonozlarından biri. Coğrafyacı Strabon gençliğinde burada okudu ve kenti kendi gözlemleriyle anlattı. Meclis binası (bouleuterion) mermer oturma sıralarıyla neredeyse eksiksiz ayaktadır.

items.text: Founded in the Hellenistic period, the city was a wealthy cultural centre of the Maeander valley. Its huge library and the tunnel-lined basilica street show the city's Roman-era splendour.

items.text: Did you know? The library at Nysa is the second-largest ancient library in Anatolia after the Library of Celsus at Ephesus. The vaulted tunnel carrying the city over its ravine runs about 100 metres — among the longest bridge vaults of antiquity. The geographer Strabo studied here as a young man and described the city from first-hand observation. The council house survives almost intact, marble seating and all.

items.text: Did you know? The city's name is linked to the region's famed dyeing industry, and its purple dye is celebrated in ancient sources. One of the seven churches of Revelation. The city was famous for dyeing. Lydia, the 'seller of purple' Paul met at Philippi in Acts, came from here. The ruins now sit on an island of ground in the middle of modern Akhisar, ringed by apartment blocks.

items.text: Biliyor muydunuz? Noel Baba olarak bilinen Aziz Nikolaos MS 270 civarında burada doğdu. Likya Birliği'nin meclis binası buradadır. Temsilcilerin kentlerinin büyüklüğüne göre oy kullandığı bu sistem, Montesquieu üzerinden ABD anayasa tartışmalarında federalizm örneği olarak anıldı. Aziz Nikolaos, yani Noel Baba, MS 3. yüzyılda bu kentte doğdu. Neron döneminde dikilen deniz feneri, dünyanın ayakta kalabilmiş en eski fenerlerinden biridir; parçaları bulunup yeniden birleştirildi.

items.text: Lycia's principal port and an oracle of Apollo, it became the Roman provincial capital and was preserved for centuries beneath sand dunes.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the Bouleuterion (Assembly), the Triumphal Arch, the Theatre, the Lighthouse and the Colonnaded Street.

items.text: Did you know? Saint Nicholas — Santa Claus — was born here around AD 270. The Lycian League met in the council house here. Its system — delegates voting in proportion to their city's size — reached the American constitutional debates as a model of federalism, by way of Montesquieu. Saint Nicholas — Father Christmas — was born in this city in the third century AD. Its lighthouse, raised under Nero, is among the oldest surviving anywhere; its blocks were found and reassembled.

items.text: Biliyor muydunuz? Nereidler Anıtı'nın özgün blokları bugün British Museum'da sergileniyor. Kent tarihinde iki kez, düşmana teslim olmaktansa kendini yaktı: önce Perslere, sonra Roma iç savaşında Brutus'a karşı. Herodotos ve Appianos ikisini de anlatır. Nereidler Anıtı ve Harpy Anıtı'nın kabartmaları 1842'de sökülüp British Museum'a götürüldü; bugün müzedeki kopyalarıyla yerinde duruyor. Likçe yazılı dikilitaş, bilinen en uzun Likçe metindir ve dilin çözülmesindeki anahtar belgelerdendir.

items.text: Twice in its history the city chose self-immolation over surrender. It yielded the richest collection of Lycian inscriptions known.
items.speech: Twice in its history the city chose self-immolation over surrender. It yielded the richest collection of Lycian inscriptions known.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the Harpy Monument, the Nereid Monument, the Lycian sarcophagi, the Theatre and the Letoon sanctuary.
items.speech: As you walk round, don't miss the Harpy Monument, the Nereid Monument, the Lycian sarcophagi, the Theatre and the Letoon sanctuary.

items.text: Did you know? The original blocks of the Nereid Monument are displayed in the British Museum today. Twice in its history the city burned itself rather than surrender — first to the Persians, then to Brutus in Rome's civil war. Herodotus and Appian each record one. The Nereid and Harpy Monument reliefs were removed to the British Museum in 1842; casts stand in their place. The inscribed pillar here carries the longest known text in Lycian, a key document in deciphering the language.

items.text: One of the six great cities of the Lycian League; in the 4th century the tomb of its bishop Nicholas turned it into a pilgrimage centre.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the Rock-cut tombs, the Roman theatre and the Andriake harbour.
items.speech: As you walk round, don't miss the Rock-cut tombs, the Roman theatre and the Andriake harbour.

items.text: Did you know? The rock tombs imitate wooden Lycian houses, with beams and doors carved into stone. The rock tombs are carved as the façades of wooden Lycian houses — a photograph, in stone, of an architecture that has otherwise vanished. Saint Nicholas served as bishop here; his church stands in modern Demre, and his tomb was in it. The theatre was rebuilt after an earthquake; blocks from the toppled stage building still lie where they fell.

items.text: Did you know? The flames of Chimaera have burned without pause for at least 2,500 years. In the first century BC the pirate chief Zeniketes made the city his base, and Rome had to clear him out. The ruins are swallowed by laurel and oleander, with a stream running through the middle of the city to the sea.

items.text: Did you know? The ancient main street still connects two harbours — and you can walk it. It had three harbours within walking distance of each other, so that whichever way the wind blew, one was sheltered. Alexander the Great wintered here in 333 BC, and the city greeted him with a golden crown. It grew rich on rose oil and timber; the colonnaded street between its harbours can still be walked.

items.text: Said to be founded by migrants after the Trojan War, it was monumentalised in Roman times by the benefactor Plancia Magna.
items.speech: Said to be founded by migrants after the Trojan War, it was monumentalised in Roman times by the benefactor Plancia Magna.

items.text: Stadium. One of the best-preserved stadiums in Anatolia: the seating is carried on seventy vaults, every third one an entrance and the rest shops. The north end closes in a horseshoe; the south end is open.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the Hellenistic Gate, the Colonnaded Street, the Theatre and the Roman Baths.
items.speech: As you walk round, don't miss the Hellenistic Gate, the Colonnaded Street, the Theatre and the Roman Baths.

items.text: Did you know? The channel running down the main street was an ancient cooling system for the city. A water channel ran down the centre of the 250-metre colonnaded street: ancient air-conditioning for the summer. Apollonius of Perga, who defined the conic sections, came from here: we owe him the words ellipse, parabola and hyperbola. The city's greatest benefactor was a woman, Plancia Magna, who rebuilt its gate; her statues and inscriptions were found there.

items.text: Enriched by salt, oil and horse trade on the Eurymedon, its theatre was built by the architect Zeno in the 2nd century and survived because the Seljuks reused it as a caravanserai.
items.speech: Enriched by salt, oil and horse trade on the Eurymedon, its theatre was built by the architect Zeno in the 2nd century and survived because the Seljuks reused it as a caravanserai.

items.text: Roman Theatre. The most completely preserved theatre of antiquity. Its seating bank and stage building are bonded into a single block, and it came down to us intact because the Seljuqs kept it in use as a caravanserai.
items.speech: Roman Theatre. The most completely preserved theatre of antiquity. Its seating bank and stage building are bonded into a single block, and it came down to us intact because the Seljuqs kept it in use as a caravanserai.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the Aqueducts, the Basilica, the Agora and the Stadium.
items.speech: As you walk round, don't miss the Aqueducts, the Basilica, the Agora and the Stadium.

items.text: Did you know? The acoustics are so precise that a whisper on stage reaches the 41st row. Its theatre is the best-preserved in the Roman world — the stage building stands to full height, and concerts are still held in it. The architect Zeno is named in an inscription. Legend has the king promising his daughter to whoever built best — and the theatre winning. Its aqueduct is one of antiquity's rare pressurised systems, working on the inverted-siphon principle.

items.text: Wussten Sie schon? Die Akustik ist so präzise, dass ein Flüstern auf der Bühne bis in die 41. Reihe dringt. Sein Theater ist das am besten erhaltene der römischen Welt – das Bühnengebäude steht in voller Höhe, und es finden noch immer Konzerte darin statt. Der Architekt Zenon wird in einer Inschrift genannt. Der Legende nach versprach der König seine Tochter demjenigen, der am besten baute – und das Theater gewann. Sein Aquädukt ist eines der seltenen Drucksysteme der Antike und arbeitet nach dem Prinzip des umgekehrten Siphons.

items.text: Founded by the Pisidians, its natural defences kept invaders out. Abandoned after an earthquake wrecked its water system, it was swallowed by forest.
items.speech: Founded by the Pisidians, its natural defences kept invaders out. Abandoned after an earthquake wrecked its water system, it was swallowed by forest.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the Theatre, the Gymnasium, the Cisterns, the Necropolis and the King's Road.

items.text: Did you know? Its theatre looks out over Güllük mountain — arguably antiquity's most dramatic backdrop. Alexander the Great besieged it and withdrew without taking it: one of the few places in Anatolia to turn him back. It sits above 1,000 metres like an eagle's nest; behind the theatre stage there is nothing but the drop and Mount Güllük. The city has never been systematically excavated. Giant sarcophagi, rock tombs and cisterns lie in the forest where they fell.

Kentin arkasındaki dik kaya duvarı, yüzlerce oyuk mezarla arı peteğine benzer; bu mezarlara nasıl çıkıldığı hâlâ tartışılır. items.text: Did you know? Pinara's legendary founder is Pandarus, regarded as the mythical ancestor of the Lycians. The sheer rock face behind the city is honeycombed with hundreds of tombs, and how anyone reached them is still argued over. The reliefs of the 'Royal Tomb' depict four walled Lycian cities: Lycians drawing their own towns. Its theatre stands in the forest with its seating entirely untouched.

items.text: Did you know? Diogenes' 25,000-word inscription is the longest philosophical text to survive from antiquity. The Epicurean Diogenes had his philosophy carved onto a wall in the city's market: some 80 metres long, the longest known inscription of antiquity. It lies at 1,400 metres on a wooded ridge, and blocks of that inscription are still being gathered among the ruins.

items.text: Founded as a trading colony in the 2nd century BC, the city grew with the support of the Cappadocian king Archelaus. Linked to land by an isthmus, it was one of Cilicia's important ports with its theatre, agora and churches.

items.text: Did you know? The city's name means 'olive city', and the island's olive trees still bear fruit today. The city began on an islet; when the channel silted up the island joined the shore and the city spread onto it. King Archelaus of Cappadocia made it his second capital and renamed it Sebaste in honour of Augustus. Theatre, baths and basilica line up along the shore, with the modern road running straight through them.

items.text: Founded by Seleucus I Nicator, the city grew on the banks of the Göksu (Calycadnus) river. At the crossroads of inland routes, it was an important centre of Cilicia in Roman and Byzantine times.

items.text: Did you know? Founded in the 3rd century BC, the city bears the name of the Seleucid dynasty, meaning 'Seleucia on the Calycadnus'. Founded by Seleucus I Nicator, Alexander's general — one of the many cities he named after himself. Frederick Barbarossa drowned in the Göksu — the ancient Calycadnus — here in 1190 on the Third Crusade, and the crusade fell apart. A column of the Temple of Jupiter and the Roman bridge still stand amid the traffic of modern Silifke.

items.text: Biliyor muydunuz? Höyükte dokuz farklı kent katmanı var; Homeros'un Truva'sı büyük olasılıkla Troya VI/VII. Höyükte dokuz kent üst üste durur. Schliemann 1871'de kazarken Homeros'un Troya'sını aradı, hızla derine inip aradığı katı geçti ve 'Priamos'un Hazinesi'ni bin yıl daha eski bir katta buldu. Truva Atı'ndan hiçbir iz bulunmadı. Buna karşılık Hitit tabletlerinde, Troya'nın yeriyle uyuşan 'Wilusa' adlı bir kentle yapılan antlaşmalar geçer. Kentin surlarındaki eğimli taş duvar, İlyada'da Patroklos'un üç kez tırmanıp üç kez geri atıldığı duvar sanılır.

items.text: Occupied for 5,000 years, it was excavated by Heinrich Schliemann in the 1870s — proving the legend real while damaging its layers.
items.speech: Occupied for 5,000 years, it was excavated by Heinrich Schliemann in the 1870s, proving the legend real while damaging its layers.

items.text: Trojan horse replica. A replica of the famous wooden horse of Homer's Iliad.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the City walls, the Ramped gateway, the Odeon and the Temple of Athena.
items.speech: As you walk round, don't miss the City walls, the Ramped gateway, the Odeon and the Temple of Athena.

items.text: Did you know? The mound holds nine city layers; Homer's Troy is most likely level VI/VII. Nine cities stand stacked in the mound. Digging in 1871, Schliemann drove straight past the layer he was looking for and found his 'Treasure of Priam' in one a thousand years too old. No trace of the wooden horse has been found. Hittite tablets, however, record treaties with a city called Wilusa, in the right place to be Troy. The battered stone wall of the citadel is taken for the one Patroclus climbs three times, and is thrown back from three times, in the Iliad.

items.text: 5.000 Jahre lang besiedelt, wurde es in den 1870er-Jahren von Heinrich Schliemann ausgegraben – der damit bewies, dass die Legende wahr ist, und zugleich ihre Schichten beschädigte.

items.text: Verpassen Sie beim Rundgang nicht: Stadtmauern, Rampentor, Odeon und Athenatempel.
items.speech: Verpassen Sie beim Rundgang nicht: Stadtmauern, Rampentor, Odeon und Athenatempel.

items.text: Wussten Sie schon? Der Hügel birgt neun Stadtschichten; Homers Troja ist höchstwahrscheinlich Schicht VI/VII. Im Hügel liegen neun Städte übereinander. Als Schliemann 1871 grub, stieß er geradewegs an der gesuchten Schicht vorbei und fand seinen „Schatz des Priamos“ in einer, die tausend Jahre zu alt war. Vom hölzernen Pferd wurde keine Spur gefunden. Hethitische Tontafeln verzeichnen jedoch Verträge mit einer Stadt namens Wilusa, die genau dort lag, wo Troja sein müsste. Die geböschte Steinmauer der Zitadelle gilt als jene, die Patroklos in der Ilias dreimal erklimmt und von der er dreimal zurückgeworfen wird.

items.text: Во время прогулки не пропустите: Городские стены, Ворота с пандусом, Одеон и Храм Афины.
items.speech: Во время прогулки не пропустите: Городские стены, Ворота с пандусом, Одеон и Храм Афины.

items.text: А вы знали? Холм хранит девять городских слоёв; Троя Гомера — скорее всего, слой VI/VII. В холме друг над другом лежат девять городов. Копая в 1871 году, Шлиман прошёл прямо сквозь искомый слой и нашёл свой «клад Приама» в слое на тысячу лет древнее. Никаких следов деревянного коня не найдено. Однако хеттские таблички упоминают договоры с городом под названием Вилуса, который находился как раз там, где должна быть Троя. Покатую каменную стену цитадели принимают за ту, на которую в «Илиаде» трижды взбирается Патрокл и с которой его трижды отбрасывают.

items.text: Did you know? Assos sarcophagi were believed to consume flesh — hence the word 'sarcophagus'. Aristotle spent three years here, founded a school, and married the ruler's niece. He began his biological work in the gulf below. The Temple of Athena is the only archaic Doric temple in Anatolia. Saint Paul walked here from Troas on his third journey and took ship from this harbour; Acts records it by name.

items.text: A Milesian colony whose electrum coins became a Mediterranean standard; its Temple of Hadrian was called the eighth wonder in antiquity.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the Temple of Hadrian, the Amphitheatre, the Aqueducts and the Harbour remains.

items.text: Did you know? Its amphitheatre is one of only a handful of true amphitheatres in Anatolia. The Temple of Hadrian was called the eighth wonder of the world; travellers in the fifteenth century still counted thirty columns standing. The city was an island. A sandbar tied it to the mainland, and it now sits on the neck of the Kapıdağ peninsula. Cyzicene electrum staters served for centuries as a common currency across Aegean and Black Sea trade.

items.text: Did you know? A 4th-century basilica lies submerged beneath the waters of Lake İznik. The Council of Nicaea met here in 325 and wrote the creed still recited today. It hosted a second council in 787, which brought iconoclasm to an end. When the crusaders took Constantinople in 1204, Nicaea became the Byzantine capital in exile — and the empire was won back from here.

items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Alexandria Troas, an ancient city in Çanakkale province. Its period: 310 BC, 6th century AD. Founded by Antigonus, one of Alexander's generals, it was one of the largest ancient cities of Anatolia.

items.text: Founded by Antigonus Monophthalmus in 310 BC in the Troad, it quickly became one of Rome's most important harbour cities. Augustus and Hadrian visited it, and St Paul passed through on his journeys west. Covering some 400 hectares, it was even larger than Ephesus and one of the largest urban fabrics of the Roman world.

items.text: Did you know? The city covered roughly 400 hectares — even more than Ephesus, making it one of the largest Roman cities in Anatolia. One of Anatolia's largest ports under Rome — and by ancient report, Constantine seriously considered founding his capital here. It was here that Saint Paul dreamed of the man calling 'Come over to Macedonia' — Christianity's crossing into Europe began at this harbour. The ruins are scattered through oak woodland; locals call the bath building the 'Honey Palace'.

items.text: Did you know? The Persian reliefs of Dascylium are among the most important examples of Achaemenid art found in Anatolia. It was the seat of the Persian satrapy of western Anatolia — the best-documented site of Persian rule in the region. Hundreds of clay sealings survive: all that is left of a burned archive, preserved because the fire baked them. The mound overlooks Lake Manyas; ancient sources describe the satrap's garden here as a hunting park.

items.text: Did you know? Lampsacus had one of the richest mints in the ancient world, and its patron god Priapus was the deity of gardens. The Persian king Artaxerxes granted this city to the exiled Athenian Themistocles to cover his wine. The philosopher Anaxagoras died here, and the city marked his memory with an annual holiday from school for its children. It was the centre of the cult of Priapus, which is why its name recurs so often in ancient literature.

items.text: Home to some 8,000 people who entered their houses through the roof. Its wall paintings and mother-goddess figurines are landmarks of prehistoric art.
items.speech: Home to some 8,000 people who entered their houses through the roof. Its wall paintings and mother-goddess figurines are landmarks of prehistoric art.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the North excavation shelter, the Experimental house, the Wall paintings and the South mound.

items.text: Did you know? A painting here is considered the world's oldest known map — and oldest volcano depiction. This 9,000-year-old settlement has no streets. Houses were built wall to wall and entered by ladder through the roof: the rooftops were the street. The dead were buried beneath the floors of the houses, under the platforms where the family slept. One wall painting shows a settlement plan from above with an erupting volcano behind it — argued by some to be the oldest map in the world.

Höyüğün eteğindeki karum, tüccarların yaşadığı ayrı bir mahalleydi, bilinen en eski uluslararası ticaret kolonilerinden.

items.text: Assyrian merchants founded a karum here; over 23,000 cuneiform tablets found on site mark the beginning of written history in Anatolia.

items.text: Did you know? Among the tablets is one of the world's earliest known marriage contracts. Anatolia met writing here. The 23,000-plus cuneiform tablets left by Assyrian merchants are the earliest written documents from Anatolia. The tablets are not epic but bookkeeping: promissory notes, partnership contracts, court records, letters home. One merchant's wife writes telling him to send better cloth. The karum at the foot of the mound was a separate merchants' quarter: one of the earliest known international trading colonies.

items.text: Homeland of the Cybele cult, Pessinus was the holiest city of Phrygia. In 205 BC Rome carried off the city's sacred black stone to secure victory over Hannibal, and the city remained important under Galatian and Roman rule.

items.text: Did you know? The Romans' removal of Cybele's sacred black stone here to Rome marks the first transfer of an Anatolian cult to the capital. It was the sanctuary of Cybele. In 204 BC, following a prophecy meant to defeat Hannibal, Rome took the goddess's sacred black stone from here to the capital. The marble steps before the sanctuary served both as a ceremonial stair and as theatre seating. The stream dividing the city was channelled in antiquity between marble-faced banks.

items.text: Did you know? The '42 Martyrs of Amorium', captured during the 838 siege, became one of the most famous tales of Christian history. One of Byzantium's largest military bases in Anatolia, and the home town of a ruling dynasty. In 838 the caliph al-Mu'tasim besieged and destroyed it. The execution of the officers who refused to convert entered the Byzantine calendar as the Forty-Two Martyrs of Amorium.

items.text: Did you know? The distinctive pottery known as 'Alişar ware' gives its name to the 'Alişar IV' period in archaeology. Excavated between 1927 and 1932, this mound is where the chronology of Anatolian archaeology was first built; other digs long dated themselves against it. Hattian, Assyrian trading-colony and Hittite layers sit one atop another: three worlds in a single hill.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Comana, an ancient city in Adana province. Its period: 2nd millennium BC – 6th century AD. A temple city of the Mother Goddess Ma, linked to the Hittite city of Kummanni.

items.text: Identified with the Kummanni of Hittite records, the city ruled a great temple-state of the Mother Goddess Ma in classical times. Called a 'holy city' under Rome, Comana hosted hundreds of sacred attendants.

items.text: Did you know? Comana was known for its school of gladiators and its sacred attendants, regarded as priestesses of the goddess. It was a temple state: its ruler was the high priest of the goddess Ma, and ranked second only to the king. Strabo puts the number of sacred servants attached to the temple at over six thousand.

items.text: Biliyor muydunuz? Kadeş Antlaşması'nın bir kopyası BM binasının duvarında sergileniyor. Hitit İmparatorluğu'nun başkentiydi ve 6 kilometrelik surla çevriliydi; Yerkapı'nın altındaki 70 metrelik taş tünel bugün de yürünebiliyor. Kadeş Antlaşması'nın Hititçe kopyası burada bulundu. Bilinen en eski yazılı barış antlaşmasıdır ve bir kopyası New York'taki BM binasında sergilenir. Yazılıkaya açık hava tapınağının kaya duvarlarında altmıştan fazla tanrı, geçit töreni halinde yürür.

items.text: Anatolia's first great empire was ruled from here. Its archives held the Treaty of Kadesh — the earliest known written peace treaty.

items.text: Did you know? A copy of the Treaty of Kadesh hangs on a wall at the United Nations. Capital of the Hittite Empire, ringed by six kilometres of wall; the 70-metre stone tunnel under Yerkapı can still be walked through. The Hittite copy of the Treaty of Kadesh was found here — the oldest known written peace treaty, with a replica on display at the UN in New York. On the rock walls of the Yazılıkaya open-air sanctuary, more than sixty gods walk in procession.

items.text: Verpassen Sie beim Rundgang nicht: Löwentor, Großer Tempel und Yazılıkaya.

items.text: Wussten Sie schon? Eine Kopie des Vertrags von Kadesch hängt an einer Wand bei den Vereinten Nationen. Die Hauptstadt des Hethiterreiches war von sechs Kilometern Mauer umgeben; den 70 Meter langen Steintunnel unter Yerkapı kann man noch heute durchschreiten. Hier wurde die hethitische Fassung des Vertrags von Kadesch gefunden – der älteste bekannte schriftliche Friedensvertrag, von dem eine Nachbildung bei den Vereinten Nationen in New York ausgestellt ist. Auf den Felswänden des Freiluftheiligtums Yazılıkaya schreiten mehr als sechzig Götter in einer Prozession.

items.text: Отсюда управлялась первая великая держава Анатолии. В её архивах хранился Кадешский договор — древнейший известный письменный мирный договор.

items.text: А вы знали? Копия Кадешского договора висит на стене в Организации Объединённых Наций. Столица Хеттской державы была окружена шестью километрами стен; по 70-метровому каменному туннелю под Еркапы можно пройти и сегодня. Здесь была найдена хеттская копия Кадешского договора — древнейшего известного письменного мирного договора, реплика которого выставлена в ООН в Нью-Йорке. На скальных стенах святилища под открытым небом Язылыкая более шестидесяти богов шествуют в процессии.

Sfenksli Kapı'nın iki yanındaki kabartmalar, Hitit dinî törenlerini adım adım gösterir. Kazı 1935'te Atatürk'ün talimatıyla başladı ve Cumhuriyet'in kendi olanaklarıyla yürüttüğü ilk büyük kazılardan biri oldu.

items.text: The first excavation of the Turkish Republic took place here; the sun discs from its royal tombs became a symbol of Anatolian civilisation.
items.speech: The first excavation of the Turkish Republic took place here; the sun discs from its royal tombs became a symbol of Anatolian civilisation.

items.text: Sphinx Gate. A monumental gate flanked by sphinx reliefs.
items.speech: Sphinx Gate. A monumental gate flanked by sphinx reliefs.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the Hattian royal tombs, the Hittite temple and the Orthostat reliefs.
items.speech: As you walk round, don't miss the Hattian royal tombs, the Hittite temple and the Orthostat reliefs.

items.text: Did you know? The sun disc found here served for decades as the emblem of Ankara. The bronze 'sun discs' from its royal tombs became the most reproduced archaeological emblem in modern Türkiye. The reliefs flanking the Sphinx Gate show a Hittite religious ceremony step by step. Excavation began in 1935 on Atatürk's instruction, among the first major digs the young Republic ran with its own resources.

items.text: Did you know? The city is named after Pompey the Great, who reorganised the region in 64 BC. Founded by Pompey after he cleared the Black Sea of pirates, it became the capital of Paphlagonia. Its colonnaded street and mosaic villa floors show how far Roman luxury reached even into provincial towns.

items.text: Biliyor muydunuz? Kuşkayası'ndaki kaya kabartması Roma yol ağının bakım kaydı gibidir. items.text: Did you know? The Kuşkayası rock relief functions as a maintenance record of the Roman road network. Queen Amastris founded the city and gave it her own name: one of the few ancient cities named for a woman. Pliny wrote to Trajan asking leave to cover the open sewer running through the city — and the emperor's reply survives too. The Roman 'Bird Gate' still stands within the street fabric of modern Amasra.

items.text: Did you know? The geographer Strabo came from Amaseia and described his city as 'a fortress built by nature'. The geographer Strabo was born here. The man who wrote the first comprehensive geography of the known world also described his own town. The rock tombs of the Pontic kings are cut into the cliff above the town, and are lit at night. Under the Ottomans, princes learned to govern here as provincial governors — hence the town's name, 'city of princes'.

items.text: Did you know? The Cynic philosopher Diogenes was born here, and the city lent its name to the reddish pigment sinopia. Diogenes the Cynic came from here — the man who lived in a jar and, asked by Alexander what he wanted, said 'stand out of my light'. It has the only naturally sheltered harbour on the Black Sea, which made it both a Milesian colony and the Pontic naval base. Mithridates VI, the king who held out longest against Rome, was born here.

items.text: Did you know? Clearchus, one of antiquity's philosopher-tyrants, seized power here, and the city was known for its philosophical school. Antiquity held that the caves here — Cehennemağzı, the Mouth of Hell — were where Heracles dragged Cerberus up from the underworld. A Megarian colony, it is singled out in ancient sources for reducing the native Mariandynians to serfdom.

items.text: Did you know? Gold jewellery from the royal tombs found at Amisos in 1995 is displayed in the Samsun Museum. The Hellenistic gold jewellery from its tumuli is the most striking evidence of wealth on this coast; it is now in the Samsun museum. One of Mithridates' principal ports, it was burned during the resistance to Rome.

items.text: Did you know? Tieion is one of the rare Anatolian cities that carried its ancient name to the present day. This city at Filyos is among the least excavated on the Black Sea coast; its theatre has only recently been uncovered. Ancient sources say it took its name from a priest, Tios, and that it was the smallest independent city in the region.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Göbekli Tepe, a sanctuary in Şanlıurfa province. Its period: 9600 BC. The world's oldest known temple complex — T-shaped pillars that rewrote history.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Göbekli Tepe, a sanctuary in Şanlıurfa province. Its period: 9600 BC. The world's oldest known temple complex, T-shaped pillars that rewrote history.

items.text: Built by hunter-gatherers millennia before agriculture, its discovery reversed the assumption that settlement preceded monumental religion.
items.speech: Built by hunter-gatherers millennia before agriculture, its discovery reversed the assumption that settlement preceded monumental religion.

items.text: Enclosures A–D. One of the oldest monumental structures known, and the earliest dated of the circles. The two pillars at its centre have arms, hands and a belt: the stones are human in form, and they face one another.
items.speech: Enclosures A–D. One of the oldest monumental structures known, and the earliest dated of the circles. The two pillars at its centre have arms, hands and a belt: the stones are human in form, and they face one another.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the T-shaped pillars, the Animal reliefs and the Protective canopy.
items.speech: As you walk round, don't miss the T-shaped pillars, the Animal reliefs and the Protective canopy.

items.text: Did you know? It predates Stonehenge by about 6,000 years and the pyramids of Giza by 7,000. Its builders were hunter-gatherers, not farmers — which reversed the assumption that people settle down first and build temples afterwards. The T-shaped pillars carry carved foxes, snakes, scorpions and cranes; the heaviest weighs about sixteen tonnes.

items.text: Wussten Sie schon? Er ist etwa 6.000 Jahre älter als Stonehenge und 7.000 Jahre älter als die Pyramiden von Gizeh. Auf den T-förmigen Pfeilern sind Füchse, Schlangen, Skorpione und Kraniche eingemeißelt; der schwerste wiegt etwa sechzehn Tonnen.

items.text: Did you know? The 'Gypsy Girl' mosaic is displayed in the world's largest mosaic museum. Its name is Greek for 'crossing': this was the easiest ford on the Euphrates, and the lock on the eastern trade. The mosaics saved in the rescue dig before the Birecik dam flooded the site include the 'Gypsy Girl', now among the best-known ancient images in Türkiye. Rome's Legio IV Scythica was stationed here, and the city's wealth came directly from the frontier garrison.

items.text: King Antiochus I of Commagene built his hierotheion here. The statues, fusing eastern and western gods, lost their heads to earthquakes.
items.speech: King Antiochus I of Commagene built his hierotheion here. The statues, fusing eastern and western gods, lost their heads to earthquakes.

items.text: East terrace. The tomb-sanctuary King Antiochus I of Commagene built at 2,150 metres: at the foot of a gravel tumulus, gods eight to nine metres tall sit enthroned — the king, Commagene, Zeus, Apollo and Herakles — with an eagle and a lion at either end and a stepped altar facing them. The model puts the heads back on their shoulders.

items.text: Did you know? The lion relief on the west terrace is one of the oldest known star charts. King Antiochus I of Commagene raised a burial mound for himself at 2,150 metres and ringed it with colossal gods. Earthquakes brought every head to the ground, and they now sit apart from their bodies. The pantheon is deliberately hybrid — Zeus-Oromasdes, Apollo-Mithras. The king fused Greek and Persian gods into a single dynastic religion.

items.text: König Antiochos I. von Kommagene errichtete hier sein Hierotheion. Die Statuen, die östliche und westliche Götter miteinander verschmelzen, verloren ihre Köpfe durch Erdbeben.

items.text: Ostterrasse. Das Grabheiligtum, das König Antiochos I. von Kommagene auf 2.150 Metern errichten ließ: Am Fuß eines Geröllhügels thronen acht bis neun Meter hohe Götter – der König, Kommagene, Zeus, Apollon und Herakles –, an beiden Enden ein Adler und ein Löwe, ihnen gegenüber ein Stufenaltar. items.text: Wussten Sie schon? Das Löwenrelief auf der Westterrasse ist eine der ältesten bekannten Sternkarten. König Antiochos I. von Kommagene ließ sich auf 2.150 Metern einen Grabhügel aufschütten und umgab ihn mit kolossalen Göttern. Erdbeben stürzten jeden Kopf zu Boden, und heute stehen sie getrennt von ihren Körpern. Das Pantheon ist bewusst hybrid – Zeus-Oromasdes, Apollon-Mithras. Der König verschmolz griechische und persische Götter zu einer einzigen dynastischen Religion.

items.text: А вы знали? Рельеф со львом на западной террасе — одна из древнейших известных звёздных карт. Царь Коммагены Антиох I насыпал для себя погребальный курган на высоте 2150 метров и окружил его колоссальными богами. Землетрясения сбросили на землю все головы, и теперь они стоят отдельно от своих тел. Пантеон намеренно смешанный — Зевс-Оромазд, Аполлон-Митра. Царь слил греческих и персидских богов в единую династическую религию.

items.text: A centre of the moon-god Sin and a caravan crossroads, it later became a hub of medieval astronomy and medicine.

items.text: Beehive houses. Harran's iconic beehive houses with conical mud-brick roofs that keep interiors cool.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the Great Mosque and minaret, the Harran Castle and the City gates.

items.text: Did you know? The beehive houses are built of mudbrick and stay about 10°C cooler inside. One of the longest continuously inhabited places on earth; in the Book of Genesis, Abraham stayed here with his family. The conical mud-brick houses are an architecture for staying cool without electricity, and their shape has not changed in millennia. It was the cult centre of the moon god Sin and one of the last places to give up its pagan tradition; under Islam its school became famous for astronomy and mathematics.

items.text: Built by Emperor Anastasius as a fortress city on the Sasanian frontier; its water system and dungeon are engineering marvels.

items.text: Did you know? The huge cistern was long mistaken for a dungeon — it was the city's water reservoir. Byzantium's forward fortress on the Sasanian frontier. At the Battle of Dara in 530, Belisarius defeated a numerically superior Persian army here. The vast rock-cut cisterns were the real weapon in a siege: they decided how long the city could hold. The multi-storey rock-cut tomb chambers in the necropolis are among the most striking late antique structures in the region.

items.text: Founded at a Euphrates crossing, the city was a regional capital under Mitanni, the Hittites and the Neo-Hittites. The Battle of Carchemish in 605 BC ended Assyria, and the site was excavated by Leonard Woolley in 1911–14.

items.text: Did you know? Carchemish lies on today's Turkish-Syrian border, leaving part of the mound inside a military zone. The city's Neo-Hittite reliefs form the backbone of the Museum of Anatolian Civilizations in Ankara. T. E. Lawrence — Lawrence of Arabia — worked here as a young archaeologist on the 1911-14 excavations. The site straddles the Turkish-Syrian border and could not be dug for years because it was mined.

items.text: Did you know? King Kilamuwa's inscription is one of the earliest Semitic-language texts found in Anatolia. Its circular double walls make a city plan with few parallels in the Near East. The inscriptions of kings Kilamuwa and Panamuwa are primary documents in the history of the Semitic languages; Phoenician, Aramaic and Luwian were all in use here. Its gate lions are now displayed in the museums of Berlin and Istanbul.

items.text: Did you know? The relief of Mithridates here is one of the largest relief carvings in Anatolia. The summer capital of Commagene: Antiochus, whose tomb crowns Nemrut, made this a sanctuary for his father Mithridates. The relief of Heracles shaking hands with King Mithridates is the best-preserved Commagene work — a god and a king shown the same height. A 158-metre shaft cut straight into the rock remains a structure whose purpose is not fully understood.

items.text: Inhabited since the Neolithic era in its Tigris-side caves, Hasankeyf became a capital under the Artuqids and Akkoyunlu. In 2020 the waters of the Ilısu Dam covered part of the old town, but the citadel still stands.

items.text: Did you know? Caves along the Tigris at Hasankeyf show evidence of settlement some 10,000 years old. A 12,000-year-old settlement, largely submerged by the Ilısu dam in 2020. The tomb of Zeynel Bey was lifted whole and moved to new ground. The Artuqid bridge was reckoned the widest-spanning in the Middle East of its day; its piers still break the water. Thousands of cave dwellings were cut into the cliff, and some were still lived in during the twentieth century.

items.text: Did you know? Local tradition holds that the Prophet Moses lived here, and his well is still visited today. items.text: Did you know? The Menüçehr Mosque is regarded as the oldest known Seljuk mosque in Anatolia. Known as the city of a thousand and one churches, it approached a hundred thousand people at its height, spoken of alongside Constantinople and Baghdad. Trdat, the cathedral's architect, was the man who repaired the earthquake-collapsed dome of Hagia Sophia in Constantinople. When the Silk Road shifted, and after the earthquake of 1319, the city emptied. It stands today on the border, alone in the steppe.

items.text: Wussten Sie schon? Die Menüçehr-Moschee gilt als die älteste bekannte seldschukische Moschee Anatoliens. Bekannt als die Stadt der tausendundein Kirchen, näherte sie sich auf ihrem Höhepunkt hunderttausend Einwohnern und wurde in einem Atemzug mit Konstantinopel und Bagdad genannt. Trdat, der Architekt der Kathedrale, war derjenige, der die bei einem Erdbeben eingestürzte Kuppel der Hagia Sophia in Konstantinopel reparierte. Als sich die Seidenstraße verlagerte, und nach dem Erdbeben von 1319, leerte sich die Stadt. Heute steht sie an der Grenze, allein in der Steppe.

items.text: А вы знали? Мечеть Менучехра считается древнейшей известной сельджукской мечетью в Анатолии. Известный как город тысячи и одной церкви, в период расцвета он приближался к ста тысячам жителей и упоминался наравне с Константинополем и Багдадом. Трдат, архитектор собора, — тот самый человек, который восстановил обрушившийся при землетрясении купол Айя-Софии в Константинополе. Когда Шёлковый путь сместился, и после землетрясения 1319 года город опустел. Сегодня он стоит на границе, одинокий посреди степи.

Argişti'nin yıllıklarına, kalenin dik yüzünden bakılabiliyor. Pers Kralı Xerxes'in üç dilli çivi yazılı yazıtı, kayalığın erişilmesi güç bir yerine oyulmuştur ve hâlâ okunabiliyor. Kalenin eteğindeki düzlük, 1915 öncesi Eski Van şehrinin yeridir; şehir bugün yok, sadece iki cami ayakta.

items.text: Founded by King Sarduri, it was Urartu's administrative heart; rock-cut royal tombs and cuneiform inscriptions survive.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the Royal tombs, the Cuneiform inscriptions and the Old Van city.
items.speech: As you walk round, don't miss the Royal tombs, the Cuneiform inscriptions and the Old Van city.

items.text: Did you know? A trilingual inscription of the Persian king Xerxes is carved into the cliff here. Capital of Urartu. The rock-cut royal tombs and the annals of Argishti I look out from the sheer face of the citadel. Xerxes' trilingual cuneiform inscription is cut into an all but unreachable spot on the cliff, and can still be read. The flat ground below the citadel is where the old city of Van stood before 1915; nothing of it remains but two mosques.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Arslantepe, a mound in Malatya province. Its period: 6th millennium BC. A mound that holds one of the earliest known palaces in the world.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Arslantepe, a mound in Malatya province. Its period: 6th millennium BC. A mound that holds one of the earliest known palaces in the world.

items.text: Its layers document the birth of the state and centralised power; the swords found here are among the oldest metal swords known.
items.speech: Its layers document the birth of the state and centralised power; the swords found here are among the oldest metal swords known.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the 4th-millennium palace, the Lion gate, the Wall paintings and the Protective shelter.
items.speech: As you walk round, don't miss the 4th-millennium palace, the Lion gate, the Wall paintings and the Protective shelter.

items.text: Did you know? Seal impressions here show how bureaucracy worked before writing was invented. Its building of around 3300 BC is among the earliest known palaces in the world: the first architecture of the thing we call a state. The arsenical copper swords found here are counted as the oldest known swords in the world. It was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2021.

items.text: Did you know? The dome of Harput's Great Mosque is among the oldest mosque domes in Anatolia. A fortress used without a break from Urartu to the Ottomans. Its name, 'Milk Castle', comes from a legend that milk was mixed into the mortar instead of water. The city of Elazığ was founded when Harput came down to the plain in the nineteenth century: the modern town is the old one, relocated.

items.text: The rock was occupied in Urartian times and rebuilt in the 17th century by Sarı Süleyman Bey of the Mahmudi tribe. The castle is among the finest surviving examples of Ottoman-Van architecture.

items.text: Did you know? The Persian inscription on the castle gate reads 'there is nothing like it in the world'. Built in 1643 by Sarı Süleyman, bey of the Mahmudi, and one of the most theatrical castles in Anatolia as it wraps a whole rock outcrop. The story goes that the bey had the architect's hand cut off so that its like could never be built again.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Akdamar Island, a monument in Van province. Its period: 10th century AD – today. The Church of the Holy Cross on an island in Lake Van, famous for its carved reliefs.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Akdamar Island, a monument in Van province. Its period: 10th century AD, today. The Church of the Holy Cross on an island in Lake Van, famous for its carved reliefs.

items.text: Built in 915–921 for King Gagik I by the architect-monk Manuel, the church was the royal church of the Kingdom of Vaspurakan. Its biblical reliefs on the exterior walls are unique in the world.

items.text: Did you know? In 2015 a service was held in the church for the first time in a century, a tradition that continues each September. The exterior of the Church of the Holy Cross, built for King Gagik I between 915 and 921, is covered wall to wall in relief: Jonah, David and Goliath, vine scrolls and animals. The church was restored as a museum in 2007, and a service has been held there once a year since.

items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Karahan Tepe, a mound in Şanlıurfa province. Its period: 10th millennium BC. A pre-pottery Neolithic sanctuary in Şanlıurfa, known as Göbekli Tepe's 'sister site' for its T-shaped pillars and sculptures.

items.text: First identified in 1997 by Bahattin Çelik, the site has been excavated since 2019 under the Taş Tepeler (Stone Hills) Project. Its monumental structures, dated to the 10th–9th millennium BC, show that hunter-gatherer communities could organize complex building and ritual work.

items.text: Did you know? Locals call the site 'Keçilitepe', and the 2.3 m seated male statue found in 2023 is among the earliest realistic human sculptures known. A contemporary of Göbekli Tepe. In the main chamber eleven pillars were left standing out of the bedrock itself, and a human head emerges from the wall. It is one of the hubs of the 'Taş Tepeler' research programme covering similar sites in the region, and only a small part of it has been dug.

items.text: Did you know? The salvaged stone heads and the stele known as the 'Nevali Çori Stela' are today displayed in the Şanlıurfa Museum. It lies beneath the Atatürk dam. The T-shaped pillars found here were the first sign that such a world existed, years before Göbekli Tepe was dug. Its limestone human and bird figures are among the oldest known monumental sculpture.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Aşıklı Höyük, a mound in Aksaray province. Its period: 9th–8th millennium BC. A pre-pottery Neolithic mound near Aksaray that has yielded the world's earliest domesticated sheep and moulded mudbrick architecture.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Aşıklı Höyük, a mound in Aksaray province. Its period: 9th–8th millennium BC. A pre-pottery Neolithic mound near Aksaray that has yielded the world's earliest domesticated sheep and moulded mudbrick architecture.

items.text: Occupied almost continuously for about a millennium between c. 8200 and 7500 BC, the site has been excavated since 1989 by Istanbul University. Its moulded mudbrick houses, planned streets and sheep domestication make it one of the earliest examples of sedentary life in Anatolia.

items.text: Did you know? The earliest domesticated sheep bones found at Aşıklı are among the strongest pieces of evidence that sheep were domesticated in present-day Turkey. The oldest known village in central Anatolia, from about 8400 BC, and a step-by-step record of how farming arrived here. A woman's skeleton found here bears the trace of skull surgery, among the oldest evidence of brain surgery anywhere — and she lived on for some time afterwards.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Acemhöyük, a mound in Aksaray province. Its period: 3rd–2nd millennium BC. A mound near Aksaray that was one of the richest centres of the Assyrian Trade Colonies period, renowned for its palaces and ivory artefacts.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Acemhöyük, a mound in Aksaray province. Its period: 3rd–2nd millennium BC. A mound near Aksaray that was one of the richest centres of the Assyrian Trade Colonies period, renowned for its palaces and ivory artefacts.

items.text: Likely ancient Purušhanda (Purušḫanda), the mound was inhabited from the early 3rd millennium BC and reached its peak during the Assyrian Trade Colonies period (c. 1950–1750 BC). With monumental buildings such as the 'Saray' and 'Hatipler Sarayı', it was a trade and administration centre contemporary with Kültepe.

items.text: Did you know? An ivory box inlaid with lapis lazuli, bronze and iron found at the mound is among the finest examples of early luxury craftsmanship in Anatolia. One of the great centres of the Assyrian trading-colony period; its palace stores yielded ivories and obsidian vessels. Seal impressions from the palace document, name by name, who the trade with Mesopotamia and Syria was done with.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Sapinuwa, an ancient city in Çorum province. Its period: 14th century BC. A Hittite religious and administrative city at Ortaköy, Çorum, that has produced thousands of cuneiform tablets.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Sapinuwa, an ancient city in Çorum province. Its period: 14th century BC. A Hittite religious and administrative city at Ortaköy, Çorum, that has produced thousands of cuneiform tablets.

items.text: Excavated since 1990 under Aygül and Mustafa Süel, the city served as a royal residence during the reign of Tudhaliya II in the 14th century BC. With an area of about 9 km² it was one of the largest cities of the ancient Near East, and thousands of tablets survived after being baked in a fire.

items.text: Did you know? Over 3,000 tablets and fragments from Building A are written in Hittite, Hurrian, Akkadian and other languages, including many Hurrian purification rituals. The fire that destroyed the palace baked the clay tablets hard, carrying the archive down to us instead of destroying it.

items.text: Did you know? The word 'Midas' in the inscription is not the legendary king but an epithet of the Phrygian Mother Goddess Matar; the monument was an open-air temple for her statue, not a tomb. The Phrygian rock monument stands seventeen metres high, and an old Phrygian inscription on it names Midas. It looks like a temple façade but there is no chamber behind it: everything, the door included, is relief — the idea of a temple drawn on rock.

items.text: Built on a 60 m volcanic hill overlooking the Euphrates in the 9th–7th century BC, the fortress was excavated by Tahsin Özgüç between 1959 and 1968. Its apadana-palace, great hall, storehouses and multi-roomed rock-cut tombs are key examples of Urartian architecture.

items.text: Did you know? Fragments of Urartian wall painting found at Altıntepe are among the most important known examples of palace wall painting in the Urartian kingdom. Its wall paintings and the bronzes from its royal tombs are among the best-preserved works of Urartian art.

items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Ayanis Fortress, an ancient city in Van province. Its period: 7th century BC. An Urartian fortress built by King Rusa II on the eastern shore of Lake Van, famous for its exceptionally well-preserved Temple of Haldi.

items.text: Founded around 673/2 BC by Rusa II as 'Rusahinili opposite Mount Eiduru', the fortress was abandoned after an earthquake and fire in the mid-7th century BC. Because the collapse effectively sealed the site, its temple walls, inscriptions and bronze weapons are remarkably preserved.

items.text: Did you know? One of the longest Urartian inscriptions survives on the temple façade, and the lion-headed bronze shield found in 1997 is the first example of its kind ever recovered in excavation. Built in one campaign by Rusa II in the seventh century BC and destroyed soon after, the fortress is a single-period time capsule. The long cuneiform inscription on the wall of the temple of Haldi tells the fortress's founding in the king's own words.

items.text: Founded in the 10th century BC, Kaunos was an important trading city with two harbours, ruled in turn by the Persians, Rhodes and Rome. Siltation of the Dalyan river filled its harbours and cut it off from the sea. A malaria epidemic led to its abandonment in the 15th century AD.

items.text: Did you know? Around 150 rock-cut tombs are carved into the cliff face; the temple-fronted ones date to the 4th century BC and show Lycian influence. Its harbour silted into a lake: a maritime city now stranded behind the reed beds. Ancient writers describe the Caunians as sallow with malaria; Strabo remarks on the greenish complexion of its people.

items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Ancient City of Stratonikeia, an ancient city in Muğla province. Its period: 3rd century BC. The 'City of Gladiators' at Eskihisar near Yatağan, a vast ancient city built of marble.

items.text: The settlement, known as Atriya in Hittite times, was renamed after Stratonike, the wife of the Seleucid king Antiochus I, after 281 BC. A major Carian city in the Hellenistic and Roman periods, it housed a renowned gladiator school under Rome. It remained continuously inhabited through the Byzantine, Beylik and Ottoman periods.

items.text: Did you know? The city is nicknamed the 'City of Gladiators' because gladiatorial games were held in its huge theatre. An Ottoman village was built inside the ancient city. The houses, coffee house and fountain of Eskihisar stand among ancient columns — two layers living inside each other. Its north gate is one of the largest ancient city gates in Anatolia. The city takes its name from the Seleucid queen Stratonice — the woman of the famous story in which she was married to her stepson's father.
