items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Labraunda (Sanctuary of Zeus Labraundos), a sanctuary in Muğla province. Its period: 7th century BC. The mountain sanctuary of Zeus Labraundos high in the Latmos mountains, linked to Mylasa by a sacred road.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Labraunda (Sanctuary of Zeus Labraundos), a sanctuary in Muğla province. Its period: 7th century BC. The mountain sanctuary of Zeus Labraundos high in the Latmos mountains, linked to Mylasa by a sacred road.

items.text: The earliest finds at the sanctuary date to around 600 BC. In the 4th century BC the Hecatomnid rulers Mausolus and his brother Idrieus transformed it into a splendid cult centre with the Temple of Zeus, androns, stoas and propylaia. The sanctuary continued in use in Roman times, and the cult lasted until a Byzantine church was built on the site.

items.text: Did you know? Zeus Labraundos was depicted holding a double-headed axe (labrys); the word 'labyrinth' shares the same root. The sanctuary of Zeus Labraundos was built by the Carian satrap Mausolus and his brother Idrieus: the mountain temple of the dynasty that raised the Mausoleum. A fourteen-kilometre Sacred Way linked it to Mylasa, and the procession is known to have climbed it on foot. Its andrones, the royal banqueting halls, are the best-preserved examples known in the Greek world.

items.text: Founded by Magnetes from Thessaly, the city was moved around 400 BC to a new site on the Lethaios river. It reached its golden age under the Seleucids and the Kingdom of Pergamon and was an independent city in the Roman period. Excavated by Carl Humann in 1891, the site is still being excavated today.

The Maeander's silt buried the city again and again; its stadium lay underground for centuries before excavation brought it back. The Amazonomachy frieze of the temple is now split between museums in Paris and Berlin.

items.text: Founded in the 11th–10th century BC, Teos was one of the twelve cities of the Ionian League. Falling to Persia in the 6th century BC, some citizens fled to found Abdera in 543 BC. In the Hellenistic period the city came under Pergamon and hosted the Guild of Dionysiac Artists in the late 3rd century BC, keeping its importance in Roman times.

items.text: Did you know? The Guild of Dionysiac Artists (Technitai Dionysou) was the ancient world's first professional union of actors, poets and musicians. Its Temple of Dionysus is the largest temple to the god known from the ancient world. The Artists of Dionysus organised here — the first known guild of actors and musicians in history. Anacreon, the poet of wine and love, came from this city.

items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Ancient City of Klazomenai, an ancient city in İzmir province. Its period: 4th millennium BC (Liman Tepe); 8th century BC (city). An Ionian city at Urla; birthplace of the philosopher Anaxagoras and a centre of early industrial olive oil production.

items.text: Settlement at Liman Tepe dates back to the 4th millennium BC. In the 5th century BC, fearing the Persians, the inhabitants left the mainland city and moved to Karantina Island. The city struck some of the earliest silver coins in the 6th century BC, ran advanced olive oil workshops, and Alexander the Great later linked the island to the mainland by a causeway.

items.text: Did you know? The 6th-century BC olive oil workshop, with 15 rock-cut pits, is among the earliest evidence of industrial-scale olive oil production. The sixth-century BC olive oil workshop found here is among the oldest known anywhere, and has been rebuilt and run experimentally. Anaxagoras — put on trial in Athens for saying the sun was a red-hot stone — came from here. The painted terracotta 'Clazomenian sarcophagi' are rare witnesses to archaic painting.

items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Klaros (Sanctuary of Apollo), a sanctuary in İzmir province. Its period: 13th century BC. The renowned oracular sanctuary of Apollo, belonging to Kolophon and rivalling Delphi and Didyma.

items.text: Tradition dates the sanctuary's foundation to the 13th century BC. The Doric oracular temple of Apollo was begun in the 3rd century BC and completed under Hadrian; the oracle operated until the 4th century AD. Linked to Notion by a 2 km sacred road, the sanctuary lay buried under alluvium for centuries and survives exceptionally well preserved.

items.text: Did you know? Eight-metre-high cult statues of Apollo, Artemis and Leto still stand in place in the temple cella, and the sanctuary contains the 'hekatomb' block used to tether a hundred sacrificial animals. An oracle of Apollo. The prophet drank from the sacred spring in a chamber beneath the temple and delivered the answer in verse. The vaulted oracular chambers and the water channel beneath the temple survive, and the stair the prophet went down can still be seen. Fragments of roughly three-metre statues of Apollo, Artemis and Leto were found here: even the surviving feet and hands are taller than a person.

Macellum'un duvarına kazınmış Diocletianus'un Fiyat Fermanı, dünyanın bilinen ilk borsa binası sayılan yapıyı bir belge haline getirir. items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Aizanoi Ancient City, an ancient city in Kütahya province. Its period: Inhabited since the 3rd millennium BC; golden age in the 2nd century AD. Aizanoi in Çavdarhisar, Kütahya, is a Roman city famous for the best-preserved Temple of Zeus in Anatolia.

items.text: Aizanoi's history reaches back to the Early Bronze Age, and the city became an important centre in the Phrygian region during the Hellenistic period. Under Rome, especially in the 2nd century AD, it enjoyed its golden age, when the Temple of Zeus and the theatre-stadium complex were built. It also housed the earliest known ancient stock exchange (macellum) building.

items.text: Temple of Zeus. The best-preserved temple of Zeus in Anatolia: a pseudodipteros of eight by fifteen columns over a vaulted chamber lit by windows. Dedicated under Domitian, most of its columns still stand.

items.text: Did you know? The macellum at Aizanoi is considered the world's first stock exchange building, bearing an inscribed inflation price list. The Temple of Zeus is the best-preserved ancient temple in Anatolia, and beneath it lies a vaulted undercroft belonging to Cybele: two religions, two storeys. Diocletian's Price Edict, carved on the wall of the macellum, turns what is called the first known exchange building into a document. Theatre and stadium were built back to back as a single structure — a combination extremely rare in the ancient world.

items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Letoon Sanctuary, a sanctuary in Muğla province. Its period: 6th century BC, 4th century AD. Letoon, a Lycian sanctuary dedicated to Leto and her twins Apollo and Artemis, is listed together with Xanthos as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

items.text: Letoon was the federal sanctuary of Lycia, where the religious and political decisions of the Lycian League were proclaimed. In the 4th century BC temples to Leto, Artemis and Apollo were built, and the famous trilingual inscription of 337 BC in Lycian, Greek and Aramaic was found here. The sanctuary was gradually abandoned in the Early Christian period.

items.text: Known as 'Zemuri' in Lycian inscriptions, Limyra became the capital of Lycia in the first half of the 4th century BC under King Pericles. Revived under Roman rule, the city was badly damaged by the earthquake of AD 141 and continued to exist as a bishopric in the Byzantine period.

items.text: Did you know? The Kaineus relief at Limyra is the most famous ancient depiction of the hero Kaineus, who was pinned into the ground with spears. Capital of the Lycian king Pericles, with more than four hundred tombs ranged on the cliff above it. Gaius Caesar, Augustus' grandson and heir, died here; the reliefs of the cenotaph raised for him were found in the city.

items.text: A member of the Lycian League, Arykanda was inhabited from the 5th century BC, and its terraced urban layout developed during the Hellenistic and Roman periods. After a major building boom in the 2nd century AD, the city was severely damaged by 6th-century earthquakes and was gradually abandoned.

items.text: Did you know? Arykanda is one of the rare ancient cities built on five large rock-cut terraces ascending a mountainside. It is terraced up a steep slope, theatre, stadium and baths stacked one above another, and its view is singled out among ancient cities. The '-anda' ending of its name is native Anatolian, showing the city existed long before Greek colonisation. Ancient sources remark on the Arykandans' appetite for pleasure — and on their debts.

items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Tlos Ancient City, an ancient city in Muğla province. Its period: From the 2nd millennium BC; Lycian and Roman periods. Tlos, with its Bellerophon rock tomb and fortress atop a cliff, is one of the oldest and largest cities of Lycia.

items.text: One of the six founding cities of the Lycian League, Tlos saw more than 4,000 years of continuous habitation. Under Roman rule it became a major metropolis of the region and a leading member of the League. The fortress on the acropolis continued in use through the Byzantine and Ottoman periods.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Kibyra Ancient City, an ancient city in Burdur province. Its period: 2nd century BC – 6th century AD. Kibyra, known as the 'City of Gladiators', is famous for its world-renowned Medusa mosaic in the odeon and its gladiator school.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Kibyra Ancient City, an ancient city in Burdur province. Its period: 2nd century BC, 6th century AD. Kibyra, known as the 'City of Gladiators', is famous for its world-renowned Medusa mosaic in the odeon and its gladiator school.

items.text: According to Strabo, Kibyra was founded by Lydians who migrated to the Kabalis region and formed the 'Tetrapolis' league of four cities with its neighbours. Destroyed by an earthquake in AD 23, the city was rebuilt with the aid of Emperor Tiberius and, in gratitude, was renamed 'Caesarea Kibyra'. Under Rome it was a centre of justice and trade, famous for its gladiator school.

items.text: Did you know? The Medusa mosaic at Kibyra is the only known Medusa depiction made in the 'opus sectile' technique and is protected under cover for most of the year. The Medusa in the floor of the odeon is worked in cut coloured marble, opus sectile, and is among the best-preserved of its kind. Its rock-cut stadium seats ten thousand, its rows carved straight out of the hillside. The city was known for training gladiators and breeding horses; ancient sources praise the Kibyran cavalry.

items.text: The city was founded around 275 BC by the Seleucid dynasty to control Galatian raids. The city remained an important Christian pilgrimage centre into the Byzantine period.

items.text: Did you know? In Roman times the city's main street, the 'Cardo Maximus', led up to the Temple of Augustus to promote the imperial cult, and the community was known as the 'People of Augustus'. Saint Paul preached his first major sermon here; this is the city whose synagogue Acts names. One of the most important Latin copies of Augustus' Res Gestae, his own account of his deeds, was found here. It was founded as a colony settled with retired legionaries, and its street plan follows the logic of a military camp.

items.text: Founded beside Cape Anamur, Anemurium was an important port city on the Eastern Mediterranean trade route during the Roman and Byzantine periods. Largely abandoned after the 7th-century Arab raids, it was partly reoccupied in the 12th century under the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia.

items.text: Did you know? Anemurium lies right beside Cape Anamur, the southernmost point of Asia Minor, only 64 km from Cyprus. It stands on the southernmost point of Anatolia; on a clear day the coast of Cyprus is visible sixty kilometres away. With over three hundred monumental tombs it has one of the largest necropolises of the ancient world, most of them two-storeyed and vaulted. With two bath complexes, two theatres and mosaic-floored churches, the city lies as it was left, sloping to the sea.

items.text: Did you know? The city takes its name, meaning 'tall tower', from the high tower beside the Temple of Zeus Olbios, a tower depicted on the city's ancient coins. The Temple of Zeus Olbios is among the earliest Corinthian temples in Anatolia, raised not long after the order itself was devised. The city was ruled by the Teucrids, a dynasty of priest-kings — a rare arrangement in which priesthood and rule sat in the same person. The twenty-two-metre Hellenistic tower that gives the village its name still stands: 'Uzuncaburç' means 'tall tower'.

items.text: Did you know? The Karatepe bilingual inscription carries the same text in Phoenician and Hieroglyphic Luwian and, like a 'Rosetta Stone', was pivotal in deciphering Anatolian hieroglyphs. The bilingual inscription here, Phoenician alphabet beside Luwian hieroglyphs, was the key that unlocked Luwian hieroglyphic: Anatolia's Rosetta Stone. The reliefs in King Azatiwataş's fortress were never removed; a visitor sees them where the king set them. Halet Çambel, who led the excavation, had the surroundings declared a national park — choosing to protect the works in place rather than move them to a museum.

items.text: Brought under Roman control in the 1st century BC, the city gained the title of metropolis under Septimius Severus. Settled through Byzantine, Arab, Armenian and Mamluk periods, it was abandoned after being taken by the Mamluks in 1375.

items.text: Did you know? Anavarza is known as the birthplace of the famous physician Dioscorides, and excavations since 2013 have revealed the world's first known double-lane colonnaded road. The city sits at the foot of a vast sheer rock; the castle is on top and the city on the plain. Its colonnaded street and triumphal arch survive, and the mosaics from its villas are among the finest in the region. Dioscorides, author of De Materia Medica — Europe's standard pharmacology text for centuries — came from here.

items.text: Did you know? The inscription on the statue of King Idrimi is one of the most important documents of the ancient Near East — an autobiography written in cuneiform in the first person. King Idrimi had his life story carved onto his own statue in 104 lines — losing his throne, fleeing, and returning. The statue is now in the British Museum. Frescoes painted in the technique of the Minoan palaces of Crete were found on the palace walls: some of the most concrete evidence of the link between the Aegean and the eastern Mediterranean. The cuneiform archive of King Niqmepa records how a small Bronze Age kingdom kept its footing between great powers.

items.text: Biliyor muydunuz? Tünelin tamamlanması yaklaşık yüz yıl sürdü; girişteki yazıtta işi başlatan Vespasianus ile bitiren Titus'un adları birlikte geçer. Tünel 1380 metre uzunluğunda, yer yer 7 metre yüksekliğinde ve tamamen elle, çekiç ve keskiyle oyulmuştur. Antik dünyanın bilinen en büyük su tahliye tünelidir. İki uçtan aynı anda kazılmaya başlandı ve ekipler dağın ortasında buluştu; birleşme noktasındaki hafif kayma bugün tünelin içinde çıplak gözle görülebiliyor. Tünelin çıkışındaki Beşikli Mağara, kayaya oyulmuş on iki mezar odasından oluşan bir Roma nekropolüdür.

Tünel 1380 metre uzunluğunda, yer yer 7 metre yüksekliğinde ve tamamen elle, çekiç ve keskiyle oyulmuştur. Antik dünyanın bilinen en büyük su tahliye tünelidir. İki uçtan aynı anda kazılmaya başlandı ve ekipler dağın ortasında buluştu; birleşme noktasındaki hafif kayma bugün tünelin içinde çıplak gözle görülebiliyor. items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Vespasian–Titus Tunnel, a monument in Hatay province. Its period: 1st century AD. A 1.3-kilometre Roman diversion tunnel, cut through solid rock by hand to keep floodwater out of the harbour of Seleucia Pieria.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Vespasian–Titus Tunnel, a monument in Hatay province. Its period: 1st century AD. A 1.3-kilometre Roman diversion tunnel, cut through solid rock by hand to keep floodwater out of the harbour of Seleucia Pieria.

items.text: Seleucia Pieria was the port of Antioch, and floodwater off the mountain behind it kept silting the harbour up. The answer, begun under Vespasian, was to cut clean through the mountain and throw the water into the sea beside the port. The tunnel was carved with hammer and chisel, without explosives; inscriptions record that Roman soldiers and convicts did the work.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the Tunnel mouth, the Channel and watercourse, the Beşikli Cave tombs and the Vespasian–Titus inscription.
items.speech: As you walk round, don't miss the Tunnel mouth, the Channel and watercourse, the Beşikli Cave tombs and the Vespasian–Titus inscription.

items.text: Did you know? The tunnel took roughly a century to finish, and the inscription at its mouth names both Vespasian, who began it, and Titus, who completed it. The tunnel runs 1,380 metres, stands up to seven metres high in places, and was cut entirely by hand with hammer and chisel — the largest known diversion tunnel of the ancient world. Digging began from both ends at once and the teams met inside the mountain; the slight misalignment where they joined can still be seen with the naked eye. The Beşikli Cave at the tunnel's outflow is a Roman necropolis of twelve rock-cut burial chambers.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Karain Cave, a cave in Antalya province. Its period: About 500,000 years ago. One of the oldest known human dwellings in Anatolia: a great karst cave used without a break from the Palaeolithic to the classical age.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Karain Cave, a cave in Antalya province. Its period: About 500,000 years ago. One of the oldest known human dwellings in Anatolia: a great karst cave used without a break from the Palaeolithic to the classical age.

items.text: The cave at the foot of Mount Katran was in use, without a break, for roughly half a million years. Its layers have yielded Neanderthal as well as Homo sapiens remains, hearths, and stone and bone tools. In the classical period its mouth became a sanctuary, with votive niches and inscriptions cut into the rock.

items.text: Did you know? It was the first Palaeolithic cave excavated in Türkiye, and the first evidence of Neanderthals in Anatolia came out of it. The cave's deposits are eleven metres deep and hold an unbroken sequence of half a million years of occupation — there is nothing else like it in Türkiye. The first Neanderthal remains found in Anatolia came from here, and traces of Homo sapiens occur in the same layers.

items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to İvriz Rock Relief, a monument in Konya province. Its period: 8th century BC. A Neo-Hittite relief cut into the rock above a spring: King Warpalawas stands before Tarhunzas, the storm god, holding ears of grain and a bunch of grapes.

items.text: Warpalawas, king of Tuwana, had himself and Tarhunzas, the god of plenty, carved into the rock above a spring in the eighth century BC. The relief is among the largest works of Neo-Hittite art: the god, shown nearly twice the king's height, holds a sheaf of grain and a bunch of grapes.

items.text: Did you know? The grain and grapes in the relief are among the earliest images of a god's bounty, and the same iconography reappears in the region's art centuries later. The grain and grapes in the god's hands are among the earliest known images of a deity holding the produce of farming.

items.text: In the last century of the Hittite Empire a monumental pool was built over a spring in dressed stone. Its north face stacks winged sun discs, gods and goddesses and mountain deities one above another, and the water is thought to have run into the pool through openings beneath the figures.

items.text: Did you know? It is the only monumental Hittite pool that still holds water: three thousand years on, the spring runs where it always did. The monument was built directly over a spring, and the water still runs: the pool designed three thousand years ago is full today. Monumental Hittite waterworks that survive can be counted on one hand, and Eflatunpınar is the most complete of them.

Tokalı Kilise'nin mavi rengi, o dönemde altından pahalı olan lapis lazuli taşından elde edilmişti.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Göreme Open Air Museum, a rock settlement in Nevşehir province. Its period: 10th–12th century AD. A cluster of monasteries and churches cut into the tuff; the frescoes of the Dark Church are among the best-preserved Byzantine paintings anywhere.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Göreme Open Air Museum, a rock settlement in Nevşehir province. Its period: 10th–12th century AD. A cluster of monasteries and churches cut into the tuff; the frescoes of the Dark Church are among the best-preserved Byzantine paintings anywhere.

items.text: Volcanic tuff is soft enough to dig with a pick and hardens once cut, which is why the Göreme valley became a landscape of monasteries from the tenth century on: churches, refectories and cells were hollowed out one by one. Some were painted on plaster, others straight onto the rock; the Dark Church kept its colours because it has so few windows.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the Dark Church, the Buckle Church, the Apple Church, the Snake Church and the Nunnery.
items.speech: As you walk round, don't miss the Dark Church, the Buckle Church, the Apple Church, the Snake Church and the Nunnery.

items.text: Did you know? The frescoes of the Dark Church emerged from a restoration that took ten years to lift the soot, and the intensity of their blue is unmatched in the Byzantine world. The Dark Church is named for its single small window: because so little light gets in, its frescoes are the most vividly coloured in Cappadocia. Most of the rock churches were carved with columns and arches that hold nothing up. Inside solid rock they are structurally pointless: they are there so the space would look like a real church. The blue of the Buckle Church was made from lapis lazuli — at the time, more expensive than gold.

items.text: Willkommen beim Audioguide für Freilichtmuseum Göreme in der Provinz Nevşehir. Epoche: 10.–12. Jahrhundert n. Chr. Eine Gruppe von Klöstern und Kirchen, in den Tuff gehauen; die Fresken der Dunklen Kirche gehören zu den am besten erhaltenen byzantinischen Malereien überhaupt.
items.speech: Willkommen beim Audioguide für Freilichtmuseum Göreme in der Provinz Nevşehir. Epoche: 10.–12. Jahrhundert nach Christus Eine Gruppe von Klöstern und Kirchen, in den Tuff gehauen; die Fresken der Dunklen Kirche gehören zu den am besten erhaltenen byzantinischen Malereien überhaupt.

items.text: Vulkanischer Tuff ist weich genug, um ihn mit der Spitzhacke abzutragen, und härtet aus, sobald er geschnitten ist; deshalb wurde das Tal von Göreme ab dem zehnten Jahrhundert zu einer Landschaft der Klöster: Kirchen, Refektorien und Zellen wurden eine nach der anderen ausgehöhlt. Manche wurden auf Putz bemalt, andere direkt auf den Fels; die Dunkle Kirche hat ihre Farben bewahrt, weil sie so wenige Fenster hat.

items.text: Wussten Sie schon? Die Fresken der Dunklen Kirche kamen bei einer Restaurierung zum Vorschein, die zehn Jahre dauerte, um den Ruß zu entfernen, und die Leuchtkraft ihres Blaus ist in der byzantinischen Welt unerreicht. Die Dunkle Kirche ist nach ihrem einzigen kleinen Fenster benannt: Weil so wenig Licht hereinfällt, sind ihre Fresken die farbenprächtigsten Kappadokiens. Die meisten Felskirchen wurden mit Säulen und Bögen gehauen, die nichts tragen. Im massiven Fels sind sie statisch sinnlos: Sie sind nur da, damit der Raum wie eine echte Kirche aussieht. Das Blau der Schnallenkirche wurde aus Lapislazuli gewonnen – damals teurer als Gold.

items.speech: Добро пожаловать в аудиогид: Музей под открытым небом Гёреме, провинция Невшехир. Период: X–XII века нашей эры Группа монастырей и церквей, высеченных в туфе; фрески Тёмной церкви, одни из наиболее сохранившихся византийских росписей в мире.

items.text: Вулканический туф достаточно мягок, чтобы копать его киркой, и твердеет после того, как его вырубят; вот почему долина Гёреме с десятого века превратилась в край монастырей: церкви, трапезные и кельи выдалбливали одну за другой. Одни расписывали по штукатурке, другие прямо по скале; Тёмная церковь сохранила свои краски, потому что в ней так мало окон.

items.text: А вы знали? Фрески Тёмной церкви открылись в ходе реставрации, на удаление копоти потребовалось десять лет, и насыщенность их синего цвета не имеет равных в византийском мире. Тёмная церковь названа так из-за единственного маленького окна: поскольку внутрь проникает так мало света, её фрески — самые яркие в Каппадокии. Большинство скальных церквей высечены с колоннами и арками, которые ничего не поддерживают. Внутри сплошной скалы они конструктивно бессмысленны: они нужны лишь для того, чтобы пространство выглядело как настоящая церковь. Синий цвет Церкви с пряжкой получали из лазурита — в то время он стоил дороже золота.

items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Derinkuyu Underground City, a rock settlement in Nevşehir province. Its period: 8th–7th century BC, extended under Byzantium. An underground city descending eight levels and some 60 metres, with stables, churches, wineries and ventilation shafts enough for thousands of people.

items.text: The underground city grew by sinking a vertical shaft into soft tuff and cutting rooms off it sideways. Eight levels can be walked, and it is thought to run deeper. Each level could be sealed from the inside with round stone doors weighing tonnes, and the 55-metre ventilation shaft doubled as a well.

items.text: Did you know? The city came to light by accident in 1963, when a householder knocked through a wall and found a room behind it — and behind that, a whole underground city. The city was found by accident during home repairs in 1963: the man knocking through a wall stopped when an unknown room appeared behind it. The round stone doors between levels weigh over a tonne each and were designed to be opened only from the inside. The 55-metre ventilation shaft also served as a well.

items.text: Did you know? A nine-kilometre tunnel is said to link Kaymaklı to Derinkuyu. The claim is unproven — but the galleries between the two have never been fully mapped. The village above still stands on these tunnels, and its people still use parts of them for storage.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Zelve Open Air Museum, a rock settlement in Nevşehir province. Its period: 9th century AD – 1952. A rock settlement spread over three valleys, lived in without a break until 1952, when the danger of collapse emptied it.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Zelve Open Air Museum, a rock settlement in Nevşehir province. Its period: 9th century AD, 1952. A rock settlement spread over three valleys, lived in without a break until 1952, when the danger of collapse emptied it.

items.text: Spread over three valleys, Zelve was one of the places where Cappadocia's Christian and Muslim inhabitants lived side by side in the same rock: rock-cut churches in one valley, a rock-cut mosque in another. When the cliffs began to crack and fall in the 1950s the village was evacuated to New Zelve, two kilometres away.

items.text: Did you know? Zelve is one of the few Cappadocian settlements whose abandonment has an exact date: the village was cleared in 1952, so some of the people who lived in it are still alive. The village was evacuated in 1952 because the rock was starting to collapse — one of the few Cappadocian settlements with an exact date of abandonment.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Ihlara Valley, a rock settlement in Aksaray province. Its period: 9th–11th century AD. A canyon cut 100 metres deep by the Melendiz river, its walls honeycombed with frescoed rock churches.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Ihlara Valley, a rock settlement in Aksaray province. Its period: 9th–11th century AD. A canyon cut 100 metres deep by the Melendiz river, its walls honeycombed with frescoed rock churches.

items.text: The Melendiz river cut a fourteen-kilometre gorge a hundred metres deep into the volcanic plateau. More than a hundred churches and chapels were carved into its walls in the Byzantine period. Their frescoes fall into two styles — the local Cappadocian manner, with eastern influence, and the court style of Constantinople — standing side by side in one valley.

items.text: Did you know? More than three hundred steps lead down into the gorge, whose floor stays markedly cooler than the plateau in summer — one reason monastic life favoured it. The valley runs fourteen kilometres and reaches a hundred metres deep, with more than a hundred churches and chapels cut into its walls. The frescoes hold two worlds together: the local Cappadocian manner shows eastern influence, while other churches in the same valley are painted in the court style of Constantinople.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Sumela Monastery, a monastery and church in Trabzon province. Its period: 4th century AD. A monastery clinging to a 300-metre cliff above the Altındere valley, its rock church covered inside and out with frescoes.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Sumela Monastery, a monastery and church in Trabzon province. Its period: 4th century AD. A monastery clinging to a 300-metre cliff above the Altındere valley, its rock church covered inside and out with frescoes.

items.text: Founded in the fourth century, the monastery owes most of its present form to the thirteenth, under the Empire of Trebizond. It began as a natural cave turned into a church and grew over centuries into a five-storey complex. Ottoman sultans confirmed its privileges by decree; it was emptied in the population exchange of 1923.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the Rock Church, the Frescoed inner and outer walls, the Students' rooms, the Library and the Aqueduct.

items.text: Did you know? The outer wall of the rock church is frescoed too: the paintings were carried outside the building so that those who could not get in could follow the liturgy from without. The monastery is pressed against a cliff 300 metres above the valley floor, reached only by the path that climbs the slope. Ottoman sultans confirmed the monastery's privileges by decree — among them Selim I.

items.text: Willkommen beim Audioguide für Sumela-Kloster in der Provinz Trabzon. Epoche: 4. Jahrhundert n. Chr. Ein Kloster, das sich an eine 300 Meter hohe Felswand über dem Altındere-Tal klammert; seine Felskirche ist innen wie außen mit Fresken bedeckt.
items.speech: Willkommen beim Audioguide für Sumela-Kloster in der Provinz Trabzon. Epoche: 4. Jahrhundert nach Christus Ein Kloster, das sich an eine 300 Meter hohe Felswand über dem Altındere-Tal klammert; seine Felskirche ist innen wie außen mit Fresken bedeckt.

items.text: Im vierten Jahrhundert gegründet, verdankt das Kloster den größten Teil seiner heutigen Gestalt dem dreizehnten, unter dem Kaiserreich Trapezunt. Es begann als natürliche Höhle, die zur Kirche umgestaltet wurde, und wuchs über Jahrhunderte zu einer fünfstöckigen Anlage. Osmanische Sultane bestätigten seine Privilegien per Erlass; beim Bevölkerungsaustausch von 1923 wurde es geräumt.

items.text: Verpassen Sie beim Rundgang nicht: Felskirche, Mit Fresken bemalte Innen- und Außenwände, Schülerzimmer, Bibliothek und Aquädukt.

items.text: Wussten Sie schon? Auch die Außenwand der Felskirche ist mit Fresken bemalt: Die Malereien wurden nach außen fortgesetzt, damit diejenigen, die nicht hineinkamen, die Liturgie von draußen verfolgen konnten. Das Kloster schmiegt sich 300 Meter über dem Talgrund an eine Felswand und ist nur über den Pfad erreichbar, der den Hang hinaufführt. Osmanische Sultane bestätigten die Privilegien des Klosters per Erlass – unter ihnen Selim I.

items.text: Добро пожаловать в аудиогид: Монастырь Сумела, провинция Трабзон. Период: IV век н. э. Монастырь, прильнувший к 300-метровому утёсу над долиной Алтындере; его скальная церковь покрыта фресками снаружи и внутри.
items.speech: Добро пожаловать в аудиогид: Монастырь Сумела, провинция Трабзон. Период: IV век нашей эры Монастырь, прильнувший к 300-метровому утёсу над долиной Алтындере; его скальная церковь покрыта фресками снаружи и внутри.

items.text: Основанный в четвёртом веке, монастырь обязан большей частью своего нынешнего облика тринадцатому веку, эпохе Трапезундской империи. Он начинался как природная пещера, превращённая в церковь, и за века разросся в пятиэтажный комплекс. Османские султаны подтверждали его привилегии указами; в ходе обмена населением 1923 года он опустел.

items.text: А вы знали? Внешняя стена скальной церкви тоже расписана фресками: росписи вынесли наружу, чтобы те, кто не мог попасть внутрь, могли следить за литургией снаружи. Монастырь прижат к утёсу на высоте 300 метров над дном долины, и добраться до него можно только по тропе, взбирающейся по склону. Османские султаны подтверждали привилегии монастыря указами — среди них был Селим I.

items.text: Justinianus, 532'deki Nika ayaklanmasında yanan kilisenin yerine bugünkü yapıyı beş yıl on ay içinde yaptırdı. items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Hagia Sophia, a monastery and church in İstanbul province. Its period: AD 537. The domed basilica Justinian raised in five years, and for a thousand years the largest enclosed space in the world.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Hagia Sophia, a monastery and church in İstanbul province. Its period: AD 537. The domed basilica Justinian raised in five years, and for a thousand years the largest enclosed space in the world.

items.text: Justinian replaced the church burned in the Nika riots of 532 with the present building in five years and ten months. Its architects, Anthemius of Tralles and Isidore of Miletus, were specialists in geometry and mechanics; the pendentive solution carrying the dome was applied at this scale for the first time here. It became a mosque after 1453, a museum in 1935, and a mosque again in 2020.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the Main dome, the Mosaics, the Sultan's loge, the Marble doors and the Viking inscription.
items.speech: As you walk round, don't miss the Main dome, the Mosaics, the Sultan's loge, the Marble doors and the Viking inscription.

items.text: Did you know? On a marble parapet in the north gallery a runic inscription, probably scratched by one of the emperor's Varangian guards, reads as 'Halfdan carved this'. The dome stands 55 metres high and 31 metres across, and for a thousand years covered the largest enclosed space in the world. The ring of forty windows at the dome's base hides its weight and makes it seem to float; Procopius wrote that it looked as if it hung from heaven on a golden chain.

items.text: Justinian ersetzte die im Nika-Aufstand von 532 niedergebrannte Kirche in fünf Jahren und zehn Monaten durch den heutigen Bau. Seine Architekten, Anthemios von Tralleis und Isidor von Milet, waren Fachleute für Geometrie und Mechanik; die Pendentiflösung, die die Kuppel trägt, wurde hier zum ersten Mal in diesem Maßstab angewandt. Nach 1453 wurde sie eine Moschee, 1935 ein Museum und 2020 wieder eine Moschee.

items.text: Wussten Sie schon? Auf einer Marmorbrüstung in der Nordempore steht eine Runeninschrift, wahrscheinlich von einem der warägischen Gardisten des Kaisers eingeritzt, die sich als „Halfdan ritzte dies“ lesen lässt. Die Kuppel ist 55 Meter hoch und misst 31 Meter im Durchmesser, und tausend Jahre lang überspannte sie den größten geschlossenen Raum der Welt. Der Kranz aus vierzig Fenstern am Fuß der Kuppel verbirgt ihr Gewicht und lässt sie zu schweben scheinen; Prokop schrieb, sie sehe aus, als hinge sie an einer goldenen Kette vom Himmel.

items.text: Юстиниан заменил церковь, сгоревшую во время восстания «Ника» в 532 году, нынешним зданием за пять лет и десять месяцев. Его архитекторы, Анфимий из Тралл и Исидор из Милета, были специалистами в геометрии и механике; решение с парусами, несущими купол, впервые было применено здесь в таком масштабе. После 1453 года она стала мечетью, в 1935 году — музеем, а в 2020 году снова мечетью.

items.text: А вы знали? На мраморном парапете северной галереи есть руническая надпись, вероятно нацарапанная одним из варяжских гвардейцев императора; она читается как «Хальвдан вырезал это». Купол возвышается на 55 метров и имеет 31 метр в поперечнике, и тысячу лет он накрывал самое большое закрытое пространство в мире. items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Chora (Kariye), a monastery and church in İstanbul province. Its period: 11th–14th century AD. The masterpiece of late Byzantine mosaic and fresco, holding the most complete surviving programme of Palaiologan painting.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Chora (Kariye), a monastery and church in İstanbul province. Its period: 11th–14th century AD. The masterpiece of late Byzantine mosaic and fresco, holding the most complete surviving programme of Palaiologan painting.

items.text: The church of the Chora monastery was founded in the eleventh century; its mosaics and frescoes date from 1315–1321 and were paid for by the statesman and scholar Theodore Metochites. The programme narrates the lives of the Virgin and of Christ scene by scene, and the Anastasis in the side chapel is the best-known image in Byzantine painting.

The programme narrates the lives of the Virgin and of Christ scene by scene, and the Anastasis in the side chapel is the best-known image in Byzantine painting.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the Anastasis fresco, the Mosaics of the life of the Virgin, the Parekklesion and the Portrait of Metochites.
items.speech: As you walk round, don't miss the Anastasis fresco, the Mosaics of the life of the Virgin, the Parekklesion and the Portrait of Metochites.

items.text: Did you know? In the mosaic above the door Metochites is shown presenting Christ with a model of the building he paid for — a donor holding his own work, which is rare in Byzantine art. The Anastasis in the side chapel is the best-known image in Byzantine art: Christ hauls Adam and Eve out of their tombs by the wrists. The donor Theodore Metochites is shown above the door offering Christ a model of the building. He later lost his fortune and ended his life as a monk in this same monastery.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Selimiye Mosque, a mosque and complex in Edirne province. Its period: 1569–1575. The complex Sinan called his masterwork, its dome — resting on eight piers — wider than that of Hagia Sophia.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Selimiye Mosque, a mosque and complex in Edirne province. Its period: 1569 to 1575. The complex Sinan called his masterwork, its dome, resting on eight piers, wider than that of Hagia Sophia.

items.text: At Selimiye, built when he was past eighty, Sinan solved the problem of his working life: he pushed the piers carrying the dome to the edges of the space and won a single undivided volume inside. The dome, 31.25 metres across on eight piers, is wider than that of Hagia Sophia. The complex was designed together with its colleges, market row and timekeeper's house.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the Main dome, the Eight elephant-foot piers, the Muezzin's platform, the Tile panels and the Arasta market.
items.speech: As you walk round, don't miss the Main dome, the Eight elephant-foot piers, the Muezzin's platform, the Tile panels and the Arasta market.

items.text: Did you know? One marble column beneath the muezzin's platform carries an upside-down tulip. The story goes that the ground belonged to a tulip grower who resisted the endowment, and that the motif records his stubbornness. At 31.25 metres the dome is wider than that of Hagia Sophia — the goal Sinan worked towards his whole life, and reached after eighty. By pushing the piers into the walls Sinan won a single volume broken by no column: the mihrab is visible from every point in the mosque.

The story goes that the ground belonged to a tulip grower who resisted the endowment, and that the motif records his stubbornness. At 31.25 metres the dome is wider than that of Hagia Sophia, the goal Sinan worked towards his whole life, and reached after eighty. By pushing the piers into the walls Sinan won a single volume broken by no column: the mihrab is visible from every point in the mosque.

items.text: В Селимие, построенной, когда ему было уже за восемьдесят, Синан решил задачу всей своей творческой жизни: он отодвинул опоры, несущие купол, к краям пространства и получил внутри единый неразделённый объём. Купол диаметром 31,25 метра на восьми опорах шире купола Айя-Софии. Комплекс проектировался вместе с медресе, торговым рядом и домом хранителя времени.

items.text: А вы знали? Одна мраморная колонна под площадкой муэдзина несёт перевёрнутый тюльпан. Рассказывают, что земля принадлежала разводчику тюльпанов, который сопротивлялся передаче её в вакф, и этот мотив запечатлел его упрямство. Купол диаметром 31,25 метра шире купола Айя-Софии — это цель, к которой Синан стремился всю жизнь и которой достиг после восьмидесяти лет. Отодвинув опоры в стены, Синан получил единый объём, не прерываемый ни одной колонной: михраб виден из любой точки мечети.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Great Mosque and Hospital of Divriği, a mosque and complex in Sivas province. Its period: 1228–1229. A paired mosque and hospital whose carved portals have no equal in Anatolia — among the first sites in Türkiye inscribed by UNESCO.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Great Mosque and Hospital of Divriği, a mosque and complex in Sivas province. Its period: 1228 to 1229. A paired mosque and hospital whose carved portals have no equal in Anatolia, among the first sites in Türkiye inscribed by UNESCO.

items.text: In 1228–29 the Mengücekid ruler Ahmet Şah and his wife Turan Melek built a mosque and a hospital side by side. What makes the complex singular is its portals: the North (Paradise), West (Textile) and Hospital doorways carry carved ornament of a depth and volume unmatched in Islamic architecture. The hospital is held to have treated patients with music.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the Paradise Portal, the Textile Portal, the Hospital Portal, the Wooden minbar and the Hospital courtyard.
items.speech: As you walk round, don't miss the Paradise Portal, the Textile Portal, the Hospital Portal, the Wooden minbar and the Hospital courtyard.

items.text: Did you know? On certain days of the year the sun casts, across the carving of the west portal, the silhouette of a figure at prayer — an effect taken to be part of the design. The carving on the portals is so deep that the stone reads as woven cloth; no other ornament in Islamic architecture works at this scale or this freedom. The hospital is held to have treated patients with the sound of water and with music, and its courtyard acoustics to have been designed for it.

items.text: Sinan's mature work, the complex was built for Süleyman the Magnificent between 1550 and 1557. The mosque was designed not alone but as a piece of city, with four colleges, a medical school, a hospital, a soup kitchen, baths, a caravanserai and tombs. Hollow jars were set into the walls to serve the acoustics of the dome.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the Main dome, the Tombs of Süleyman and Hürrem, the Colleges, the Hospital and the Sinan's tomb.

items.text: Did you know? Soot from the mosque's lamps was drawn by the airflow into a single chamber, where it was collected and made into ink for calligraphers. Hollow jars were built into the walls for the acoustics: without amplification, the imam is heard everywhere in the mosque. Sinan placed his own tomb outside the complex, in a modest corner — facing not the mosque he built but the road to it.

items.text: Зрелое творение Синана, комплекс был построен для Сулеймана Великолепного между 1550 и 1557 годами. Мечеть проектировалась не сама по себе, а как часть города — с четырьмя медресе, медицинской школой, лечебницей, бесплатной кухней, банями, караван-сараем и гробницами. В стены были вмурованы полые сосуды, служащие акустике купола.

items.text: А вы знали? Копоть от светильников мечети потоком воздуха уносилась в одну-единственную камеру, где её собирали и делали из неё чернила для каллиграфов. Ради акустики в стены были встроены полые сосуды: без всякого усиления имама слышно в любой части мечети. Синан поместил собственную гробницу за пределами комплекса, в скромном углу, — обращённой не к построенной им мечети, а к дороге, ведущей к ней.

items.text: Fatih Sultan Mehmet, fetihten sonra sarayını Marmara, Boğaz ve Haliç'in birleştiği burna kurdurdu. Topkapı tek bir bina değil, dört avlu boyunca sıralanan köşkler, koğuşlar ve hizmet yapılarından oluşan bir yerleşkedir: dışarıdan içeriye doğru gidildikçe erişim daralır, dördüncü avlu yalnızca padişaha ve en yakınlarına açıktır. Saray 19. yüzyılda Dolmabahçe'ye taşınana kadar kullanıldı.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Topkapı Palace, a palace in İstanbul province. Its period: 1460s. A palace built as a compound rather than a building, growing around four courtyards, from which the Ottomans ruled for four centuries.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Topkapı Palace, a palace in İstanbul province. Its period: 1460s. A palace built as a compound rather than a building, growing around four courtyards, from which the Ottomans ruled for four centuries.

items.text: After the conquest Mehmed II set his palace on the point where the Marmara, the Bosphorus and the Golden Horn meet. Topkapı is not one building but a compound of kiosks, dormitories and service blocks strung along four courtyards, access narrowing as you go inward until the fourth court, open only to the sultan and his closest circle. It served until the court moved to Dolmabahçe in the nineteenth century.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the Gate of Salutation, the Harem, the Treasury, the Sacred Relics, the Baghdad Kiosk and the Palace kitchens.
items.speech: As you walk round, don't miss the Gate of Salutation, the Harem, the Treasury, the Sacred Relics, the Baghdad Kiosk and the Palace kitchens.

items.text: Did you know? The palace kitchens fed close to five thousand people a day; their chimneys were redesigned by Sinan, and the buildings now hold the collection of Chinese porcelain. The palace is a compound, not a building: four courtyards deep, each admitting fewer people, until the fourth is open to the sultan alone. The İznik tiles of the Harem carry the coral red that was lost in the sixteenth century and never reproduced.

items.speech: Willkommen beim Audioguide für Topkapı-Palast in der Provinz Istanbul. Epoche: 1460er-Jahre. Ein Palast, der nicht als einzelnes Gebäude, sondern als Anlage um vier Höfe herum wuchs und von dem aus die Osmanen vier Jahrhunderte lang regierten.

items.text: Nach der Eroberung errichtete Mehmed II. seinen Palast auf der Landspitze, an der Marmarameer, Bosporus und Goldenes Horn zusammentreffen. Topkapı ist kein einzelnes Gebäude, sondern eine Anlage aus Pavillons, Schlafsälen und Wirtschaftsbauten, aufgereiht an vier Höfen; der Zugang wird nach innen immer enger bis zum vierten Hof, der nur dem Sultan und seinem engsten Kreis offenstand. Er diente als Residenz, bis der Hof im neunzehnten Jahrhundert nach Dolmabahçe umzog.

items.text: Verpassen Sie beim Rundgang nicht: Tor der Begrüßung, Harem, Schatzkammer, Heilige Reliquien, Bagdad-Pavillon und Palastküchen.

items.text: Wussten Sie schon? Die Palastküchen versorgten täglich fast fünftausend Menschen; ihre Schornsteine wurden von Sinan umgestaltet, und heute beherbergen die Gebäude die Sammlung chinesischen Porzellans. Der Palast ist eine Anlage, kein Gebäude: vier Höfe tief, von denen jeder weniger Menschen einlässt, bis der vierte allein dem Sultan offensteht. Die İznik-Fliesen des Harems tragen das Korallenrot, das im sechzehnten Jahrhundert verloren ging und nie wieder hergestellt wurde.

items.text: Добро пожаловать в аудиогид: Дворец Топкапы, провинция Стамбул. Период: 1460-е годы. Дворец, построенный не как единое здание, а как комплекс, разраставшийся вокруг четырёх дворов; отсюда османы правили четыре столетия.
items.speech: Добро пожаловать в аудиогид: Дворец Топкапы, провинция Стамбул. Период: 1460-е годы. Дворец, построенный не как единое здание, а как комплекс, разраставшийся вокруг четырёх дворов; отсюда османы правили четыре столетия.

items.text: После завоевания Мехмед II поставил свой дворец на мысу, где сходятся Мраморное море, Босфор и Золотой Рог. Топкапы — это не одно здание, а комплекс павильонов, спален и служебных корпусов, нанизанных вдоль четырёх дворов; доступ сужается по мере продвижения вглубь вплоть до четвёртого двора, открытого лишь для султана и его ближайшего окружения. Дворец служил резиденцией, пока в девятнадцатом веке двор не переехал в Долмабахче.

items.text: А вы знали? Дворцовые кухни кормили почти пять тысяч человек в день; их дымоходы перестроил Синан, а сегодня в этих зданиях хранится коллекция китайского фарфора. Дворец — это комплекс, а не здание: четыре двора в глубину, каждый из которых пропускает всё меньше людей, пока четвёртый не оказывается открыт лишь для султана. Изникские изразцы гарема несут коралловый красный цвет, секрет которого был утрачен в шестнадцатом веке и так и не был воспроизведён.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to İshak Pasha Palace, a palace in Ağrı province. Its period: 1685–1784. A palace on the slope above the Silk Road at Doğubayazıt, fusing Seljuk, Ottoman, Georgian and Armenian architecture in one building.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to İshak Pasha Palace, a palace in Ağrı province. Its period: 1685 to 1784. A palace on the slope above the Silk Road at Doğubayazıt, fusing Seljuk, Ottoman, Georgian and Armenian architecture in one building.

items.text: Begun in 1685 on the rock above the Doğubayazıt pass of the Silk Road, it took about a century to finish. The palace gathers mosque, tomb, harem, public quarters, council hall, prison and baths inside a single walled island of building. Its stonework carries Seljuk, Ottoman, Georgian and Armenian traditions together, and it is held to have had a central heating system.

items.text: Did you know? The palace's gilded door leaves were removed to Russia in 1917 and are displayed today in a museum in Moscow. The palace had central heating and a drainage system — no other residence in eighteenth-century Anatolia is known to have had either. Seljuk, Ottoman, Georgian and Armenian stonework stand side by side on the same façade — a rare case in which no one style takes over.

items.text: Fatih Sultan Mehmet, İstanbul kuşatmasından önce Boğaz'ın en dar noktasında, Anadolu Hisarı'nın tam karşısında bir kale yaptırdı. İnşaat 1452 yazında dört ay sürdü; üç büyük kulenin her biri bir vezirin sorumluluğuna verildi ve kuleler onların adıyla anılır. Kaleye yerleştirilen toplar Boğaz'dan geçen gemileri durdurabiliyordu.

items.text: Before the siege of Constantinople, Mehmed II built a fortress at the narrowest point of the Bosphorus, directly opposite Anadolu Hisarı. Construction took four months in the summer of 1452; each of the three great towers was assigned to a vizier and still carries his name. The guns mounted here could stop any ship in the strait.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Diyarbakır Fortress and Hevsel Gardens, a castle and walls in Diyarbakır province. Its period: 4th century AD. Five point eight kilometres of basalt wall, reckoned the longest unbroken defensive circuit after the Great Wall, wrapping the Hevsel Gardens on the Tigris.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Diyarbakır Fortress and Hevsel Gardens, a castle and walls in Diyarbakır province. Its period: 4th century AD. Five point eight kilometres of basalt wall, reckoned the longest unbroken defensive circuit after the Great Wall, wrapping the Hevsel Gardens on the Tigris.

items.text: The walls took their present form under Rome in the fourth century AD and were repaired and extended by Byzantines, Marwanids, Artuqids, Aq Qoyunlu and Ottomans. Built of black basalt, the circuit runs 5.8 kilometres with 82 towers and four main gates. The inscriptions and animal reliefs on those towers form a stone archive in which every dynasty that held the city left its signature.

items.text: Did you know? The Hevsel Gardens below the walls have been farmed without a break for eight thousand years. They fed the city, and UNESCO inscribed them together with the walls as a single whole. Its 5.8 kilometres of basalt are reckoned the longest unbroken defensive circuit in the world after the Great Wall. The inscriptions on its towers carry the signature of every dynasty that held the city, from Rome to the Ottomans: the wall is an archive of power written in stone.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Safranbolu, a historic town in Karabük province. Its period: 17th–19th century. A town where a thousand registered Ottoman houses still stand, preserving almost intact the fabric of a caravan-road trading centre.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Safranbolu, a historic town in Karabük province. Its period: 17th–19th century. A town where a thousand registered Ottoman houses still stand, preserving almost intact the fabric of a caravan-road trading centre.

items.text: Safranbolu was a staging and trading town on the caravan road linking Istanbul to the Black Sea and inland Anatolia. Its wealth came from tanning and from the saffron trade it is named for. The town is really two settlements: Şehir, around the market, and Bağlar, the summer vineyard houses. Railways and highways passed it by, which is why its fabric survived.

items.text: Did you know? Most of the houses still have their revolving cupboard between the family quarters and the guest rooms, through which food could be passed without either side seeing the other. More than a thousand registered Ottoman houses still stand. The railway and the highway both passed the town by, and that is what preserved it. The town is named for the saffron grown around it, once weighed against gold.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Cumalıkızık, a historic town in Bursa province. Its period: 14th century. A foundation village from the Ottomans' first century, lived in on the same plan for seven hundred years, cobbled lanes and overhanging houses intact.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Cumalıkızık, a historic town in Bursa province. Its period: 14th century. A foundation village from the Ottomans' first century, lived in on the same plan for seven hundred years, cobbled lanes and overhanging houses intact.

items.text: Cumalıkızık was one of the endowment villages that fed Bursa in the Ottomans' first century, and because its income was tied to a foundation it was never broken up. More than half of its roughly 270 houses still stand, their three storeys of timber-laced mudbrick almost meeting overhead across the lanes. The street pattern and plot divisions have not changed since the fourteenth century.

items.text: Did you know? The village was inscribed by UNESCO not on its own but together with Bursa's monuments, under the title 'Bursa and Cumalıkızık: the Birth of the Ottoman Empire'. Because its income was tied to a foundation, the village was never broken up: its street pattern and plot divisions are unchanged since the fourteenth century. More than half of its roughly 270 houses still stand and are still lived in: this is a working village, not a museum.

items.speech: Mardin Eski Kent sesli rehberine hoş geldiniz. Burası Mardin ilinde bir tarihi kent dokusu. Dönemi: 12 ile 19. yüzyıl. Mezopotamya ovasına bakan yamaca teraslar halinde kurulmuş kent; kalker taşı işçiliğiyle bezeli medreseler, camiler ve Süryani kiliseleri iç içe.

items.text: Mardin, Mezopotamya ovasına hâkim kalker bir sırtın güney yamacına teraslar halinde kurulmuştur. Her evin damı bir üstündekinin avlusu olacak biçimde dizilen yapı, kente kesintisiz bir manzara ve doğal havalandırma sağlar. Artuklu döneminde biçimlenen kent dokusunda cami, medrese, kilise ve manastır aynı sokakta yan yana durur; taş işçiliği bölgenin ayırt edici sanatıdır.

Artuklu döneminde biçimlenen kent dokusunda cami, medrese, kilise ve manastır aynı sokakta yan yana durur; taş işçiliği bölgenin ayırt edici sanatıdır.

Kent, her evin damı bir üstündeki evin avlusu olacak biçimde teraslanmıştır; bu düzen bütün kente kesintisiz bir ova manzarası verir. Cami, medrese, kilise ve manastır aynı sokakta yan yana durur; Süryani cemaatinin Deyrulzafaran Manastırı 1500 yıldır aynı yerdedir.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Old Mardin, a historic town in Mardin province. Its period: 12th–19th century. A city terraced down the slope above the Mesopotamian plain, its carved limestone madrasas, mosques and Syriac churches standing side by side.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Old Mardin, a historic town in Mardin province. Its period: 12th–19th century. A city terraced down the slope above the Mesopotamian plain, its carved limestone madrasas, mosques and Syriac churches standing side by side.

items.text: Mardin is terraced down the south face of a limestone ridge commanding the Mesopotamian plain, each house's roof serving as the courtyard of the one above, which gives the whole town an unbroken view and natural ventilation. In a fabric shaped under the Artuqids, mosque, madrasa, church and monastery stand on the same street, and carved stone is the region's distinctive art.

items.text: Did you know? The long pool in the courtyard of the Kasımiye Madrasa was designed to describe a human life: water rises from its source, rests in the basin, and flows away. The town is terraced so that each house's roof is the courtyard of the one above, which gives every house an unbroken view over the plain. Mosque, madrasa, church and monastery stand on the same street, and the Syriac monastery of Deyrulzafaran has been in the same place for 1,500 years.

items.text: I. Ahmed, Ayasofya'nın karşısındaki Bizans Büyük Sarayı'nın kalıntıları üzerine kendi camisini yaptırmaya karar verdiğinde henüz on dokuz yaşındaydı ve savaş ganimeti olmadan cami yaptıran ilk padişah oldu. Sedefkâr Mehmed Ağa yapıyı 1609-1617 arasında tamamladı. Altı minare kararı Mekke'deki Harem-i Şerif'le eşitlik iddiası sayılınca, Mekke'ye yedinci minare eklendi.

Altı minare, yapıldığı sırada yalnızca Mekke'deki Harem-i Şerif'te vardı; iddia tartışma yaratınca Mekke'ye bir minare daha eklendi. Cami hâlâ ibadete açıktır ve ziyaret saatleri namaz vakitlerine göre değişir; giriş ücretsizdir. Yapı, Bizans Büyük Sarayı'nın üzerine kuruldu; sarayın mozaik tabanı bugün caminin arkasındaki müzede yerinde durur.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Sultan Ahmed Mosque, a mosque and complex in İstanbul province. Its period: 1609–1617. Known for its six minarets and the twenty thousand İznik tiles lining its walls, the mosque was raised directly opposite Hagia Sophia, over the old Byzantine palace.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Sultan Ahmed Mosque, a mosque and complex in İstanbul province. Its period: 1609 to 1617. Known for its six minarets and the twenty thousand İznik tiles lining its walls, the mosque was raised directly opposite Hagia Sophia, over the old Byzantine palace.

items.text: Ahmed I was nineteen when he decided to build his mosque on the ruins of the Byzantine Great Palace facing Hagia Sophia, and he became the first sultan to raise one without the spoils of a victory to pay for it. Sedefkâr Mehmed Ağa completed it between 1609 and 1617. When its six minarets were read as a claim to equal the sanctuary at Mecca, a seventh was added there.
items.speech: Ahmed I was nineteen when he decided to build his mosque on the ruins of the Byzantine Great Palace facing Hagia Sophia, and he became the first sultan to raise one without the spoils of a victory to pay for it. Sedefkâr Mehmed Ağa completed it between 1609 and 1617. When its six minarets were read as a claim to equal the sanctuary at Mecca, a seventh was added there.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the Main dome and semi-domes, the Six minarets, the İznik tiles, the Imperial Lodge, the Tomb of Ahmed I and the Courtyard and fountain.
items.speech: As you walk round, don't miss the Main dome and semi-domes, the Six minarets, the İznik tiles, the Imperial Lodge, the Tomb of Ahmed I and the Courtyard and fountain.

items.text: Did you know? The tiles that make it the 'Blue Mosque' came from İznik, and the order was so large that it drove the workshops' prices past recovery — İznik tilemaking never regained its footing. Six minarets were, at the time, matched only by the sanctuary at Mecca; when the claim caused offence, a further minaret was added there. The mosque is still in use for prayer, so visiting hours shift with the prayer times. There is no entry charge. It was built over the Byzantine Great Palace, whose mosaic floor still lies in place in the museum behind it.

items.text: Willkommen beim Audioguide für Sultan-Ahmed-Moschee (Blaue Moschee) in der Provinz Istanbul. Epoche: 1609–1617. Bekannt für ihre sechs Minarette und die zwanzigtausend İznik-Fliesen an ihren Wänden, wurde die Moschee direkt gegenüber der Hagia Sophia über dem alten byzantinischen Palast errichtet.
items.speech: Willkommen beim Audioguide für Sultan-Ahmed-Moschee (Blaue Moschee) in der Provinz Istanbul. Epoche: 1609 bis 1617. Bekannt für ihre sechs Minarette und die zwanzigtausend İznik-Fliesen an ihren Wänden, wurde die Moschee direkt gegenüber der Hagia Sophia über dem alten byzantinischen Palast errichtet.

items.text: Ahmed I. war neunzehn, als er beschloss, seine Moschee auf den Ruinen des byzantinischen Großen Palastes gegenüber der Hagia Sophia zu bauen, und er wurde der erste Sultan, der eine Moschee errichtete, ohne sie mit der Beute eines Sieges zu bezahlen. Sedefkâr Mehmed Ağa vollendete sie zwischen 1609 und 1617. Als ihre sechs Minarette als Anspruch gedeutet wurden, dem Heiligtum in Mekka gleichzukommen, wurde dort ein siebtes hinzugefügt.

items.text: Wussten Sie schon? Die Fliesen, die sie zur „Blauen Moschee“ machen, kamen aus İznik, und der Auftrag war so groß, dass er die Preise der Werkstätten unwiederbringlich in die Höhe trieb – die Fliesenkunst von İznik kam nie wieder auf die Beine. Sechs Minarette besaß damals nur das Heiligtum in Mekka; als der Anspruch Anstoß erregte, wurde dort ein weiteres Minarett hinzugefügt. Die Moschee wird noch immer zum Gebet genutzt, daher richten sich die Besuchszeiten nach den Gebetszeiten. Der Eintritt ist frei. Sie wurde über dem byzantinischen Großen Palast erbaut, dessen Mosaikboden noch heute an Ort und Stelle im Museum hinter ihr liegt.

items.text: Добро пожаловать в аудиогид: Голубая мечеть (мечеть Султанахмет), провинция Стамбул. Период: 1609–1617. Известная своими шестью минаретами и двадцатью тысячами изникских изразцов на стенах, мечеть была возведена прямо напротив Айя-Софии, на месте старого византийского дворца.
items.speech: Добро пожаловать в аудиогид: Голубая мечеть (мечеть Султанахмет), провинция Стамбул. Период: 1609-1617. Известная своими шестью минаретами и двадцатью тысячами изникских изразцов на стенах, мечеть была возведена прямо напротив Айя-Софии, на месте старого византийского дворца.

items.text: Ахмеду I было девятнадцать лет, когда он решил построить свою мечеть на руинах Большого императорского дворца византийцев напротив Айя-Софии, и он стал первым султаном, возведшим мечеть без военной добычи, которая оплатила бы строительство. Седефкяр Мехмед-ага завершил её между 1609 и 1617 годами. Когда её шесть минаретов восприняли как притязание на равенство со святилищем в Мекке, там был добавлен седьмой.

items.text: А вы знали? Изразцы, сделавшие её «Голубой мечетью», привезли из Изника, и заказ был так велик, что безвозвратно взвинтил цены мастерских, — изникское изразцовое производство так и не оправилось. Шесть минаретов в то время были только у святилища в Мекке; когда это притязание вызвало недовольство, там добавили ещё один минарет. Мечеть по-прежнему используется для молитвы, поэтому часы посещения меняются в зависимости от времени намаза. Вход бесплатный. Она построена над Большим императорским дворцом византийцев, мозаичный пол которого до сих пор лежит на своём месте в музее позади мечети.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Great Mosque of Bursa, a mosque and complex in Bursa province. Its period: 1396–1400. The masterpiece of the multi-domed plan — twenty domes carried on twelve piers — with a fountain at its centre lit through an opening left where a dome would be.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Great Mosque of Bursa, a mosque and complex in Bursa province. Its period: 1396 to 1400. The masterpiece of the multi-domed plan, twenty domes carried on twelve piers, with a fountain at its centre lit through an opening left where a dome would be.

items.text: Bayezid I had promised twenty mosques if he won at Nicopolis; on his return he built one mosque with twenty domes instead. Finished in 1400, it was damaged when Timur took Bursa two years later and afterwards repaired. Its fountain stands beneath the opening left where one of the domes would have been.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the Twenty domes, the Ablution fountain, the Walnut minbar, the Calligraphic panels and the Two minarets.
items.speech: As you walk round, don't miss the Twenty domes, the Ablution fountain, the Walnut minbar, the Calligraphic panels and the Two minarets.

items.text: Did you know? The more than 190 calligraphic panels on its walls let the mosque be read as a museum of the art, most of them by nineteenth-century masters. The twenty domes stand in place of the twenty mosques Bayezid I had vowed for his victory at Nicopolis. The fountain at the centre sits under the opening left where a dome would be: with no courtyard, the interior does the courtyard's work.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Green Tomb, a tomb in Bursa province. Its period: 1421. The tomb of Mehmed I, its turquoise tiles picking it out from across Bursa, and its cenotaph carrying the richest tilework of the age.

items.text: Mehmed I, the sultan who brought the Ottomans out of the interregnum, died in 1421 and was buried on the slope of the complex he had built for himself in Bursa. His vizier Hacı İvaz Paşa oversaw the tomb and the Green Mosque opposite; the turquoise tiles that gave it its name were renewed after the earthquake of 1855.

items.text: Did you know? The tiles over the cenotaph were made in the coloured-glaze technique its masters brought from Tabriz, and their signatures can still be read. The turquoise tiling that gives the tomb its name was renewed after the earthquake of 1855; some of the original tiles survive inside. The cenotaph of Mehmed I is the most elaborate piece of Ottoman tilework surviving from the Bursa period.

items.text: Eşrefoğlu Süleyman Bey'in 1297-1299 arasında yaptırdığı cami, Anadolu'nun ahşap direkli camilerinin en büyüğü ve en iyi korunmuşudur. Kırk iki sedir sütun, düz bir ahşap tavanı yedi yüz yıldır taşır. 2023'te 'Anadolu'nun Ahşap Hipostil Camileri' başlığıyla UNESCO Dünya Mirası Listesi'ne alınan camilerden biridir.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Eşrefoğlu Mosque, a mosque and complex in Konya province. Its period: 1297–1299. Forty-two cedar columns carry a wooden ceiling still in place after seven centuries, and the snow well at its centre is left open so winter snow can keep the timber from drying out.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Eşrefoğlu Mosque, a mosque and complex in Konya province. Its period: 1297 to 1299. Forty-two cedar columns carry a wooden ceiling still in place after seven centuries, and the snow well at its centre is left open so winter snow can keep the timber from drying out.

items.text: Built between 1297 and 1299 for Eşrefoğlu Süleyman Bey, this is the largest and best preserved of Anatolia's wooden hypostyle mosques: forty-two cedar columns have carried its flat timber ceiling for seven centuries. In 2023 it became one of those inscribed as the Wooden Hypostyle Mosques of Medieval Anatolia.
items.speech: Built between 1297 and 1299 for Eşrefoğlu Süleyman Bey, this is the largest and best preserved of Anatolia's wooden hypostyle mosques: forty-two cedar columns have carried its flat timber ceiling for seven centuries. In 2023 it became one of those inscribed as the Wooden Hypostyle Mosques of Medieval Anatolia.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the Cedar columns, the Snow well, the Tiled mihrab, the Wooden minbar and the Portal.
items.speech: As you walk round, don't miss the Cedar columns, the Snow well, the Tiled mihrab, the Wooden minbar and the Portal.

items.text: Did you know? The snow well at its centre is engineering, not ornament: snow falling through the roof in winter melts and evaporates, keeping the air damp enough that the timber does not split. None of the forty-two cedar columns has ever been replaced: the same trees have carried the roof for seven centuries. In 2023 Anatolia's wooden hypostyle mosques entered the World Heritage List, and Eşrefoğlu is the largest of them.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Great Mosque of Diyarbakır, a mosque and complex in Diyarbakır province. Its period: Rebuilt 1091. One of Anatolia's oldest mosques, its two-storey courtyard front built from columns and capitals lifted straight out of the city's Roman buildings.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Great Mosque of Diyarbakır, a mosque and complex in Diyarbakır province. Its period: Rebuilt 1091. One of Anatolia's oldest mosques, its two-storey courtyard front built from columns and capitals lifted straight out of the city's Roman buildings.

items.text: The building stands where a Roman temple and then the church of Mar Toma had stood; when the city was taken in 639 part of the church became a mosque. Its present form comes from the rebuilding ordered in 1091 by the Seljuk sultan Melikşah. The two-storey courtyard front was assembled from columns and capitals lifted out of the city's Roman buildings.

items.text: Did you know? The sundial in the courtyard is associated with al-Jazari, the engineer and inventor who served the Artuqid court in the twelfth century. The columns and capitals of the courtyard front were taken from the city's Roman buildings and used again. The mosque forms a complex with the Mesudiye and Zinciriye madrasas, which share its courtyard.

items.text: I. Alâeddin Keykubad'ın 1229'da yaptırdığı han, Konya-Aksaray-Kayseri yolundaki kervanların gecelediği en büyük duraktı. items.text: Built in 1229 for Alâeddin Keykubad I, this was the largest stop for caravans on the Konya–Aksaray–Kayseri road. After a fire it was enlarged at the end of the thirteenth century to more than four thousand square metres. The pairing of an open summer court with a covered winter hall is the standard Seljuk plan.

items.text: Did you know? In a Seljuk han, lodging, food and the shoeing of animals were free for three days, paid for by the endowment that ran the building. The kiosk mosque in the middle of the court stands on four piers, so a loaded caravan could pass beneath it into the yard. The han is split between an open summer court and a covered winter hall — the Anatolian winter wrote the Seljuk plan.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Cendere Bridge, a bridge in Adıyaman province. Its period: Late 2nd century AD. A Roman bridge crossing the Cendere in a single arch, three of the four columns raised by the XVI Legion for Septimius Severus and his family still standing.

items.text: The bridge was built at the end of the second century AD by the XVI Legion together with the surrounding Commagenian cities, for the emperor Septimius Severus, his wife Julia Domna and their sons. Three of the four columns still stand; the fourth, Geta's, was taken down after he was murdered and his name struck from the record.

items.text: Did you know? The bridge has stood for eighteen centuries and carried vehicles until recently; traffic stopped only when a new bridge was built beside it. One of the bridge's four columns is missing: when Geta's name was struck from the record after his death, his column came down with it. The bridge sits on the road up to Mount Nemrut, so most Commagene itineraries cross it.

items.text: Built over the Batman river in 1147 under the Artuqids, its single arch spans more than thirty-eight metres. The width was a defence against the spring floods that carry snowmelt down the valley. Chambers in its flanks were set aside for travellers and caravans to spend the night.

The rooms in the bridge's flanks were built so that travellers could spend a winter night inside it.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Döner Kümbet, a tomb in Kayseri province. Its period: c. 1276. A twelve-sided tomb built for Şah Cihan Hatun, its conical cap and bands of tree-of-life, double-headed eagle and lion reliefs the emblem of Seljuk funerary architecture.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Döner Kümbet, a tomb in Kayseri province. Its period: around 1276. A twelve-sided tomb built for Şah Cihan Hatun, its conical cap and bands of tree-of-life, double-headed eagle and lion reliefs the emblem of Seljuk funerary architecture.

items.text: Built around 1276 for Şah Cihan Hatun, this is the best known of Kayseri's Seljuk tomb towers. Its twelve-sided body and conical cap take their name from the way the building seems to turn as you walk around it. The burial chamber beneath is separate from the prayer room inside the shaft.

items.text: Did you know? The double-headed eagle on its shaft was a Seljuk dynastic emblem, a device that would turn up centuries later on European coats of arms. The tomb does not turn: the name comes from the way the twelve-sided shaft seems to rotate as you walk around it. The animals facing each other across the tree-of-life relief continue a decorative tradition carried from Central Asia.

items.text: Completed in AD 373 under the emperor Valens, the aqueduct was the last link inside the city of the long line running from the springs of Thrace. items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Basilica Cistern, a cistern in İstanbul province. Its period: 6th century AD. An underground reservoir on 336 columns, holding the water of the palace quarter through a siege; two of them stand on reused Medusa heads, one upside down and one on its side.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Basilica Cistern, a cistern in İstanbul province. Its period: 6th century AD. An underground reservoir on 336 columns, holding the water of the palace quarter through a siege; two of them stand on reused Medusa heads, one upside down and one on its side.

items.text: Built by Justinian after the Nika revolt of 532, the cistern covers 138 by 65 metres and held close to eighty thousand cubic metres of water, fed from the Valens aqueduct and distributed to the Great Palace quarter. It was forgotten under the Ottomans and recorded again in the sixteenth century only because householders were lowering buckets through their cellar floors and pulling up fish.

items.text: Did you know? Two Medusa heads serve as column bases, one upside down and one on its side. Why they were set that way is unknown; the likeliest answer is that they were simply the right height. Its 336 columns were gathered from different buildings, so where the heights did not match, bases were raised and capitals turned over. The cistern had been forgotten under the Ottomans, and was recorded again in the sixteenth century only because people were pulling fish up through their cellar floors.

Ein unterirdischer Speicher auf 336 Säulen, der das Wasser des Palastviertels während einer Belagerung vorhielt; zwei der Säulen stehen auf wiederverwendeten Medusenhäuptern, eines kopfüber, eines auf der Seite liegend.
items.speech: Willkommen beim Audioguide für Yerebatan-Zisterne in der Provinz Istanbul. Epoche: 6. Jahrhundert nach Christus Ein unterirdischer Speicher auf 336 Säulen, der das Wasser des Palastviertels während einer Belagerung vorhielt; zwei der Säulen stehen auf wiederverwendeten Medusenhäuptern, eines kopfüber, eines auf der Seite liegend.

items.text: Von Justinian nach dem Nika-Aufstand von 532 erbaut, misst die Zisterne 138 mal 65 Meter und fasste fast achtzigtausend Kubikmeter Wasser, das über das Valens-Aquädukt zufloss und im Viertel des Großen Palastes verteilt wurde. Unter den Osmanen geriet sie in Vergessenheit und wurde im sechzehnten Jahrhundert nur deshalb wieder verzeichnet, weil Hausbewohner Eimer durch ihre Kellerböden hinabließen und Fische heraufzogen.

items.text: Wussten Sie schon? Zwei Medusenhäupter dienen als Säulenbasen, eines kopfüber, eines auf der Seite liegend. Warum sie so gesetzt wurden, ist unbekannt; die wahrscheinlichste Antwort ist, dass sie einfach die richtige Höhe hatten. Ihre 336 Säulen wurden aus verschiedenen Bauten zusammengetragen; wo die Höhen nicht passten, wurden deshalb Basen erhöht und Kapitelle umgedreht. Die Zisterne war unter den Osmanen in Vergessenheit geraten und wurde im sechzehnten Jahrhundert nur deshalb wieder verzeichnet, weil Menschen Fische durch ihre Kellerböden heraufzogen.

items.text: Построенная Юстинианом после восстания «Ника» 532 года, цистерна занимает площадь 138 на 65 метров и вмещала почти восемьдесят тысяч кубометров воды, поступавшей по акведуку Валента и распределявшейся по кварталу Большого дворца. При османах о ней забыли, и в шестнадцатом веке её снова описали лишь потому, что жители опускали вёдра сквозь полы своих подвалов и вытаскивали рыбу.

items.text: А вы знали? Две головы Медузы служат основаниями колонн: одна перевёрнута, другая лежит на боку. Почему их установили именно так, неизвестно; вероятнее всего, они просто подходили по высоте. Её 336 колонн были собраны из разных зданий, поэтому там, где высота не совпадала, основания приподнимали, а капители переворачивали. items.text: When Sultan Abdülmecid found Topkapı inadequate for the diplomacy of the age, he moved the court to a filled-in bay on the Bosphorus. Built by the Balyan family between 1843 and 1856, it holds 285 rooms, 46 halls and six hundred metres of quay frontage. In the Republic it became Atatürk's residence and workplace in İstanbul, and he died here on 10 November 1938.

items.text: Als Sultan Abdülmecid den Topkapı-Palast für die Diplomatie seiner Zeit unzureichend fand, verlegte er den Hof an eine aufgeschüttete Bucht am Bosporus. items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Galata Tower, a monument in İstanbul province. Its period: 1348. Raised by the Genoese at the highest point of their Galata walls, used for centuries as a fire watchtower, and known today for the view down over the Golden Horn.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Galata Tower, a monument in İstanbul province. Its period: 1348. Raised by the Genoese at the highest point of their Galata walls, used for centuries as a fire watchtower, and known today for the view down over the Golden Horn.

items.text: The Genoese, granted their colony at Galata by Byzantium, crowned its walls with this tower in 1348 and called it the Tower of Christ. Under the Ottomans it served as a prison, an observatory and a fire watchtower. Its cap changed several times after fires and earthquakes; the present cone dates from a twentieth-century restoration.
