items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the Conical cap, the Viewing gallery, the Remains of the Genoese walls and the Stone shaft.

items.text: Did you know? Evliya Çelebi's account of Hezârfen Ahmed Çelebi strapping on wings and gliding from this tower to Üsküdar is the tower's best known and least verifiable story. The Genoese raised the tower in 1348 at the highest point of their own walls and named it the Tower of Christ. Under the Ottomans it was a fire watchtower — in a city of timber, the alarm was raised from here.

items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Anıtkabir, a monument in Ankara province. Its period: 1944 to 1953. The mausoleum of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk. Its Lion Road climbing to the ceremonial court draws Hittite and Seljuk forms into a deliberately plain language of stone.

items.text: The international competition opened after Atatürk's death in 1938 was won by Emin Onat and Orhan Arda. Built between 1944 and 1953 on Rasattepe above Ankara, it reduces forms drawn from Hittite lions to Seljuk stonework into a deliberately plain monumental language. Atatürk was moved here on 10 November 1953.

items.text: Did you know? The stone of the ceremonial plaza was brought from every part of the country, and the twenty-four lions of the Lion Road are carved seated, in the Hittite manner. The monument stands on Rasattepe above Ankara, and the building work uncovered Phrygian tumuli beneath the hill. The twenty-four lions of the Lion Road are carved seated rather than standing, following Hittite sculptural practice.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Alanya Castle, a castle and walls in Antalya province. Its period: 13th century. A Seljuk fortress wrapping the peninsula in 6.5 kilometres of wall, with the shipyard and the Red Tower below it surviving from the years the city was a naval base.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Alanya Castle, a castle and walls in Antalya province. Its period: 13th century. A Seljuk fortress wrapping the peninsula in 6.5 kilometres of wall, with the shipyard and the Red Tower below it surviving from the years the city was a naval base.

items.text: When Alâeddin Keykubad I took the town in 1221 he made it the Seljuk state's winter seat on the Mediterranean. The 6.5 kilometres of wall around the peninsula went up with more than a hundred towers and hundreds of cisterns. The shipyard below and the Red Tower belong to the years the navy was built here.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the Red Tower, the Shipyard, the Inner citadel, the Süleymaniye Mosque and the Arsenal.
items.speech: As you walk round, don't miss the Red Tower, the Shipyard, the Inner citadel, the Süleymaniye Mosque and the Arsenal.

items.text: Did you know? The five-bay shipyard is the only one the Seljuks built on the Mediterranean coast, and it is still standing eight centuries on. The wall around the peninsula runs 6.5 kilometres and encloses hundreds of cisterns: under siege the castle collected its own water. The Red Tower was built to protect the Seljuk shipyard and is the best preserved tower of Anatolian Seljuk military architecture.

items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Maiden's Castle, a castle and walls in Mersin province. Its period: 12th century. A sea castle on an islet two hundred metres offshore, closing the harbour from one side while Korykos Castle on the mainland closed the other.

items.text: The island castle was raised in the twelfth century under Byzantium, and passed later to the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia and the Karamanids. A chain could be drawn between it and Korykos Castle on the shore to close the harbour mouth. Its name comes from the tale of a king's daughter shut up here to keep her from a prophesied snakebite.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Odunpazarı Houses, a historic town in Eskişehir province. Its period: 18th–19th century. The Ottoman quarter on the slope where Eskişehir began: timber houses corbelled out over narrow lanes, with the city's meerschaum carvers still working in them.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Odunpazarı Houses, a historic town in Eskişehir province. Its period: 18th–19th century. The Ottoman quarter on the slope where Eskişehir began: timber houses corbelled out over narrow lanes, with the city's meerschaum carvers still working in them.

items.text: The quarter on the slope where Eskişehir began takes its name from the firewood market held here. Its timber-framed houses of the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries corbel out over the lane, each upper floor wider than the one below. The meerschaum seams of the region also made it the centre of the pipe and carving workshops.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the Bow-fronted timber houses, the Kurşunlu Complex, the Meerschaum workshops and the Atlıhan.
items.speech: As you walk round, don't miss the Bow-fronted timber houses, the Kurşunlu Complex, the Meerschaum workshops and the Atlıhan.

items.text: Did you know? Meerschaum is mined in only a few places on earth and the finest comes from Eskişehir. It is carved while still soft from the ground and hardens as it dries. The upper floors are wider than the lower ones: the bays corbel out over the lane and win extra rooms from a narrow plot. The quarter houses the pipe and carving workshops fed by the Eskişehir seams, which produce the finest meerschaum in the world.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Mor Hananyo Monastery, a monastery and church in Mardin province. Its period: 493. Seat of the Syriac Orthodox patriarchate for six centuries; the vaulted room beneath it survives from a sun temple that stood here before the monastery.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Mor Hananyo Monastery, a monastery and church in Mardin province. Its period: 493. Seat of the Syriac Orthodox patriarchate for six centuries; the vaulted room beneath it survives from a sun temple that stood here before the monastery.

items.text: Founded in 493, the monastery was the seat of the Syriac Orthodox patriarchate from the twelfth century until 1932. Its name comes from the story that saffron was mixed into its mortar. The vaulted room beneath the buildings, its blocks laid without mortar, is far older than the monastery and belongs to the sun temple that stood here.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Soğanlı Valley, a rock settlement in Kayseri province. Its period: 9th–13th century. The quiet valley of Cappadocia: dozens of churches cut into its slopes, their frescoes standing — unlike Göreme's — mostly without a crowd in front of them.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Soğanlı Valley, a rock settlement in Kayseri province. Its period: 9th–13th century. The quiet valley of Cappadocia: dozens of churches cut into its slopes, their frescoes standing, unlike Göreme's, mostly without a crowd in front of them.

items.text: This valley in southern Cappadocia was a monastic district settled by Byzantine monks between the ninth and thirteenth centuries. The dozens of churches cut into its slopes repeat, in domed and cross-plan form, what Göreme offers — the difference being that their frescoes usually stand without anyone in front of them. The valley falls within the World Heritage inscription made with the Göreme National Park.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Museum of Anatolian Civilizations, a museum in Ankara province. Its period: Founded 1921. Housed in an Ottoman bedesten, it tells Anatolia from the Palaeolithic to Rome along a single route, and holds the world's fullest Hittite and Neo-Hittite collection.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Museum of Anatolian Civilizations, a museum in Ankara province. Its period: Founded 1921. Housed in an Ottoman bedesten, it tells Anatolia from the Palaeolithic to Rome along a single route, and holds the world's fullest Hittite and Neo-Hittite collection.

items.text: The museum was created by restoring and joining the fifteenth-century Mahmut Pasha bedesten and the Kurşunlu Han. What began with Atatürk's wish for a 'Hittite Museum' grew into a collection covering every period of Anatolia. The display is chronological, starting in the Palaeolithic and running through Çatalhöyük, Hittite, Phrygian and Urartian halls to Rome.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Istanbul Archaeological Museums, a museum in İstanbul province. Its period: Founded 1891. Türkiye's first museum, founded by Osman Hamdi Bey: the Alexander Sarcophagus, the Kadesh treaty tablet and the Tiled Kiosk share one garden.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Istanbul Archaeological Museums, a museum in İstanbul province. Its period: Founded 1891. Türkiye's first museum, founded by Osman Hamdi Bey: the Alexander Sarcophagus, the Kadesh treaty tablet and the Tiled Kiosk share one garden.

items.text: Opened by Osman Hamdi Bey in 1891, the museum was born alongside the regulations that stopped antiquities leaving the Ottoman Empire: what came out of the ground needed somewhere to stay. It has three parts today — the Archaeological Museum, the Museum of the Ancient Orient and the Tiled Kiosk — and the sarcophagi from the royal necropolis of Sidon are the core of the collection.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the Alexander Sarcophagus, the Sarcophagus of the Mourning Women, the Kadesh treaty tablet, the Ishtar Gate panels and the Tiled Kiosk.
items.speech: As you walk round, don't miss the Alexander Sarcophagus, the Sarcophagus of the Mourning Women, the Kadesh treaty tablet, the Ishtar Gate panels and the Tiled Kiosk.

items.text: Did you know? The Alexander Sarcophagus is misnamed: it was made not for Alexander but for Abdalonymus, king of Sidon in his time. Alexander appears only in the carving. items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Zeugma Mosaic Museum, a museum in Gaziantep province. Its period: Opened 2011. The largest mosaic museum in the world, showing the floors rescued from Zeugma before the Birecik dam flooded the city.

items.text: When the Birecik dam began filling in 2000 it was set to drown most of Zeugma. An international rescue excavation lifted the floor mosaics out of the villas. The museum lays them out following the plan of the rooms they came from, so that a visitor walks through the houses rather than across the mosaics.

items.text: Antioch was the third city of the Roman Empire, and floor mosaics were laid in the villas around it on an extraordinary scale. A museum was founded in 1948 for what the excavations of the 1930s had produced, and the collection moved to a new building in 2014. The mosaics show not only mythological scenes but daily life, dining tables and charms against the evil eye.

items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Troy Museum, a museum in Çanakkale province. Its period: Opened 2018. Designed as a cube half-sunk beside the mound, it lays out Troy's nine layers and traces what was carried away from the city.

items.text: Opened in 2018 a kilometre from the mound, the museum was designed as a rusted steel cube sunk into the ground, so that the building, like the excavation, is read from the bottom up. The display works through Troy's nine layers in order, and states plainly where the objects taken from the city — the Treasure of Priam included — are held today.

items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Mevlâna Museum, a museum in Konya province. Its period: 13th century. The tomb of Mevlâna Celâleddin Rumi and the Mevlevi lodge around it, its green-tiled dome the emblem of Konya.

items.text: The building stands on ground that had been the rose garden of the Seljuk palace, given to Mevlâna's father. When Mevlâna died in 1273 a tomb was raised over him, and in later centuries a semahane, dervish cells, kitchens and a fountain grew around it into a Mevlevi lodge. It opened as a museum in 1926.

items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Great Palace Mosaic Museum, a museum in İstanbul province. Its period: Opened 1953. The mosaic floor of the Byzantine Great Palace courtyard, kept where it was found and roofed over: scenes of hunting, herding and animals rather than of court life.

items.text: Excavations behind Sultanahmet in the late 1930s uncovered a vast mosaic floor paving the colonnaded court of the Byzantine Great Palace. It was not lifted and moved: it was roofed where it lay and opened as a museum. Dated to the early Byzantine period, it shows not court life but the countryside.

items.text: The museum was installed in 1984 in the vaulted halls of the Roman baths of Hierapolis. Its collection is the reliefs taken from the city's theatre, the sarcophagi lifted from its necropolis and the finds of the other Lycus valley cities — Laodicea and Colossae.
items.speech: The museum was installed in 1984 in the vaulted halls of the Roman baths of Hierapolis. Its collection is the reliefs taken from the city's theatre, the sarcophagi lifted from its necropolis and the finds of the other Lycus valley cities, Laodicea and Colossae.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the Theatre reliefs, the Sarcophagus hall, the Small finds and the The Roman bath building.

items.text: Did you know? The necropolis of Hierapolis is among the largest ancient cemeteries in Anatolia — over a thousand tombs along two kilometres — and most of the sarcophagi in the museum came out of it. The museum was installed in the vaulted halls of the city's Roman baths, so the building is part of the collection. The reliefs taken from the theatre's stage building are among the fullest Roman sequences describing the cult of Apollo and Artemis.

items.text: The museum's history is bound up with the looting of the Lydian tumuli around Uşak in the 1960s. The pieces taken out of the country came back in 1993, after a suit brought against the Metropolitan Museum in New York. The collection known as the Lydian Hoard has been shown here ever since.

items.speech: As you walk round, don't miss the The Lydian Hoard, the Winged sea-horse brooch, the Finds from the tumuli and the Coin collection.

items.text: Did you know? The winged sea-horse brooch, the emblem of the collection, was stolen a second time after its return and replaced with a fake; the original was later recovered. The Lydian Hoard was brought back from New York years after it was smuggled out, through a lawsuit.

items.text: The Roman agora baths of Side were repaired in the early 1960s and turned into the museum, which opened in 1962. Sculpture from the city's agora, theatre and temples stands in the bath halls, and the courtyard is a stone garden of sarcophagi and inscriptions.

items.text: In 2017 the museum moved into the restored halls of the Milli Mensucat textile mill, built at the start of the twentieth century, becoming one of the largest museum buildings in Türkiye. Alongside finds running from the mounds of the Çukurova to its Roman cities, it also displays the mill's own looms.

items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Mardin Museum, a museum in Mardin province. Its period: Opened 1995. In the 19th-century mansion of the Syriac patriarchate, laying out the region's layers from Assyria to the Artuqids through the finds of Girnavaz and Dara.

items.text: The museum opened in 1995 in the mansion built at the end of the nineteenth century for the Syriac Catholic patriarchate. Its collection lets the region be read in layers: the Assyrian levels of the Girnavaz mound near Nusaybin, the Byzantine buildings of Dara, and the Artuqid work of the city around it.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Van Museum, a museum in Van province. Its period: Founded 1972. One of the few museums anywhere with an Urartian collection of this depth: the bronze belts, helmets and cuneiform tablets from Çavuştepe, Ayanis and Toprakkale.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Van Museum, a museum in Van province. Its period: Founded 1972. One of the few museums anywhere with an Urartian collection of this depth: the bronze belts, helmets and cuneiform tablets from Çavuştepe, Ayanis and Toprakkale.

items.text: Founded in 1972, the museum gathers the excavations of the Urartian centres around Lake Van — Çavuştepe, Ayanis, Toprakkale. Its bronze belts, helmets, horse harness and cuneiform tablets make one of the fullest collections of Urartian metalwork anywhere. The group of stelae found at Hakkâri is also displayed here.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Trabzon Museum, a museum in Trabzon province. Its period: Opened 2001. The Kostaki mansion, its painted ceilings and joinery left in place, turned into a museum with the region's Roman and Byzantine finds on the floor below.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Trabzon Museum, a museum in Trabzon province. Its period: Opened 2001. The Kostaki mansion, its painted ceilings and joinery left in place, turned into a museum with the region's Roman and Byzantine finds on the floor below.

items.text: The house was built at the start of the twentieth century for the banker Kostaki Theophylaktos, passed later to the Nemlizade family, and served as Atatürk's residence in the city in 1924. Restored, it opened as a museum in 2001, its painted ceilings and joinery left in place, with the region's Roman and Byzantine finds on the floor below.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the The Kostaki mansion rooms, the Painted ceilings, the Roman and Byzantine finds and the Ethnography floor.
items.speech: As you walk round, don't miss the The Kostaki mansion rooms, the Painted ceilings, the Roman and Byzantine finds and the Ethnography floor.

items.text: Did you know? The rooms are as much on show as the collection: the painted decoration of their ceilings is among the best preserved of nineteenth-century Black Sea mansion work. The building was a banking family's mansion and became Atatürk's residence in Trabzon in 1924. The painted ceiling decoration was left in place, and the house is among the best examples of nineteenth-century Black Sea domestic architecture.

items.text: The madrasa built in 1251 for the Seljuk emir Celâleddin Karatay has served since the middle of the twentieth century as a museum of tiles. The blue, black and turquoise of its dome compose a night sky, reflected in the pool below. The weight of the collection is the figured tilework taken from the Kubadabad palace on the shore of Lake Beyşehir.

items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Miletus Museum, a museum in Aydın province. Its period: Opened 1973. Gathering the finds of Miletus, Didyma and Priene, it lays out in one hall what a city whose four harbours silted up managed to leave behind.

items.text: The museum stands at the entrance to the Miletus site, beside the excavation house. Its collection covers Didyma and Priene as well as Miletus — and because the harbours of all three silted up under the Meander, the finds are now displayed kilometres inland.
items.speech: The museum stands at the entrance to the Miletus site, beside the excavation house. Its collection covers Didyma and Priene as well as Miletus, and because the harbours of all three silted up under the Meander, the finds are now displayed kilometres inland.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the Archaic sculpture, the Roman portraits, the Finds from Didyma and the Byzantine-period works.
items.speech: As you walk round, don't miss the Archaic sculpture, the Roman portraits, the Finds from Didyma and the Byzantine-period works.

items.text: Did you know? Miletus was the home of Hippodamus, who devised the grid city plan — the layout the museum explains is still the one most of the world's cities use. The museum holds the finds of Didyma and Priene as well as Miletus — the harbours of all three were filled by silt from the Meander. Hippodamus, who devised the grid plan, was from Miletus, and the city was rebuilt to his design after the Persians destroyed it.

items.text: The museum was built at the edge of the site in 1979, when the excavations had produced more sculpture than the town could hold. The marble quarry was two kilometres away and the city's school of sculptors supplied the empire; the museum keeps their work where it was made.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Kütahya Tile Museum, a museum in Kütahya province. Its period: Opened 1999. Housed in the imaret of Yakup Bey II, it follows four centuries of the Kütahya workshops that carried Ottoman tilemaking on after İznik declined.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Kütahya Tile Museum, a museum in Kütahya province. Its period: Opened 1999. Housed in the imaret of Yakup Bey II, it follows four centuries of the Kütahya workshops that carried Ottoman tilemaking on after İznik declined.

items.text: The museum occupies the imaret built by Yakup Bey II in the fifteenth century. After the İznik workshops closed in the seventeenth, Kütahya became the centre of Ottoman tilemaking, carried on into the twentieth century in workshops where Armenian and Turkish masters worked side by side.

items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Kayseri Archaeology Museum, a museum in Kayseri province. Its period: Opened 1969. Holding the finds of the Kültepe-Kanesh excavation, including the cuneiform tablets and clay envelopes of the Assyrian merchants.

items.text: The core of the museum is the Kültepe-Kanesh excavation twenty kilometres north-east of the city: the seat of the karum founded by Assyrian merchants in the second millennium BC, which produced Anatolia's earliest written documents — trade contracts and promissory notes.
items.speech: The core of the museum is the Kültepe-Kanesh excavation twenty kilometres north-east of the city: the seat of the karum founded by Assyrian merchants in the second millennium BC, which produced Anatolia's earliest written documents, trade contracts and promissory notes.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the The Kültepe tablets, the Clay envelopes and seals, the Hittite works and the Roman sculpture.
items.speech: As you walk round, don't miss the The Kültepe tablets, the Clay envelopes and seals, the Hittite works and the Roman sculpture.

items.text: Did you know? The Kültepe tablets came out inside clay envelopes: a summary of the contract was written on the envelope, sealed, and broken open only if there was a dispute. The Kültepe-Kanesh tablets are Anatolia's earliest written documents, and every one of them is a trade record, a contract or a note of debt.

items.text: Opened in 1967, the museum gathers the Early Bronze Age cultures of eastern Anatolia. At its core is the black burnished pottery tradition named after the Karaz mound near Erzurum, which spread across a wide belt from the Caucasus to Iran.

items.text: Did you know? Karaz pottery was built by hand rather than thrown, then burnished with a pebble after firing — which is why it still shines like a mirror thousands of years on. The same pottery appears across a belt from the Caucasus to Iran, pointing to a wide network of movement in the Early Bronze Age.

items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Pera Museum, a museum in İstanbul province. Its period: Opened 2005. A private museum known for its Orientalist painting collection, and the home of Osman Hamdi Bey's 'The Tortoise Trainer'.

items.text: Founded by the Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation, the museum opened in 2005 in the Bristol Hotel building of 1893. At the centre of its collection are the works of European painters who depicted the Ottoman world between the seventeenth and twentieth centuries, together with the paintings of Osman Hamdi Bey.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Yarımburgaz Cave, a cave in İstanbul province. Its period: Lower Palaeolithic. One of Thrace's longest caves: its Lower Palaeolithic layers hold the oldest human traces around the Sea of Marmara, its upper ones a Byzantine church.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Yarımburgaz Cave, a cave in İstanbul province. Its period: Lower Palaeolithic. One of Thrace's longest caves: its Lower Palaeolithic layers hold the oldest human traces around the Sea of Marmara, its upper ones a Byzantine church.

items.text: Overlooking Lake Küçükçekmece, the two-storey cave runs more than a kilometre and is among the largest in Thrace. Stone tools and cave-bear bones in its Lower Palaeolithic layers record the oldest human presence around the Sea of Marmara; a church was cut into its upper levels in Byzantine times.

items.text: Did you know? The cave was used for years as a quarry and a mushroom farm, and part of its archaeological sequence was destroyed before it could be excavated. The cave's Lower Palaeolithic layers record the oldest human presence around the Sea of Marmara. A Byzantine church was cut into its upper levels: the same cave was used twice, hundreds of thousands of years apart.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Öküzini Cave, a cave in Antalya province. Its period: Upper Palaeolithic. Next door to Karain, the cave is one of the few places where the passage from the end of the ice age to the Neolithic is recorded in an unbroken sequence of layers.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Öküzini Cave, a cave in Antalya province. Its period: Upper Palaeolithic. Next door to Karain, the cave is one of the few places where the passage from the end of the ice age to the Neolithic is recorded in an unbroken sequence of layers.

items.text: A kilometre south of Karain, the cave's layers between 16,000 and 10,000 BC document the end of the ice age in Anatolia better than anywhere else. Turkish and French excavations traced step by step how hunter-gatherer groups changed their diet and their tools as the climate warmed.

items.speech: Mağlova Kemeri sesli rehberine hoş geldiniz. Burası İstanbul ilinde bir su kemeri. Dönemi: 1554 ile 1563. Mimar Sinan'ın Kırkçeşme su yolları için Alibey Deresi üzerine kurduğu iki katlı kemer; su mühendisliğiyle anıt mimarisini aynı yapıda birleştirir.

items.text: Kanuni Sultan Süleyman'ın İstanbul'a su getirmek için görevlendirdiği Mimar Sinan, Kırkçeşme sisteminin en zor noktasını Alibey Deresi'nin geçtiği vadide çözdü. İki katlı kemer 1563'teki büyük selde zarar gördü ve Sinan tarafından yeniden yapıldı. Bugün Alibey Barajı'nın suları kemerin ayaklarına kadar gelir.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Mağlova Aqueduct, an aqueduct in İstanbul province. Its period: 1554–1563. The two-tier aqueduct Sinan threw across the Alibey stream for the Kırkçeşme water system, joining hydraulic engineering to monumental architecture in one structure.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Mağlova Aqueduct, an aqueduct in İstanbul province. Its period: 1554 to 1563. The two-tier aqueduct Sinan threw across the Alibey stream for the Kırkçeşme water system, joining hydraulic engineering to monumental architecture in one structure.

items.text: Charged by Süleyman with bringing water to İstanbul, Sinan solved the hardest point of the Kırkçeşme system where the Alibey stream cuts its valley. The two-tier aqueduct was damaged in the great flood of 1563 and rebuilt by him. Today the Alibey reservoir reaches its piers.
items.speech: Charged by Süleyman with bringing water to İstanbul, Sinan solved the hardest point of the Kırkçeşme system where the Alibey stream cuts its valley. The two-tier aqueduct was damaged in the great flood of 1563 and rebuilt by him. Today the Alibey reservoir reaches its piers.

items.text: As you walk round, don't miss the Two tiers of arches, the The pointed cutwaters, the The Kırkçeşme conduit and the Flood relief openings.
items.speech: As you walk round, don't miss the Two tiers of arches, the The pointed cutwaters, the The Kırkçeşme conduit and the Flood relief openings.

items.text: Did you know? Sinan gave the piers a pointed section that splits the current — the detail that has carried the structure through four and a half centuries of floods. The aqueduct was damaged in the great flood of 1563 and rebuilt by Sinan himself.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Halime Hatun Tomb, a tomb in Van province. Its period: 1358. A twelve-sided tomb tower above Lake Van at Gevaş — the best preserved piece of Kara Koyunlu stonework and, for its geometric carving, the emblem of the district.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Halime Hatun Tomb, a tomb in Van province. Its period: 1358. A twelve-sided tomb tower above Lake Van at Gevaş, the best preserved piece of Kara Koyunlu stonework and, for its geometric carving, the emblem of the district.

items.text: The tomb was built in 1358 for Halime Hatun, daughter of the Kara Koyunlu lord Melik İzzeddin. It stands on a slope above Lake Van at Gevaş, in the middle of a cemetery of the same period. The geometric and vegetal carving on its twelve faces follows a different arrangement on each one.

items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Gümüşkesen Tomb, a tomb in Muğla province. Its period: 2nd century AD. A Roman tomb at Milas taken to be a scaled-down copy of the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus, its pyramid roof and colonnaded upper storey still standing.

items.text: The two-storey tomb at Milas was built in the second century AD: a burial chamber below, a colonnaded storey carrying a pyramid roof above. It is taken to be a scaled-down reading of the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus a hundred kilometres away — and since that building was stripped to its foundations, Gümüşkesen gives the clearest idea of the lost wonder.

items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Bridge of Justinian, a bridge in Sakarya province. Its period: AD 559 to 562. The 430-metre bridge Justinian threw over the Sakarya. The river later shifted its bed, so the bridge now stands largely on dry ground.

items.text: Justinian built the bridge between 559 and 562 to lift the road linking the capital to the eastern provinces above the floods of the Sakarya. Procopius describes it as a contemporary witness. The river shifted its bed in later centuries, so the 430-metre bridge now stands largely over dry ground.

items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Irgandı Bridge, a bridge in Bursa province. Its period: 1442. A bridge with a market built along it, one of four of the type still standing anywhere in the world, and still housing craftspeople today.

items.text: Built in 1442 by the Bursa merchant Hoca Muslihiddin, the bridge carried a market of thirty-two shops. Wrecked by the earthquake of 1855 and a fire, it was finally demolished and replaced in 1949 by a flat concrete crossing. Its original form was rebuilt in 2004 and the shops handed back to craftspeople.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Beylerbeyi Palace, a palace in İstanbul province. Its period: 1861–1865. The summer palace Sultan Abdülaziz built on the Asian shore of the Bosphorus, used to house visiting heads of state; Abdülhamid II died here under house arrest.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Beylerbeyi Palace, a palace in İstanbul province. Its period: 1861 to 1865. The summer palace Sultan Abdülaziz built on the Asian shore of the Bosphorus, used to house visiting heads of state; Abdülhamid II died here under house arrest.

items.text: Sultan Abdülaziz had Sarkis Balyan build this summer palace between 1861 and 1865 in place of a wooden kiosk. It was used to receive visiting heads of state — the Empress Eugénie of France and the Shah of Persia stayed here. After his deposition, Abdülhamid II spent his last six years in the palace under house arrest.

items.speech: Kubadabad Sarayı sesli rehberine hoş geldiniz. Burası Konya ilinde bir saray. Dönemi: 1226 ile 1237. Birinci Alâeddin Keykubad'ın Beyşehir Gölü kıyısına kurdurduğu saray kenti; duvarlarını kaplayan figürlü çiniler bugün Konya'daki Karatay Müzesi'nde.

items.text: I. Alâeddin Keykubad, Beyşehir Gölü'nün batı kıyısında kendisi için bir saray kenti kurdurdu. Yapı topluluğu büyük ve küçük saray, tersane, av köşkleri ve göldeki adada bir köşkten oluşuyordu. 1949'da başlayan kazılarda ortaya çıkan figürlü çiniler, Selçuklu sarayının nasıl bezendiğine dair bilinen en zengin kaynaktır.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Kubadabad Palace, a palace in Konya province. Its period: 1226–1237. The palace town Alâeddin Keykubad I raised on the shore of Lake Beyşehir; the figured tiles that lined its walls are now in the Karatay Museum in Konya.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Kubadabad Palace, a palace in Konya province. Its period: 1226 to 1237. The palace town Alâeddin Keykubad I raised on the shore of Lake Beyşehir; the figured tiles that lined its walls are now in the Karatay Museum in Konya.

items.text: Alâeddin Keykubad I had a palace town built for himself on the western shore of Lake Beyşehir: a great and a lesser palace, a boatyard, hunting lodges and a pavilion on an island in the lake. The figured tiles uncovered in excavations from 1949 are the richest source we have for how a Seljuk palace was decorated.

items.text: Bayezid I raised this fortress in 1394 at the narrowest point of the Bosphorus, at the mouth of the Göksu, while preparing to besiege Constantinople. Sixty years later Mehmed II built Rumeli Hisarı on the opposite shore, and every ship passing the strait was caught between the guns of the two castles.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Ankara Castle, a castle and walls in Ankara province. Its period: 7th century AD. The citadel wrapping the hill the city grew on, its walls built course by course from column drums and inscribed blocks stripped out of Roman buildings.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Ankara Castle, a castle and walls in Ankara province. Its period: 7th century AD. The citadel wrapping the hill the city grew on, its walls built course by course from column drums and inscribed blocks stripped out of Roman buildings.

items.text: The present walls went up in the seventh century, when Byzantium was building a defensive line against Arab raids. Most of the material was stripped from the city's Roman buildings: column drums, funerary stelae and inscribed blocks stand side by side in the masonry. It was repaired and kept in use under the Seljuks and Ottomans.

items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Mamure Castle, a castle and walls in Mersin province. Its period: 12th–15th century. Set right on the shore at Anamur, its thirty-nine towers and moat make it the largest and best preserved castle on the Mediterranean coast.

items.text: The castle was rebuilt by the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia over a Roman fort, then enlarged by the Karamanids and the Ottomans. With thirty-nine towers, a moat and three separate courtyards it is the largest castle on the Mediterranean coast, and the sea comes right up to the foot of its walls.

items.text: Fatih Sultan Mehmed, 1458'de Theodosius surlarının Altın Kapı bölümüne üç kule ekletti; var olan dört kuleyle birlikte yedi kuleli bir hisar oluştu. items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Yedikule Fortress, a castle and walls in İstanbul province. Its period: 1458. The seven-towered fortress Mehmed II grafted onto the Golden Gate of the Theodosian walls, used as treasury, arsenal and the state prison where envoys were held.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Yedikule Fortress, a castle and walls in İstanbul province. Its period: 1458. The seven-towered fortress Mehmed II grafted onto the Golden Gate of the Theodosian walls, used as treasury, arsenal and the state prison where envoys were held.

items.text: In 1458 Mehmed II added three towers to the Golden Gate section of the Theodosian walls; with the four already there, the result was a seven-towered fortress. It served first as treasury and arsenal, then became the state prison. Ambassadors of states going to war with the Ottomans were held here, and Osman II was killed in it in 1622.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Vazelon Monastery, a monastery and church in Trabzon province. Its period: 270. Older than Sümela, the monastery leans into the steep side of the Maçka valley; under the Empire of Trebizond it kept the land registers of the region.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Vazelon Monastery, a monastery and church in Trabzon province. Its period: 270. Older than Sümela, the monastery leans into the steep side of the Maçka valley; under the Empire of Trebizond it kept the land registers of the region.

items.text: The monastery was founded in 270, about a century before Sümela. Set into the steep side of the Maçka valley, it kept the land and tax registers of the region under the Empire of Trebizond — records that are among the most important sources for the medieval social history of the Black Sea. It was abandoned in 1923.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Beypazarı Houses, a historic town in Ankara province. Its period: 18th–19th century. The bow-fronted, whitewashed houses of a town on the Ankara branch of the Silk Road — one of the few Anatolian towns restored and kept whole rather than house by house.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Beypazarı Houses, a historic town in Ankara province. Its period: 18th–19th century. The bow-fronted, whitewashed houses of a town on the Ankara branch of the Silk Road, one of the few Anatolian towns restored and kept whole rather than house by house.

items.text: The town was a stop and market on the branch of the Silk Road that ran through Ankara. Its timber-framed, mud-brick-filled, whitewashed houses were built in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. A restoration programme from the 1990s preserved the streets as a whole — one of the few cases in Anatolia where the fabric rather than individual buildings was saved.

items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Şirince, a historic town in İzmir province. Its period: 19th century. A Greek village on the slope above Ephesus, its stone houses emptied by the 1923 exchange of populations and preserved rather than replaced.

items.text: The village was a Greek settlement on the slope above Ephesus, living by winemaking. The population exchange of 1923 emptied it and Turks from Salonica settled in its place. The two-storey whitewashed houses on stone footings and the two churches stayed where they were, and from the 1980s the village was listed as a fabric to be protected.

Selçuklu ve Osmanlı dönemlerinde kent bu surların içinde kaldı; dar sokaklara sıralanan cumbalı ahşap konaklar 18. ve 19. yüzyıla aittir.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Antalya Old Town, a historic town in Antalya province. Its period: From the 2nd century AD. The walled old town wrapped around the Roman harbour, where Hadrian's Gate, the Fluted Minaret and Ottoman mansions stand along the same narrow lanes.

items.text: Kaleiçi is the present name of the walled city that grew around the harbour of Roman Attaleia. The three-arched gate raised for the emperor Hadrian's visit in AD 130 is still one of its main entrances. The city stayed within these walls through Seljuk and Ottoman centuries, and the bow-fronted timber mansions along its lanes date from the eighteenth and nineteenth.

items.text: Did you know? The building beneath the Broken Minaret was in turn a Roman temple, a Byzantine church, a mosque, a church again and a mosque once more: the city's whole history is legible on one set of foundations. Hadrian's Gate was built for the emperor's visit in AD 130 and is still one of the main ways into the old town.

items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Alâeddin Mosque, Konya, a mosque and complex in Konya province. Its period: 1155 to 1221. The congregational mosque of the Anatolian Seljuk capital: a flat-roofed hall on forty-two reused columns, with the tombs of eight sultans beside it.

items.text: The mosque stands on the mound at the centre of Konya, beside what was the Seljuk palace. Building began in 1155 and finished in 1221 under Alâeddin Keykubad I, which is why its parts follow different plans. Forty-two reused columns carry a flat wooden ceiling. Two tombs in its courtyard hold eight Seljuk sultans.

items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Üç Şerefeli Mosque, a mosque and complex in Edirne province. Its period: 1437 to 1447. The turning point of Ottoman architecture: the first attempt at a central dome on this scale, with each of its four minarets built to a different design.

items.text: The mosque Murad II built at Edirne between 1437 and 1447 is the turning point of Ottoman architecture: for the first time a central dome twenty-four metres across was set over the prayer hall on a six-support system. Each of its four minarets is a different height with different shaft decoration, and the mosque takes its name from the three balconies on the tallest.

items.text: The mosque in the village of Kasaba near Kastamonu was built in 1366 for Mahmut Bey of the Candarid dynasty. Its posts, beams and ceiling are joined entirely by interlocking joinery, without a single nail. The painted decoration on the ceiling and capitals is original and has never been renewed in six hundred and fifty years. It entered the World Heritage List in 2023.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Rüstem Pasha Mosque, a mosque and complex in İstanbul province. Its period: 1561–1563. Sinan's mosque raised over the Eminönü market, sheathed inside and out in İznik tiles at a density no other Ottoman building attempts.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Rüstem Pasha Mosque, a mosque and complex in İstanbul province. Its period: 1561 to 1563. Sinan's mosque raised over the Eminönü market, sheathed inside and out in İznik tiles at a density no other Ottoman building attempts.

items.text: Built by Sinan for Rüstem Pasha, Süleyman's grand vizier and son-in-law, the mosque sits above the Eminönü market on a platform formed by the shops beneath it — an arrangement that both funded the mosque and lifted it above the crowd. Its İznik tiling, inside and out, is denser than in any other Ottoman mosque.

items.text: The first structure on the islet off Üsküdar was raised in the fifth century BC by the Athenian commander Alcibiades, to tax ships passing the strait. Under Byzantium it anchored a chain drawn to the opposite shore; under the Ottomans it served as a quarantine station, lighthouse and watchtower. The building standing today dates from the eighteenth century.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Yesemek Quarry and Sculpture Workshop, a monument in Gaziantep province. Its period: 14th–8th century BC. The largest known open-air sculpture workshop of the Near East: more than three hundred half-finished lions, sphinxes and mountain gods lie across the slope where they were left.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Yesemek Quarry and Sculpture Workshop, a monument in Gaziantep province. Its period: 14th–8th century BC. The largest known open-air sculpture workshop of the Near East: more than three hundred half-finished lions, sphinxes and mountain gods lie across the slope where they were left.

items.text: The workshop opened in the fourteenth century BC under the Hittite empire and worked on into the eighth under the Neo-Hittite states. On the slope where the basalt was quarried, more than three hundred roughed-out sculptures lie where they were left: gate lions, sphinxes and mountain gods. Because the workshop was abandoned suddenly under Assyrian attack, the production process froze in place.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Obelisk of Theodosius, a monument in İstanbul province. Its period: 15th century BC. The granite obelisk Thutmose III raised at Karnak, moved to the Hippodrome in AD 390; the reliefs on its base show step by step how it was set upright.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Obelisk of Theodosius, a monument in İstanbul province. Its period: 15th century BC. The granite obelisk Thutmose III raised at Karnak, moved to the Hippodrome in AD 390; the reliefs on its base show step by step how it was set upright.

items.text: The obelisk was raised at Karnak by Pharaoh Thutmose III in the fifteenth century BC. Constantius had it brought to Alexandria in the fourth century AD, and Theodosius I moved it to Constantinople in 390 and set it up on the spine of the Hippodrome. It broke in transit, so about a third of its original height stands today.

items.speech: Özkonak Yeraltı Şehri sesli rehberine hoş geldiniz. Burası Nevşehir ilinde bir kaya yerleşimi. Dönemi: milattan sonra 4. yüzyıl. Avanos'un kuzeyindeki yeraltı şehri; kat aralarına açılmış borularla saldırganların üzerine kaynar yağ dökülebilen savunma düzeni Kapadokya'da tektir.

items.text: The underground city north of Avanos was found in 1972 when a farmer watering his field noticed the water disappearing. Four of its levels are open. What sets it apart from Cappadocia's other underground cities are the narrow pipes cut between the storeys: while attackers worked at the rolling stone door, hot liquid could be poured down on them.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Açıksaray, a rock settlement in Nevşehir province. Its period: 9th–11th century. The rock settlement near Gülşehir is made up of dwellings and stables rather than churches — the clearest picture in Cappadocia of how a provincial Byzantine landowner lived.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Açıksaray, a rock settlement in Nevşehir province. Its period: 9th–11th century. The rock settlement near Gülşehir is made up of dwellings and stables rather than churches, the clearest picture in Cappadocia of how a provincial Byzantine landowner lived.

items.text: Unlike Cappadocia's other sites, the rock settlement near Gülşehir is civil rather than religious. Its six separate complexes, dated to the ninth to eleventh centuries, hold dwellings, stables, kitchens and courtyards, each group arranged as the unit of a household or farm. There are few churches and they are small.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Yazılıkaya, a sanctuary in Çorum province. Its period: 13th century BC. The open-air sanctuary of Hattusa: along the walls of two rock chambers, a procession of more than sixty gods and goddesses is carved in relief.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Yazılıkaya, a sanctuary in Çorum province. Its period: 13th century BC. The open-air sanctuary of Hattusa: along the walls of two rock chambers, a procession of more than sixty gods and goddesses is carved in relief.

items.text: The rock clefts a kilometre and a half north-east of Hattusa formed the largest open-air sanctuary of the Hittite empire. On the walls of Chamber A two processions of gods walk towards each other and meet in the middle at the chief god and goddess; Chamber B is dedicated to king Tudhaliya IV. The reliefs were carved in the thirteenth century BC and are the Hittite roll of gods set into stone.

items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Smintheion, a sanctuary in Çanakkale province. Its period: 2nd century BC. The temple of Apollo Smintheus, centre of the cult named in the opening pages of the Iliad, its frieze carved with scenes from the epic itself.

items.text: The temple of Apollo Smintheus was built in the second century BC at Chryse in the Troad. The cult appears in the opening pages of the Iliad: it is from here that Apollo, answering the prayer of his priest Chryses, sends plague arrows into the Greek camp. The temple's frieze is carved with scenes from the Iliad — a rare case of an epic depicted at its own cult centre.

items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Yumuktepe, a mound in Mersin province. Its period: 7000 BC. With thirty-three settlement layers, one of the longest continuously inhabited mounds in the world; its Chalcolithic walls are among the earliest fortifications known.

items.text: The mound inside the city of Mersin, with thirty-three settlement layers reaching back to 7000 BC, is one of the longest continuously occupied places on earth. John Garstang dug it in the 1930s, Turkish and Italian teams from the 1990s. Its Chalcolithic wall and gate system is among the earliest fortifications known anywhere.

items.text: The mound on the Kahramanmaraş plain is the largest known settlement of the Halaf culture and dates to the sixth millennium BC. Excavations from the 1990s uncovered a mass burial called the Death Pit, in which the disarticulated bones of at least thirty-five people were found mixed with animal bone. What the deposit means is still argued over.

items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Sillyon, an ancient city in Antalya province. Its period: 5th century BC. On a flat-topped hill over the plain, one of the few Anatolian cities Alexander failed to take; the only substantial inscription in the Pamphylian dialect was found here.

items.text: On a flat-topped hill with sheer sides above the plain, the city was one of the four great cities of Pamphylia. Alexander besieged it in 333 BC and withdrew without taking it — one of the few places in Anatolia to end that way. Its Hellenistic tower and gate system largely survives. A landslip in 1969 carried away part of the hill along with the theatre and stadium.

items.text: The Pisidian city ringed by cliffs was founded in the third century BC and made a Roman colony by Augustus in 25 BC. In AD 278 a rebel named Lydius seized it, and the Romans heaped an enormous earth ramp against the town to break the siege. That ramp, and the siege camp with it, can still be traced on the ground.

items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Heracleia under Latmus, an ancient city in Muğla province. Its period: 4th century BC. On the shore of Lake Bafa among the boulders of the Beşparmak range, its Hellenistic walls running six kilometres around the slope.

items.text: The city was built among the granite boulders of the Beşparmak range on the shore of what was then a sea gulf. Silt from the Meander closed the gulf, the sea became Lake Bafa, and the harbour town was left inland. Its Hellenistic walls run six kilometres around the slope.

items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Rhodiapolis, an ancient city in Antalya province. Its period: 3rd century BC. The city of Opramoas, Lycia's greatest benefactor, whose tomb carries one of the longest records of public giving to survive from antiquity.

items.text: The small city in Lycia's mountainous interior was the home of the benefactor Opramoas, who in the second century AD sent aid to twenty-eight Lycian cities after earthquakes. The inscription cut into the walls of his tomb lists every one of those gifts.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Sanctuary of Apollo Lairbenos, a sanctuary in Denizli province. Its period: 2nd century BC. A temple on the slope above the Meander gorge, whose hundreds of confession inscriptions are the frankest record of popular religion in the Roman countryside.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Sanctuary of Apollo Lairbenos, a sanctuary in Denizli province. Its period: 2nd century BC. A temple on the slope above the Meander gorge, whose hundreds of confession inscriptions are the frankest record of popular religion in the Roman countryside.

items.text: The temple on the slope above the Meander gorge grew where a local Anatolian god was identified with Apollo. Hundreds of inscriptions from it record, plainly and by name, the offences of people the god had punished with illness or misfortune — the so-called confession inscriptions.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Panionium, a sanctuary in Aydın province. Its period: 7th century BC. The common sanctuary of the twelve Ionian cities and the seat of their league; Herodotus writes that resistance to Persia was debated here.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Panionium, a sanctuary in Aydın province. Its period: 7th century BC. The common sanctuary of the twelve Ionian cities and the seat of their league; Herodotus writes that resistance to Persia was debated here.

items.text: The common sanctuary of the twelve Ionian cities stood at the foot of Mount Mycale and was the meeting place of the Ionian League. Herodotus writes that what to do about Persia was debated here, and it was at these meetings that Thales proposed the cities unite under a single government.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Hacılar, a mound in Burdur province. Its period: 7000 BC. Excavated by James Mellaart in the 1950s, the mound produced the earliest and richest Neolithic painted pottery in Anatolia.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Hacılar, a mound in Burdur province. Its period: 7000 BC. Excavated by James Mellaart in the 1950s, the mound produced the earliest and richest Neolithic painted pottery in Anatolia.

items.text: The mound was excavated by James Mellaart between 1957 and 1960 and changed the understanding of the Anatolian Neolithic. Its painted pottery is among the earliest and most accomplished in the Near East. The fake Hacılar vessels that appeared on the market afterwards became a famous case of forgery in archaeology.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Column of Constantine, a monument in İstanbul province. Its period: AD 330. The porphyry column Constantine set at the centre of his forum when he founded the new capital: the city's oldest standing monument, in the same place for seventeen centuries.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Column of Constantine, a monument in İstanbul province. Its period: AD 330. The porphyry column Constantine set at the centre of his forum when he founded the new capital: the city's oldest standing monument, in the same place for seventeen centuries.

items.text: When Constantine founded his new capital in 330 he set this column of porphyry drums at the centre of his forum and placed his own statue on top. The statue came down in a storm in 1106. The shaft, blackened by fires, was strengthened with iron hoops, which is where its Turkish name comes from.

items.text: Mazı is one of Cappadocia's underground cities, with four separate entrances and much of it still unexcavated. Mangers for the stables, ovens and church spaces are cut into the rock, and rolling stone doors closed the passages when danger came.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Gümüşler Monastery, a rock settlement in Niğde province. Its period: 8th–12th century AD. The frescoes in this rock-cut monastery's church are among the best preserved in Cappadocia, and include the rare Byzantine image in which the Virgin is shown smiling.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Gümüşler Monastery, a rock settlement in Niğde province. Its period: 8th–12th century AD. The frescoes in this rock-cut monastery's church are among the best preserved in Cappadocia, and include the rare Byzantine image in which the Virgin is shown smiling.

items.text: The rock-cut monastery was in use between the eighth and twelfth centuries and was found by chance in 1963. In the frescoes of its main church the Virgin is shown smiling — an extremely rare choice in Byzantine iconography. Around a courtyard lie the church, burial chambers and a wine press.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Hagia Irene, a monastery and church in İstanbul province. Its period: 4th century AD. The city's first church, where the Second Ecumenical Council met in 381. It was never converted into a mosque, so the interior survives as it was.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Hagia Irene, a monastery and church in İstanbul province. Its period: 4th century AD. The city's first church, where the Second Ecumenical Council met in 381. It was never converted into a mosque, so the interior survives as it was.

items.text: The city's first church was built under Constantine, and the Second Ecumenical Council met in it in 381. It burned in the Nika revolt of 532 and Justinian rebuilt it. After the conquest it stood inside the first court of Topkapı Palace, so it was never converted into a mosque and its interior survives as it was.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Church of St Nicholas, a monastery and church in Antalya province. Its period: 6th century AD. At Demre, the church where Nicholas of Myra — the source of the Father Christmas story — was buried, its floor mosaics and part of its frescoes still in place.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Church of St Nicholas, a monastery and church in Antalya province. Its period: 6th century AD. At Demre, the church where Nicholas of Myra, the source of the Father Christmas story, was buried, its floor mosaics and part of its frescoes still in place.

items.text: The church was built over the tomb of Nicholas, bishop of Myra in the fourth century, and became a major place of pilgrimage under Byzantium. In 1087 Italian merchants carried most of the saint's bones off to Bari. The building standing today rests on eighth-century foundations and has been repaired several times.

items.text: The mosque of Mehmed I's complex at Bursa was finished in 1419. Tile masters from Tabriz carried out its decoration, and the tiling of the royal loge and the mihrab are reckoned the high point of early Ottoman ornament. It is the most developed example of the inverted-T Bursa plan.

items.text: The mosque below Ankara castle was built around 1290 and takes its name from the Roman lion relief set into its wall. Its wooden hypostyle plan is joined to a stucco mihrab that is among the most elaborate pieces of Seljuk plasterwork. The tomb of Ahi Şerafeddin adjoins it.

items.text: Built at the end of the thirteenth century, this is the largest open-courtyard madrasa in Anatolia and it rises two storeys. The two brick minarets framing its portal, and the tree-of-life and double-headed eagle carved on either side of the door, are reckoned the summit of Seljuk stonework. Who commissioned it is still argued over.

items.text: The madrasa built at Sivas in 1271 for the vizier Sahip Ata takes its name from the turquoise tiles sheathing its minarets. items.text: Built in 1217 for the Seljuk sultan Kaykaus I, the building was both hospital and medical school. When the sultan died of tuberculosis he was buried in the tiled tomb set in the south iwan of the courtyard. Running water and music were part of the treatment, and the pool at the centre of the court belonged to that regime.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Gevher Nesibe Hospital, a madrasa and hospital in Kayseri province. Its period: 1206. The first building to set a hospital and a medical school side by side: patients were treated while students took their lessons across the same courtyard.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Gevher Nesibe Hospital, a madrasa and hospital in Kayseri province. Its period: 1206. The first building to set a hospital and a medical school side by side: patients were treated while students took their lessons across the same courtyard.

items.text: In 1206 Kayhusraw I, acting on the will of his sister Gevher Nesibe, had a hospital and a medical school built side by side at Kayseri. Setting them adjoining brought the treatment of patients and the teaching of students into the same courtyard — the first known arrangement of its kind.

items.text: In 1877 Abdülhamid II moved the court from Dolmabahçe to Yıldız and governed from it for thirty-three years. items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Edirne Palace, a palace in Edirne province. Its period: 1450–1475. On the bank of the Tunca, this was the Ottomans' principal palace before Topkapı. It was destroyed when its magazine was blown up in 1878, and its foundations are being excavated now.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Edirne Palace, a palace in Edirne province. Its period: 1450 to 1475. On the bank of the Tunca, this was the Ottomans' principal palace before Topkapı. It was destroyed when its magazine was blown up in 1878, and its foundations are being excavated now.

items.text: Begun under Murad II and finished under Mehmed II, the palace on the bank of the Tunca was the Ottomans' principal seat before Topkapı — a wide compound of the Cihannüma pavilion, baths, kitchens and hunting lodges. Most of it came down in 1878 when its magazine was blown up during the Russian occupation, and its foundations are being uncovered by excavation.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Amasra Castle, a castle and walls in Bartın province. Its period: 9th century. Walls wrapping the headland between two bays and the island opposite; Genoese coats of arms still sit above its gates, and a neighbourhood lives inside it.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Amasra Castle, a castle and walls in Bartın province. Its period: 9th century. Walls wrapping the headland between two bays and the island opposite; Genoese coats of arms still sit above its gates, and a neighbourhood lives inside it.

items.text: The walls founded under Rome were renewed under Byzantium and then by the Genoese. They enclose the headland between two bays and the island of Boztepe opposite, with the bridge between them still in use. Genoese coats of arms sit above the gates, and a neighbourhood still lives inside the circuit.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Urfa Castle, a castle and walls in Şanlıurfa province. Its period: 9th century. The citadel looking down on the pool of Balıklıgöl, its two Corinthian columns and the Syriac inscription between them left from a monument raised by the kings of Edessa.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Urfa Castle, a castle and walls in Şanlıurfa province. Its period: 9th century. The citadel looking down on the pool of Balıklıgöl, its two Corinthian columns and the Syriac inscription between them left from a monument raised by the kings of Edessa.

items.text: The citadel above the pool of Balıklıgöl had been the city's defence since the kingdom of Edessa and took its present form in the ninth century. The two Corinthian columns at its eastern end, and the Syriac inscription between them, survive from a monument raised by king Manu of Edessa. Locally they are called the throne of Nimrod.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Erzurum Castle, a castle and walls in Erzurum province. Its period: 5th century AD. An inner citadel founded under Theodosius, with the Tepsi Minaret added by the Saltukids and still serving as the city's clock tower.

items.text: The inner citadel was founded under Theodosius in the fifth century and stayed at the centre of fifteen hundred years of the city's defence. The Tepsi Minaret, added under the Saltukids, was later put to use as a clock tower and has served that way ever since.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Silifke Castle, a castle and walls in Mersin province. Its period: 7th century. On the hill commanding the Göksu valley, the castle was the key to Cilicia through the crusades, its ditch cut straight into the rock.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Silifke Castle, a castle and walls in Mersin province. Its period: 7th century. On the hill commanding the Göksu valley, the castle was the key to Cilicia through the crusades, its ditch cut straight into the rock.

items.text: The castle on the hill commanding the Göksu valley was founded under Byzantium and counted through the crusades as the key to Cilicia. Its ditch is cut into the rock. It changed hands repeatedly between the Knights Templar and the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Zerzevan Castle, a castle and walls in Diyarbakır province. Its period: 3rd century AD. A Roman garrison town on the Persian frontier, whose rock-cut Mithraeum is the best preserved temple of that cult known in Anatolia.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Zerzevan Castle, a castle and walls in Diyarbakır province. Its period: 3rd century AD. A Roman garrison town on the Persian frontier, whose rock-cut Mithraeum is the best preserved temple of that cult known in Anatolia.

items.text: The Roman garrison town on the Persian frontier was founded in the third century AD and used into the seventh. Its wall, watchtower, church, cisterns and underground shelters largely survive. The rock-cut Mithraeum is the best preserved temple of that soldiers' cult known in Anatolia.
items.speech: The Roman garrison town on the Persian frontier was founded in the third century AD and used into the seventh. items.text: Did you know? The cult of Mithras spread through the Roman army and its temples were deliberately built dark and cave-like; the one at Zerzevan is that rule cut into rock. The rock-cut Mithraeum is the best preserved temple of that soldiers' cult known in Anatolia. The town was a Roman garrison on the Persian frontier and stayed in use for four centuries.

items.text: Welcome to the audio guide to Aspendos Aqueduct, an aqueduct in Antalya province. Its period: 2nd century AD. The aqueduct feeding the city crosses its valley on an inverted siphon worked by pressure towers — among the most ambitious pieces of Roman hydraulic engineering.
items.speech: Welcome to the audio guide to Aspendos Aqueduct, an aqueduct in Antalya province. Its period: 2nd century AD. The aqueduct feeding the city crosses its valley on an inverted siphon worked by pressure towers, among the most ambitious pieces of Roman hydraulic engineering.

items.text: The line feeding the city crosses its valley on an inverted siphon worked by pressure towers: the water drops, then is pushed up the far slope under pressure. The solution avoided the cost of holding an arcade high the whole way, and is among the most ambitious pieces of Roman hydraulic engineering.

items.text: The town in Bolu had been a staging point since the early Ottoman centuries. Its whitewashed timber-framed houses, stepping down the slope, date from the eighteenth and nineteenth. items.text: Son olarak, bu modelin bilmediği şeyler. Cephenin genişliği ve yüksekliği ölçülmüştür. Aralıkların düzeni — dört sütun çifti, aralarındaki üç kapı, üst kattaki üç pencere ve onların üzerindeki üçgen/yay alınlıklar — 1970-78'de yeniden dikilmiş cephenin fotoğraflarından çıkarılmıştır; iki katın 16 metreyi nasıl paylaştığı, sütun çapları ve heykellerin duruşu ise orantıdır, ölçü değil. Nişlerdeki dört erdem ve üst kattaki iki erkek figür kumaş kıvrımlarına kadar modellenmiştir ama Viyana'daki özgün heykellerin kopyası değildir; duruşları ve giysileri yorumdur. Avludaki bronz atlılar da Roma'daki Marcus Aurelius heykelinin oranlarıyla kurulmuştur. Başlıkların akant yaprakları ve volütleri modellenmiştir ama taştaki işçiliğin kopyası değildir; frizlerdeki yazıtlar ve bezeme modelde yoktur. **Renkler de ölçü değil, yorumdur:** Roma mermer cepheleri boyalıydı ve bugün Efes'te boya izi kalmamıştır — modeldeki kırmızı panolar, mavi-altın silmeler, ahşap kapılar, altın kafes pencereler ve merdivenin iki yanındaki bronz atlı heykeller yayımlanmış bir rekonstrüksiyon resminden alınmıştır, kazıdan değil. Salonun tavanı da yoktur: yapının iki katlı mı üç katlı mı olduğu tartışmalıdır.

items.text: Finally, what this model does not know. The façade's width and height are measured. The rhythm of the front — four pairs of columns, three doorways between them, three windows above and the triangular and segmental pediments over those — is read off photographs of the front re-erected in 1970-78; how the two orders divide the 16 metres, the column diameters and the poses of the statues are proportion rather than measurement. The four virtues in the niches and the two male figures above are modelled down to the folds of their dress, but they are not copies of the originals in Vienna; their poses and clothing are interpretation. The bronze horsemen in the court are likewise built on the proportions of the Marcus Aurelius in Rome. The acanthus and volutes of the capitals are modelled but are not a copy of the carving on the stone, and the inscriptions and the ornament of the friezes are absent. **The colour is interpretation, not measurement:** Roman marble fronts were painted, and no pigment survives at Ephesus — the red panels, the blue and gilded mouldings, the timber doors, the gilded window lattices and the bronze horsemen flanking the stairs are taken from a published reconstruction painting, not from the excavation. So is the hall's ceiling absent: whether the building had two storeys or three is disputed.

items.text: Zum Schluss: was dieses Modell nicht weiß. Breite und Höhe der Fassade sind gemessen. Der Rhythmus der Front – vier Säulenpaare, drei Türen dazwischen, drei Fenster darüber und die Dreiecks- und Segmentgiebel über diesen – ist an Fotografien der 1970–78 wiedererrichteten Front abgelesen; wie die beiden Ordnungen die 16 Meter unter sich aufteilen, die Säulendurchmesser und die Haltung der Statuen sind Proportion, nicht Messung. Die vier Tugenden in den Nischen und die beiden männlichen Figuren darüber sind bis in die Falten ihrer Gewänder modelliert, sind aber keine Kopien der Originale in Wien; Haltung und Kleidung sind Deutung. Auch die bronzenen Reiter im Hof sind nach den Proportionen des Mark Aurel in Rom gebaut. Akanthus und Voluten der Kapitelle sind modelliert, aber keine Kopie der Steinmetzarbeit; die Inschriften und der Schmuck der Friese fehlen. **Die Farbe ist Deutung, nicht Messung:** Römische Marmorfassaden waren bemalt, und in Ephesos sind keine Farbspuren erhalten – die roten Felder, die blauen und vergoldeten Profile, die hölzernen Türen, die vergoldeten Fenstergitter und die bronzenen Reiter zu beiden Seiten der Treppe stammen aus einem veröffentlichten Rekonstruktionsgemälde, nicht aus der Grabung. Ebenso fehlt die Decke des Saals: Ob der Bau zwei oder drei Geschosse hatte, ist umstritten.
items.speech: Zum Schluss: was dieses Modell nicht weiß. Breite und Höhe der Fassade sind gemessen. Der Rhythmus der Front, vier Säulenpaare, drei Türen dazwischen, drei Fenster darüber und die Dreiecks- und Segmentgiebel über diesen, ist an Fotografien der 1970 bis 1978 wiedererrichteten Front abgelesen; wie die beiden Ordnungen die 16 Meter unter sich aufteilen, die Säulendurchmesser und die Haltung der Statuen sind Proportion, nicht Messung. Die vier Tugenden in den Nischen und die beiden männlichen Figuren darüber sind bis in die Falten ihrer Gewänder modelliert, sind aber keine Kopien der Originale in Wien; Haltung und Kleidung sind Deutung. Auch die bronzenen Reiter im Hof sind nach den Proportionen des Mark Aurel in Rom gebaut. Ebenso fehlt die Decke des Saals: Ob der Bau zwei oder drei Geschosse hatte, ist umstritten.

items.text: И напоследок — чего эта модель не знает. Ширина и высота фасада измерены. Ритм фасада — четыре пары колонн, три дверных проёма между ними, три окна выше и треугольные и лучковые фронтоны над ними — считан с фотографий фасада, вновь возведённого в 1970–78 годах; то, как два ордера делят между собой 16 метров, диаметры колонн и позы статуй — это пропорция, а не измерение. Четыре добродетели в нишах и две мужские фигуры над ними смоделированы вплоть до складок одежды, но это не копии оригиналов, хранящихся в Вене; их позы и одеяния — интерпретация. Бронзовые всадники во дворе также построены по пропорциям статуи Марка Аврелия в Риме. Аканты и волюты капителей смоделированы, но не копируют резьбу по камню; надписей и орнамента фризов в модели нет. **Цвет — интерпретация, а не измерение:** римские мраморные фасады были расписаны, а в Эфесе следов краски не сохранилось — красные панели, синие и позолоченные профили, деревянные двери, позолоченные оконные решётки и бронзовые всадники по сторонам лестницы взяты с опубликованной реконструкционной картины, а не из раскопок. Нет и потолка зала: было ли здание двух- или трёхэтажным, остаётся спорным.

Modeldeki sıra sayısı ölçülmüş değil, türetilmiştir: 96 metrelik dış çap ile 23,9 metrelik orkestra arasındaki yamaç, 0,75 m basamak derinliği ve üstteki tonozlu galeri payıyla 40 sıraya bölünmüştür. items.text: Finally, what this model does not know. The row count in the model is derived, not measured: the slope between the 96 m outer diameter and the 23.9 m orchestra is divided into 40 rows at a tread of 0.75 m, allowing for the vaulted gallery on top. The arrangement of the stage wall — two storeys of aediculae, five doorways, the rows of square sockets left by its beams — is read off photographs of the building. The statuary of that front, its wooden roof and the awning are not modelled; the sloping wooden sounding-board over the stage was already lost in antiquity.

items.text: The Temple of Apollo at Didyma. 300 BC - 2nd century AD. One of the largest temples ever attempted: some 500 years in the building, and never finished. It never had a roof — behind the forest of columns lay an open court holding the oracle spring and the laurel tree.

items.text: Son olarak, bu modelin bilmediği şeyler. Yapının çapı için yayınlarda 20 ile 30 metre arasında değerler geçer; model 30 metreyi esas alır. Dikilitaşların yüzündeki hayvan kabartmaları çizilmemiştir: kazıda çıkan kabartmaların fotoğrafları yükseklik haritası olarak kullanılıp taşa oyulmuştur, yani derinlik gerçektir ve gölgesini kendi düşürür. Gerçek olmayan, hangi hayvanın hangi taşın neresinde durduğudur — fotoğraflar C Yapısı'nın taşlarından gelir, model ise D Yapısı'nı gösterir. Merkezdeki iki taşın kolları, elleri, kemeri ve peştamalı D Yapısı için belgelenmiştir ve alçak kabartma olarak modellenmiştir. Çemberin üstünün örtülü olup olmadığı bilinmiyor; model açık bırakır.

items.text: Finally, what this model does not know. Published diameters for the enclosure range from 20 to 30 metres; the model takes 30. The animals on the pillars are not drawn: photographs of the excavated reliefs are used as height maps and cut into the stone, so the depth is real and throws its own shadow. What is not real is which animal stood where on which pillar — the photographs come from the pillars of Enclosure C, while the model shows Enclosure D. The arms, hands, belt and loincloth of the two central stones are documented for D, and are modelled as the low relief they are. Whether the circle was roofed is unknown, and the model leaves it open.

items.text: Zum Schluss: was dieses Modell nicht weiß. Die veröffentlichten Durchmesser der Anlage reichen von 20 bis 30 Metern; das Modell nimmt 30 an. Die Tiere auf den Pfeilern sind nicht gezeichnet: Fotografien der ausgegrabenen Reliefs dienen als Höhenkarten und sind in den Stein geschnitten, sodass die Tiefe echt ist und ihren eigenen Schatten wirft. Nicht echt ist, welches Tier auf welchem Pfeiler wo stand – die Fotografien stammen von den Pfeilern der Anlage C, während das Modell Anlage D zeigt. Arme, Hände, Gürtel und Lendenschurz der beiden zentralen Steine sind für D belegt und als das flache Relief modelliert, das sie sind. Ob der Kreis überdacht war, ist unbekannt, und das Modell lässt es offen.

items.text: И напоследок — чего эта модель не знает. Опубликованные диаметры сооружения колеблются от 20 до 30 метров; в модели принято 30. Животные на столбах не нарисованы: фотографии раскопанных рельефов использованы как карты высот и вырезаны в камне, так что глубина настоящая и отбрасывает собственную тень. Ненастоящее здесь другое — какое животное где стояло и на каком столбе: фотографии сделаны со столбов сооружения C, а модель показывает сооружение D. Руки, кисти, пояс и набедренная повязка двух центральных камней задокументированы для D и смоделированы таким же низким рельефом, каким они являются. Было ли круглое сооружение перекрыто, неизвестно, и модель оставляет этот вопрос открытым.

items.text: The Temple of Artemis at Ephesus. 4th century BC - AD 401. One of the Seven Wonders, and the only one with not a single column left standing: a marble forest 137 metres long, raised on marshy ground. Pliny says 36 of the columns were carved in relief at the base. The model shows the third temple, rebuilt in the 4th century BC.

items.text: Finally, what this model does not know. Only foundations and scattered fragments survive, so the plan is disputed: the sources give the dimensions and Pliny's 127 columns, not the grid they stood in. The model is laid out to reach 127, but the spacing, the pitch of the roof and the ornament of the pediment are all inference. The carved column bases are left plain.

items.text: Der Artemistempel von Ephesos. 4. Jahrhundert v. Chr. – 401 n. Chr. Eines der Sieben Weltwunder und das einzige, von dem keine einzige Säule mehr steht: ein 137 Meter langer Wald aus Marmor, errichtet auf sumpfigem Boden. Laut Plinius waren 36 der Säulen am Fuß mit Reliefs verziert. Das Modell zeigt den dritten Tempel, der im 4. Jahrhundert v. Chr. neu errichtet wurde.

items.text: Zum Schluss: was dieses Modell nicht weiß. Erhalten sind nur Fundamente und verstreute Fragmente, daher ist der Grundriss umstritten: Die Quellen nennen die Maße und die 127 Säulen des Plinius, nicht aber das Raster, in dem sie standen. Das Modell ist so angelegt, dass es auf 127 kommt, doch die Abstände, die Dachneigung und der Schmuck des Giebels sind allesamt Schlussfolgerung. Die skulptierten Säulenbasen sind schlicht gelassen.

items.text: Храм Артемиды в Эфесе. IV век до н. э. – 401 г. н. э. Одно из семи чудес света и единственное, от которого не осталось ни одной стоящей колонны: мраморный лес длиной 137 метров, возведённый на болотистой почве. По словам Плиния, 36 колонн были украшены рельефами у основания. Модель показывает третий храм, отстроенный заново в IV веке до н. э.

items.text: И напоследок — чего эта модель не знает. Сохранились лишь фундаменты и разрозненные фрагменты, поэтому план спорен: источники сообщают размеры и 127 колонн Плиния, но не сетку, по которой они стояли. Модель построена так, чтобы получилось 127, но расстояния между колоннами, уклон кровли и убранство фронтона — всё это умозаключение. Резные базы колонн оставлены гладкими.

items.text: Son olarak, bu modelin bilmediği şeyler. Taban ölçüleri, friz ve merdiven genişliği kazılmış parçalardan bilinir; 12 metrelik yükseklik ise Ampelius'un antik notundan gelir ve tartışmalıdır. Üstteki sütun dizisinin oranları, çatının olup olmadığı ve kanatların ayrıntıları modellemedir. Friz bandında Berlin'deki Pergamon Müzesi'nde yeniden kurulmuş Gigantomakhia'nın fotoğrafı dolanır: kabartma gerçek, ama 113 metrelik anlatının hangi sahnesinin yapının hangi yüzünde durduğu modelde doğru değildir.

items.text: The Great Altar of Pergamon. c. 170 - 159 BC. Less an altar than a stage: the 113-metre Gigantomachy frieze wraps the building in a battle told in stone. It was dismantled and shipped to Berlin between 1878 and 1886; what stands at Pergamon now is the terrace and the footings.

items.text: Finally, what this model does not know. The base, the frieze and the width of the stairway are known from excavated blocks; the height of 12 metres comes from Ampelius' ancient note and is disputed. The proportions of the colonnade on top, whether it was roofed, and the detail of the wings are inference. The frieze band carries a photograph of the Gigantomachy as re-erected in the Pergamonmuseum in Berlin: the carving is real, but which scene of that 113-metre narrative sat on which face of the building is not what the model shows.

items.text: Zum Schluss: was dieses Modell nicht weiß. Sockel, Fries und Breite der Treppe sind aus ausgegrabenen Blöcken bekannt; die Höhe von 12 Metern stammt aus einer antiken Notiz des Ampelius und ist umstritten. Die Proportionen der Säulenhalle oben, ob sie überdacht war, und die Einzelheiten der Flügel sind Schlussfolgerung. Das Friesband trägt eine Fotografie der Gigantomachie, wie sie im Pergamonmuseum in Berlin wiederaufgebaut ist: Die Skulptur ist echt, aber welche Szene dieser 113 Meter langen Erzählung an welcher Seite des Baus saß, zeigt das Modell nicht.
